pages.d: A web UI for AI agents in Python. Streaming chat, an artifacts canvas, selectable layouts, a dashboard and docs sites, from one pip package.

s.x: Python 3.10 or higher. Open . The app opens in the React app shell, in its chat layout. Connect a model with aiui.stream_token() in the quick start, or open the canvas with AIUI_LAYOUT=chat-canvas aiui run app.py.

Stream replies, tool calls and approvals from the agent you already have. The app shell, the chat, the dashboard and the other styles, side by side. Five frames for the same app, and the canvas the agent's work opens in. Add pages, settings and themes from a Python package. A folder of Markdown becomes a site like this one. Behind a proxy, with auth on every route and WebSocket. Looking something up? The CLI, the Python API and the YAML configuration cover every command, function and key. PraisonAIUI is MIT licensed. Install it from PyPI as aiui; the import name is praisonaiui and the command is aiui.

s.x: PraisonAIUI is one Python package. The PyPI name is aiui, you import it as praisonaiui, and the command is aiui. The browser UI ships inside the wheel, so you do not need Node.js or npm to run an app or build a docs site.
Python 3.10 or higher. The browser UI ships inside the wheel. You need Node.js only to change the React frontend in a clone of the repository (version in src/frontend/.nvmrc).
pip uv pipx Check the install: A version number means the aiui command is on your path. Next: the quick start. The wheel installs two commands that do the same thing: aiui and praisonaiui.

The base install runs the server, the chat UI and aiui build. Extras add integrations. Install one with pip install "aiui[ ]". Extra Adds praisonai PraisonAI Agents, the PraisonAI wrapper, gateway and bot dependencies, for --backend praisonai. A YAML chat app (aiui run chat.yaml) needs only pip install praisonaiagents memory ChromaDB and LiteLLM for agent memory knowledge mem0, ChromaDB, MarkItDown and Chonkie for the knowledge base graph mem0 graph memory sql SQLAlchemy (async) and aiosqlite for SQLAlchemyDataStore postgres sql plus asyncpg bot Telegram, Discord and Slack bot libraries slack, discord, teams One channel's SDK only mcp The MCP client SDK a2ui PraisonAI Agents with A2UI support (agent canvas) langchain, llama-index, semantic-kernel Framework integrations all Every extra above dev pytest, ruff, mypy and the test dependencies (for contributors) The list is [project.optional-dependencies] in pyproject.toml.

Nothing in this repository is published to npm for the current UI: src/frontend/package.json is private and its build is committed into the Python package. Plugins for the React app shell import @aiui/sdk, which the shell provides at runtime; see UI plugins. The older praisonaiui package on npm (0.1.0) is a separate docs-site runtime, described under TypeScript SDK; aiui run and aiui build do not use it.
To work on PraisonAIUI itself: See Testing for the test commands.

pages.d: Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.

s.x: Ship your AIUI docs site to GitHub Pages with one workflow file.
Create aiui.yaml:
Create .github/workflows/deploy.yml:
Go to Settings → Pages in your GitHub repo Set Source to Deploy from a branch Set Branch to gh-pages / / (root) Push to main — your site deploys automatically

A repository other than .github.io is published at https:// .github.io/ /, under a path prefix. --base-path auto in the workflow above handles it: in GitHub Actions it reads the repository name, so every asset, page, link, search and Markdown URL starts with /, and the sitemap, llms.txt and canonical links use https:// .github.io/ as the site URL. Nothing else to configure, and no custom domain needed. auto builds for the root when the repository has a CNAME file, when the repository is .github.io, when seo.siteUrl is set (its path is the prefix), and outside GitHub Actions. To set the prefix yourself: The same works for any host that serves the site under a path, such as example.com/docs behind a reverse proxy (--base-path /docs). Write links in your Markdown as usual (/docs/guide, ../img/x.png): the build and the app add the prefix. Order of precedence: --base-path, then site.basePath, then the path of seo.siteUrl. --base-path / builds for the root. If you deploy with actions/configure-pages (Pages source "GitHub Actions"), you can pass its output instead, which also knows a custom domain set in the repository settings: --base-path "${{ steps.pages.outputs.base_path }}". Preview a prefixed build locally: aiui serve --base-path /my-repo serves it at http://127.0.0.1:8000/my-repo/ (and aiui serve --no-build serves an existing build under the prefix it was built for). Under a prefix, the legacy plugins that read the URL themselves (content-loader, homepage, topnav) are not supported; the default nav-intercept and fetch-retry are.

To use a custom domain (e.g., docs.example.com): Create a CNAME file in your repo root: Configure DNS — add a CNAME record pointing to .github.io The workflow above copies CNAME into the build output. The build also uses it as the site URL for the sitemap and canonical links.

MkDocs AIUI mkdocs.yml aiui.yaml mkdocs build → ./site/ aiui build --output site → ./site/ mkdocs serve aiui dev pip install mkdocs-material pip install aiui What carries over from Material for MkDocs pages: Admonitions (!!! note "Title", collapsible ???), content tabs (=== "Tab" with 4-space indented content) and fenced code blocks render. attr_list ({ .class }) is not supported and shows as literal text; :material-*: icon shortcodes do not render as icons; raw HTML blocks are not styled. Remove them. The nav: list in mkdocs.yml is not read. Pages are ordered by the frontmatter order value, then a number prefix in the file name (01-intro.md), then the file name. See Navigation.

Create aiui.yaml (see the example above) and run aiui validate --strict. Replace mkdocs build with aiui build --output site --minify in your CI workflow. Check the pages for the unsupported syntax listed above. Push to main.
See Hot Reload.

aiui build --output site produces: With a site URL (seo.siteUrl, or the CNAME file) the build also writes sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt; see SEO. Everything is static, so GitHub Pages serves it directly.

Opening a page from the sidebar fetches its .md file. A reader on a lossy network (Wi-Fi, VPN, a mobile link) sometimes gets one new connection that hangs for 15 to 30 seconds while every other request is fast. The docs app keeps one such request from freezing the page: Time limit and retry. Each request for a page has 5 seconds to get an answer from the server. Past that it is cancelled and a fresh request goes out, which opens a new connection. There are three attempts (5 s, 5 s, then 10 s for a link that is only slow), with a short random pause between them. A network error or a 5xx answer is retried the same way; a 404 is not. Stalled downloads. Once the answer starts, a page whose download sends nothing for 5 seconds has stalled and is requested again; one that keeps arriving, however slowly, gets up to 15 seconds. Prefetch. Resting the pointer on a sidebar, previous / next or in-article docs link for 80 ms, focusing it with the keyboard, or pressing it starts loading that page. Once a page has shown, its previous and next pages load while the browser is idle. In-memory cache. A page loaded or prefetched once shows at once when you come back to it, without a request, until the tab is reloaded. The last click wins. Clicking another link cancels the request for the page you left, so fast clicking never builds a queue. No long wait for the renderer. A fetched page waits at most one second for the code highlighter and math renderer; after that the text shows and upgrades when they arrive. Retry state. When every attempt fails, the page says "Couldn't load this page" with a Retry button instead of a loading skeleton. First load. Every page aiui build writes carries the navigation (docs-nav.json), the route manifest and the page's own Markdown, so a first visit asks for none of them; ui-config.json is preloaded with the page (a live aiui serve adds Ask AI, MCP and feedback to it, so it is not baked in). The loader's tag names the plugins, so plugins/plugins.json is not requested either: on this site a first docs page went from five JSON requests and three plugin scripts to one and two. A file the page does not carry (a navigation over 100 KB, the navigation of a site with sign-in, a page served without its content) loads with the same time limit and retries as a page. If it cannot load, the page says "Couldn't load the docs" with a Retry button instead of staying blank. This site, https://ui.praison.ai, is built the same way: see .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml.

The docs app renders code (Shiki), mermaid diagrams, MkDocs tabs and admonitions, "On this page" and the header tabs itself. By default a build loads only one of the vanilla plugins in plugins/: Plugin Why it loads nav-intercept Keeps in-article /docs links on in-app navigation (no full page load) fetch-retry (retry a failed request for the site manifests) is no longer in the default list: the app reads the navigation and route manifest from the page and fetches ui-config.json with its own time limit and retries, which fetch-retry leaves alone. List it under site.plugins to keep it. mermaid, syntax-highlight, code-copy, toc, mkdocs-compat, content-loader, homepage and topnav no longer load by default: they skip React docs pages, and mermaid and syntax-highlight fetched about 40 files from cdn.jsdelivr.net and cdnjs.cloudflare.com on every page (each new origin is another connection that can stall). A site can still list any of them under site.plugins in aiui.yaml. index.html loads plugins/plugin-loader.js?v=, where the version is a hash of the plugin files in the build (also in plugins/plugins.json), and names the plugins on the same tag (data-plugins), so the loader does not fetch plugins.json (a server's pages, which lack it, still do). The loader imports every plugin with the same ?v=, so browsers and the CDN cache them until a build changes a plugin.

Style What it renders chat React chat interface: sessions, streaming, starters, profiles agents React multi-agent view with a tabbed agent/session sidebar playground React side-by-side input and output panels for prompt testing dashboard Vanilla-JS admin dashboard with built-in and custom pages docs React documentation site (sidebar, table of contents, search) custom React site built from your YAML templates and components, with an optional floating chat widget app The React app shell with selectable layouts (the aiui run default) app is what aiui run opens when nothing else picks a style; it starts in the chat layout (no canvas) unless the app, its YAML or AIUI_LAYOUT picks another. See React app shell for what it contains and Layouts for its layouts.

After loading app.py, the CLI looks at the callbacks and agents it registered (server.detect_style): Your code registers Detected style @aiui.profiles and at least one aiui.register_agent() agents one or more @aiui.page(...) callbacks dashboard anything else, such as @aiui.reply only app (the React app shell, chat layout)
--style has no default value, so any style you name, chat included, wins over aiui.set_style() and detection.
A YAML chat app (aiui run chat.yaml) reads style: and applies it through aiui.set_style():
AIUI_SHELL=app turns the dashboard style into app; AIUI_SHELL=legacy turns app back into dashboard (the kill switch). It has no effect on the other styles.
style: in a YAML chat app CLI --style aiui.set_style() in Python Auto-detection (agents or dashboard) Default: app

layout.mode in a YAML site config places the React chat on the page instead of filling it: layout.mode Description fullscreen Full-page chat (default) sidebar Fixed right-side panel bottom-right Floating widget, bottom-right corner bottom-left Floating widget, bottom-left corner top-right Floating widget, top-right corner top-left Floating widget, top-left corner In the docs and custom styles, chat.enabled: true with one of the four corner modes adds the floating chat widget on top of the site. In the dashboard style the equivalent is aiui.set_chat_mode("fullpage" | "floating" | "sidebar").

pages.d: The app shell is a React interface for the PraisonAIUI dashboard: a sidebar,

s.x: The app shell is a React interface for the PraisonAIUI dashboard: a sidebar, a header with a command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K), a React chat and a host that runs every existing dashboard page inside it. It is opt-in in this release. The default style is still dashboard (the vanilla-JS dashboard), and it renders exactly as it did in v0.3.153.

Any one of these: Where How YAML config style: app Python aiui.set_style("app") before the server starts CLI aiui run app.py --style app Environment AIUI_SHELL=app aiui run app.py (alias: AIUI_SHELL=react) AIUI_SHELL=app only changes the dashboard style (explicit or default) into app. Other styles (chat, docs, agents, playground, custom) are never rewritten.
AIUI_SHELL=legacy turns app back into dashboard, whatever the config says. It is the documented way back once the default flips (see flip criteria).

Every page you have today. A page is resolved in this order: a React page registered through the SDK (built-in ports such as chat, or a UI plugin page); a server-driven page (register_page with a handler, @aiui.page), rendered from its _components tree as blocks; otherwise the original dashboard view, mounted inside the shell. Nothing disappears: dashboard plugins (kanban, sample-board, video-studio), set_custom_js and custom.js registerView pages keep working as hosted pages. React chat over the WebSocket /api/chat/ws (streaming, tool calls, reasoning, inline approvals and questions, attachments, Stop, history). When the socket cannot open it falls back to Server-Sent Events (POST /run); on SSE an agent's question says that answering needs a live connection. One markdown renderer (Streamdown) for chat and docs, with lazy code highlighting (74 languages), Mermaid and KaTeX. In chat, external links open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow", and remote images are shown as a click-to-load placeholder naming their host (same-origin, data:image/ and blob: images load directly). Approval toasts. A new approval anywhere raises a toast with a "Review" button that opens the Approvals page. On the chat page the approval is shown in the thread instead.

Existing API dashboard (default) app (opt-in) register_page with a handler / @aiui.page unchanged server-driven blocks page register_page without a handler unchanged hosted custom.js registerView page register_page_action unchanged the page's action endpoint set_pages, pages.enabled/disabled unchanged applied set_custom_js unchanged injected; runs when the hosted runtime loads set_custom_css unchanged unchanged; HSL triples warn (see below) set_theme, set_brand_color, register_theme unchanged converted to theme seeds dashboard plugins unchanged hosted pages; dashboard.plugins allowlist honoured chat, docs, agents, playground, custom styles same app, now lazy-loaded with the new markdown renderer and tokens n/a aiui build static docs same app; index.js/index.css get a ?v= content hash n/a

Colours now come from a small set of seeds (--seed-accent, --seed-ink, --seed-paper, …). Everything else (--background, --primary, sidebar and chart colours) is derived from them in CSS with color-mix(), separately for light and dark. Python emits seeds only (praisonaiui.themes.get_seed_theme_css(preset, radius, accent, density)): neutral presets (zinc, slate, stone, gray, neutral) are monochrome: the accent follows the ink; colour presets (rose, blue, …) seed the accent from the 600 shade in light mode, and the button text colour is picked automatically for at least 4.5:1 contrast; radius presets are unchanged. get_theme_css() is kept for API compatibility but the compiler no longer uses it. Runtime themes (register_theme, named presets) are converted to seeds in the browser.

Listed in the changelog for the release that ships the app shell. shadcn variables used to hold bare HSL triples that the stylesheet wrapped in hsl(). They are now complete colours: aiui validate warns (code 5001) when site.custom_css sets one of these variables to a bare triple. Custom CSS and runtime themes that still use triples are converted in the browser where possible, but update the CSS.

Code chunks are content-hashed (assets/ - .js) and served with Cache-Control: immutable. assets/index.js and assets/index.css keep fixed names and are referenced as ?v=, so a release never mixes an old entry with new chunks. aiui build writes index.html (and every route page) with /assets/index.js?v= and the same for index.css, and copies aiui-manifest.json next to it. The docs deploy keeps the previous build's chunks, and with its ledger (aiui-carried.json) older builds' chunks for --keep-days (default 2) (src/frontend/scripts/carry-forward-assets.mjs), so a reader with an old page open can still load its lazy parts. A stale chunk that does fail to load triggers one automatic reload, and only when the server's HTML (fetched past the cache) names another build. The reload opens the page as ?aiui-build=, a URL no browser or CDN cache holds, and the boot removes the parameter again. When the boot chunks themselves cannot load, the page says so and offers Reload. A docs page never waits for good: each markdown request has a time limit for its headers and one for its body, a stalled request is sent again, and a page that still cannot load shows "Couldn't load this page" with Retry (src/frontend/src/docs/docLoader.ts). Static files are sent gzip-compressed. Each file is compressed once per version (path, mtime, size) in a worker thread and kept in memory (at most 64 MB), so a cold page load does not compress the bundle again on the event loop. Range requests get the plain bytes. The page HTML, /api/shell/manifest, /api/pages and dashboard-plugin files are compressed too. aiui run app.py serves the bundle from the installed package; it no longer copies it into ./aiui on every start (a ./aiui left by an older version is ignored for a chat app; delete it). A site built with aiui run --config is served gzip-compressed with Cache-Control: no-cache, likeaiui serve, and its ownassets/ (for example theme.css) is looked up after the package's. aiui serve answers a page's canonical URL (/docs/x) from docs/x.html directly, without a redirect to /docs/x/.

pages.d: A layout is the frame of the React app shell (style: app): the navigation,

s.x: A layout is the frame of the React app shell (style: app): the navigation, the session list, the top bar, side panels and the phone chrome. The page stays the page. Every page (chat, logs, config, a plugin page, a blocks page) renders inside every layout, in the outlet the shell hands the frame. The design is ADR 0003. Layouts exist only in the app shell. The default dashboard style is not affected and renders exactly as before.

Id Title What it is for Opens on Primary nav chat-canvas (default) Chat and Canvas Chat beside a canvas of the artifacts the agent makes chat chat, artifacts, agents, cron, knowledge, sessions, config chat Chat The Chat and Canvas frame without the canvas or artifact cards (same Paper look); what aiui run opens chat chat, agents, cron, knowledge, sessions, config workbench Quiet Workbench A quiet sidebar with your chats, and the page beside it chat chat, agents, knowledge, runs, config command Command Deck Keyboard first: a command bar, session tabs and a run inspector chat chat, runs, agents, jobs, config guided Guided Studio Plain language and large buttons; every step explained start start, chat, agents, templates mission Mission Control Agents, runs and approvals at a glance overview overview, agents, approvals, chat, runs, sessions classic is not a layout. It is the core's own frame (the sidebar and header the app shell had before layouts): always available, and the fallback. A primary nav may name a page that is not there (a disabled record's page, for example); the shell keeps only the ids the manifest carries. Each built-in frame is its own design, built on the shared layout kit (src/frontend/src/app-layouts/kit/: nav and session lists, page icons, the connection line, phone sheet and tabs). Its page above has the regions, keys, phone frame and the data it reads. The features only one layout uses are lazy chunks of their own: the run inspector and command bar (Command Deck), the step tracker (Guided Studio) and the mission board (Mission Control). The Chat and Canvas frame shows the canvas of artifacts once the artifacts feature (layout-features/artifacts, ADR track A) is in the build; without it the canvas stays empty. Each built-in layout is its own lazy chunk (layout-), with the kit in layout-kit. The browser downloads only the chunks of the layout on screen; an inactive layout costs nothing.

Layouts apply to style: app only. A layout chosen under another style is ignored, and the server logs one warning: layout ignored: style is 'dashboard'; use style: app. Choosing a layout never changes the style.

layout: is the existing LayoutConfig. Its chat position keys (mode, width, height) keep working. The layout keys are added next to them: A layout id is lower-case letters, digits and -, starts with a letter and has at most 40 characters. classic is reserved: it is a valid default, never an available entry. layout: classic keeps an app that already used style: app on the frame it had before. A malformed entry never fails the config. The server ignores it with a warning, and aiui validate reports it as 5103 (for example layout: Bad_Id, or available: command where a list goes). The rest of the section still applies.
set_layout(default=None, *, available=None, user_choice=None, primary=None, options=None) raises ValueError for a malformed id. Call it before the server starts.
AIUI_LAYOUT= or AIUI_LAYOUT=classic sets the default for one run. A malformed value is ignored with a warning.

On the server, the default is the first of these that is set: AIUI_LAYOUT aiui.set_layout() YAML layout: the aiui run default: chat (only under aiui run; create_app() and PraisonAI keep the style default) the style default: chat-canvas for style: app The shell manifest's layouts key carries the layouts the server offers (available), its default and whether the viewer may choose (userChoice). A shell that receives no layouts key (an older server) renders the classic frame. In the browser, the shell renders the first of these that the server offers: A ?layout= preview. It is kept for the tab (sessionStorage aiui-layout-preview), so it survives navigation and reload, and it is never saved as the viewer's choice. ?layout=classic previews the classic frame. Use it for screenshots and support links. The viewer's own choice (localStorage aiui-layout), only when the server allows a user choice. The server's default. The classic frame. A layout the server does not offer is never chosen, whatever is stored. The viewer switches with the command palette ("Switch layout: …", group "Layout"; one command per offered layout, named after its manifest title, and Classic; the group is listed after the pages, with Preferences and Theme, until a query ranks it higher) or with Settings → Appearance (a select of the same list, shown only when the server allows a user choice). The choice is saved in this browser and applies at once, without a reload: the frame and the page remount, and chat state is kept. When the server does not allow a choice, the palette commands still switch, for this tab only. Saving the choice per user across devices is (planned) (no server-side preference store yet).

An available id that no enabled plugin declares is dropped, with one warning. A default that is not available falls back to chat-canvas when it is offered, otherwise to the first available layout, with one warning. With nothing available, the shell uses classic. aiui validate warns with code 5101 for an id that is not a built-in layout (a plugin may still provide it; plugin layouts are only known once the server runs), 5102 for a layout chosen while the style is not app, and 5103 for a malformed entry.
Each built-in layout is a first-party record, builtin.layout-: A disabled layout leaves the picker and takes its own pages with it.

A page can belong to a layout. Such a page is shell_only, so it is never in the page table, GET /api/pages or the dashboard. It is in the app shell manifest only while a layout it names is offered. Its manifest row carries layouts (and replaces, the page it stands in for while that layout is active), and its source is the owning record, for example builtin.layout-guided. The shell's nav shows such a page only while one of its layouts is on screen; its URL renders under any layout. Guided owns start (its Home, where / opens while Guided is the layout) and templates. Mission's ops-overview, which replaces overview, arrives with the Mission frame (planned). A layout record adds a page only with the frame that renders it.

Six built-in pages have a React page in the Pro design that renders inside any layout frame (src/frontend/src/app-pages/, one lazy chunk each, registered by builtin.overview, builtin.sessions, builtin.agents, builtin.knowledge, builtin.logs, builtin.config and builtin.cron with the usual registerPage): Page Design What it shows overview ProOverview A greeting and one sentence, "Today at a glance" tiles with sparklines, what needs your approval (the approvals feed plus the open chat's gates), agents, recent runs or chats, the model provider, a collapsible feature health list sessions ProList Search (/), status chips, an agent filter, a sortable table (title, agent, messages, tokens, relative time, status), a detail panel, a labelled row menu, Delete with a confirmation agents ProList Search (/), a model filter, one New agent button, a sortable table (monogram, name, description, model, tools, updated, status), a detail panel (temperature, tools, instructions, system prompt, Training history), Edit and New agent in that panel (name, description, model from /api/agents/models, temperature, instructions, system prompt), Duplicate, Delete with a confirmation, a skeleton while loading and Try again on an error; agents the app registers in code are read-only; on a phone the panel replaces the list knowledge ProList A joined stat strip (entries, files, semantic or keyword search, the store with a status chip in plain words), search (/) with marked snippets and the relevance the store reports, "Add knowledge" for text or files (drop zone, drag and drop onto the page, per-file progress and errors), a table (name, type, size, added), a detail panel (facts, content, Copy, Delete with a confirmation), Clear all; on a phone the detail replaces the list logs ProLogs Level toggles with counts, search with match navigation, Pause, Download, Clear with a confirmation cron ProList Search, status chips, New schedule, a table (schedule in words and as cron, in UTC; next and last run; an enabled switch), a detail panel with recent runs, Run now, Edit and Delete, a builder (every N minutes or hours, daily, weekly, custom cron with the next runs) config ProSettings A section list, a breadcrumb, shadcn Select / Switch / Input with help for each field, a masked API key with a show toggle, Test connection, a sticky "Unsaved changes" bar In the classic frame (layout: classic) these pages render their legacy view exactly as before, and the default dashboard style never loads them. The one layout page shipped today is artifacts (layouts: [chat-canvas]), owned by the data record builtin.artifacts rather than a layout record: the index of every chat's artifacts, where the canvas's Share links land. See Layout data.

s.h: Data that only some layouts need
s.x: A first-party record can declare for_layouts=("command", "mission"). It is mounted only while one of those layouts is offered, or while extensions.enabled names it. Otherwise GET /api/plugins?origin=builtin lists it as disabled with the reason no layout needs it, its routes answer 404 and its feature module is never imported.

A reply handler can offer follow-up prompts for the answer it is writing. They go out on the run's run_completed frame as suggestions (an optional field; clients that do not know it ignore it), and a layout that shows follow-up chips (Guided) renders them: A later call replaces the list and aiui.suggest([]) clears it. Blank entries are dropped, each prompt is cut to 200 characters and at most 8 are kept. Outside a chat run the call does nothing.

A plugin adds a layout with the same SDK call the built-ins use, registerLayout(id, meta, Frame | loader). Its Python side declares it with a layouts() hook, the same way first-party records do: module is required. A relative path resolves into the plugin's static dir (/_plugins/deck/deck.js, with an SRI hash). That module calls registerLayout("deck", …), and the shell imports it only while the layout is active. An id that another plugin (or a built-in) already provides is ignored with a warning, and so is a classic or malformed id. On a remote or auth-enforced server, an entry-point plugin's layouts follow the same default-deny rule as its pages: list the plugin in extensions.enabled. Plugin pages may carry layouts and replaces too. shell_only=True keeps a blocks page out of GET /api/pages. The browser module, the props a frame receives (LayoutProps: Outlet, nav, chrome, viewport, layout) and a complete example are in UI Plugins → Layouts. The fixture src/frontend/e2e/fixtures/layout-plugin/ is a working third-party layout plugin. In short, a frame: renders once, inside a main with id={chrome.mainId}; draws its navigation from nav (primary at most 7 items, groups for the rest, footer) and navigates with nav.go(pageId); uses chrome.openPalette() for search and commands (there is one palette), lists the groups plugins declared (nav.groups entries with declared: true, kept in order and folded as given) even when it keeps other groups in More, and shows a settings entry calling chrome.openSettings() when it is set (only while some plugin contributes a settings section); the kit's DeclaredNavGroups and PluginSettingsRow draw both, and chrome.Slot for the shell's slots (header:actions, …); draws its phone frame when viewport === 'phone' (below 768 px), with touch targets of at least 44 px; reads data such as the session list with useLayoutData('sessions'), and renders without it when that returns null.

A layout whose module fails to import, or whose frame throws while rendering, is replaced by the classic frame. The viewer sees one toast ("The "…" layout failed to load"), and the shell fires one aiui:plugin-error window event whose detail.layout is the layout id. Other layouts and the pages are not affected. While a plugin layout is still loading, the shell shows a frame skeleton; a selected layout that no plugin ever registers falls back to the classic frame with a console warning.

These rules keep layouts independent (ARCHITECTURE.md R17): every layout lives in src/frontend/src/app-layouts/ / and is built as the chunk layout-; shared pieces live in app-layouts/kit/ (layout-kit), never copied; layout-specific features live in src/frontend/src/layout-features/ / (lf-) (planned: none exist yet); a layout never imports another layout or the shell, and loads a feature only with import(); the core (shell/, sdk/, legacy/, blocks/) names no layout id and imports neither folder (shell/core-purity.test.ts); the boot path loads no layout chunk, and a layout's closure contains no other layout, no feature, and no Streamdown, Shiki, Mermaid, KaTeX or @assistant-ui (scripts/check-layout-isolation.mjs, part of npm run check:closure); in the browser, e2e/specs/layouts-host.spec.ts checks that each layout downloads only its own chunks and the kit. Looks on first paint. The server writes data-aiui-tokens="pro" on the app shell's when there is a default layout, and also the layout's look (data-aiui-look="paper" for Chat and Canvas and Chat, from the catalog record's look). The page then paints Paper and fetches only the Paper fonts, never Geist first. An inline script drops the look before first paint for a viewer who will not see it: one who chose plain Pro ("Switch look: Pro"), or one whose ?layout=, tab preview or stored pick (with user_choice) is another layout. The layout host clears it for a frame without a look (the classic frame drops the Pro tokens, and the look's CSS applies only with them). Each layout, the kit and the /chat first screen with the default layout have gzip budgets in src/frontend/.size-limit.mjs (listed in ARCHITECTURE.md R10). npm run size fails when a budgeted layout or the kit is missing from the build.

GET /api/shell/manifest has a top-level layouts key (ShellLayouts in src/frontend/src/sdk/manifest.ts): Outside style: app it is {"default": "", "userChoice": true, "available": []}, which the shell reads as classic.

pages.d: chat-canvas is the default layout of the React app shell (style: app).

s.x: chat-canvas is the default layout of the React app shell (style: app). The chat is on the left; the tables, code and files the agent makes sit on a canvas beside it, where you can sort, copy, download and compare versions. See Layouts for how layouts are chosen, and ADR 0003 for the design. The Chat and Canvas layout in dark mode, in its Paper look: the conversation on the left with a pending approval, and on the right the canvas split between the comparison table and the sort_demo.py script the agent wrote

Desktop and tablet Region What it holds Sidebar (240 px) The site name and a collapse button (⌘B / Ctrl+B); New chat (⌘N / Ctrl+N); the primary pages (chat, artifacts, agents, cron, knowledge, sessions, config; the Artifacts row shows how many artifacts exist across chats); Chats, your conversations as two-line rows (the title over "3 artifacts · now"), with a search button, the open one raised, a running one marked "Working…"; at the foot Settings (the config page), More (⌘K), which opens the command palette with every other page (the footer pages such as Inspector among them) and command, and the connection line ("Connected · local" when the server is this machine). Top bar On the chat page: the open chat's title over "Researcher · 3 artifacts · edited 2 min ago" (the agent of the latest answer, the chat's artifacts, their latest change; "reconnecting" joins it while the chat's connection is down). On other pages: the page title. Then Search or run a command (⌘K), on the chat page the Canvas toggle (pressed while the canvas is open, with the artifact count), Share (copies the link; a chat's link opens that chat) and the light/dark switch. The page Any page renders here. The chat page uses speech-bubble messages under a header with the agent's letter tile, name and time; each tool call is one compact row (the call in mono, "→" and the first line of its output, its state, how long it took); "Thought for 2s" is a quiet disclosure; explained approval cards (the tool and its risk with Details, "Researcher wants to run a command" and why, the exact $ command, then Approve, Deny, "Why am I asked?" and "Paused until you choose"); the composer has the message on two rows ("Ask a follow-up, or type @ to edit an artifact") above attach, @, the model and a round Send in the accent (lighter, and aria-disabled, while there is nothing to send); @ (or typing @) lists this chat's artifacts, and a choice puts a plain-text mention such as @"Model table" in the message for the agent to read; and, when the artifacts feature is installed, the Canvas panel on the right. A new chat starts with the canvas collapsed; it opens once the chat has an artifact, and the toggle opens or closes it at any time. The "Chat + Canvas" page (/chat-canvas) is the same React chat in the app shell. Open, the canvas is the main surface: it takes about 58% of the chat page and the chat a narrower column (never under about 400 px); with the canvas closed the chat is a centred column. On a tablet the canvas starts closed. Drag the gap between the chat and the canvas (or focus it and use the arrow keys, Home and End) to resize it; the share is kept in this browser. Hiding the sidebar is kept in this browser too. Phone A header with the menu (the sidebar's contents in a sheet, with 44 px rows), the chat title centred over "Mock · gpt-4o-mini" (the agent and the model the composer shows), and New chat. Approval cards split the width into Deny | Approve (44 px), and the composer keeps the model on its bottom row. On the chat page a Chat | Canvas (n) switch flips between the conversation and the canvas.

The layout paints with its own look, Paper (the design board's palette and type): warm paper neutrals with a navy accent in light and dark, titles, the wordmark (and a serif "P" on the ink brand tile), artifact titles and table row headers in Newsreader, text in Source Sans 3 and code in JetBrains Mono. The fonts ship with aiui (no font CDN) and download only while the look is on. The chat layout (this frame without the canvas) has the same look; every other layout, and the classic frame, keep their own. Prefer the plain Pro look? Open the command palette (⌘K) and run Switch look: Pro; Switch look: Paper brings it back. The choice is saved in this browser. A brand colour (theme.accent, aiui.set_brand_color(...)) and the Pro accent presets replace the navy accent; the paper neutrals stay. Theme authors: the look is with the tokens in src/frontend/src/styles/paper.css; see DESIGN.md "Looks".

The canvas, the artifact cards under each answer and the artifacts index page come from the artifacts feature (layout-features/artifacts, record builtin.artifacts). The layout loads that code only on the chat page, and works without it: with the feature missing from the build, or switched off, the chat page has no canvas and everything else stays. The canvas (Canvas.dc.html): a tab per artifact with its kind icon, then the split toggle, + (open another of this chat's artifacts below the shown one, or All artifacts), expand and close. The shown artifact has its title, kind and time, the version menu ("v2 · edited by Researcher"), Copy, Download and Share; a table sorts by any column header; History (each version, who made it, what changed, Restore) sits on the right, and folds under the viewer on a phone. When the chat has code next to a table or a document, the code docks below it (Run ⌘↵ and its Output strip, "Ran 1 min ago · 0.02s", when the server can run it) until you close the split. Each artifact shows once. While the canvas is there, a code block or table that is an artifact (3+ lines of code, a table with 2+ rows) leaves the reply: the reply shows its card ("Comparison table · Table · 3 rows · v2 · edited by Researcher · In canvas"), and a card opens the artifact in the canvas (on a phone, the Canvas side). Shorter snippets stay in the reply. Choose artifactsInChat: inline to keep the blocks in the reply as well, a long code block cut to its first 12 lines and a long table to its first 6 rows (the rest scrolls inside the block): The chat layout has no canvas and keeps every block in the reply.

extensions.disabled: [builtin.artifacts]: no canvas, no Artifacts page; the rest of the layout is unchanged. extensions.disabled: [builtin.approvals]: no approval toasts; the approval card in the thread still decides the gate. extensions.disabled: [builtin.layout-chat-canvas]: the layout is not offered; the app shell opens on the next offered layout, or the classic frame.

The frame is the chunk layout-chat-canvas. It imports only the SDK, components/ui, lib and the layout kit, and loads the artifacts feature with import(). Styling hooks: [data-aiui-layout-frame="chat-canvas"] on the frame (data-viewport is phone, tablet or desktop), [data-cc-title] and [data-cc-subtitle] in the top bar, [data-aiui-aside-slot] (where the chat's aside toggle is portalled; without it the toggle stays in the chat's own header), [data-cc-chat-meta] on a chat row's second line, [data-aiui-session] on chat rows, [data-aiui-nav-item] on nav rows. The shell's header:actions slot is at the end of the top bar and sidebar:footer at the foot of the sidebar. [data-in-canvas] marks a reply block that is shown as its card (data-cc-artifacts="card" on the frame hides it); the window event aiui:chat-aside ({open: true} / {open: false}) opens or closes the chat's aside, as an artifact card does. The artifacts feature plugs in through files the layout looks for: layout-features/artifacts/CanvasPanel.tsx (the canvas, a chat region), ArtifactCards.tsx (the cards under an answer, a turn region) and feed.ts (the artifacts data feed, exported as artifactsFeed or as the default export).

pages.d: A calm sidebar with your chats, a focused top bar and the page beside it. It

s.x: A calm sidebar with your chats, a focused top bar and the page beside it. It suits people who live in one conversation at a time and want nothing else on screen. It is one of the layouts of the React app shell (style: app); the default dashboard style is not affected. The Quiet Workbench layout: the chats in a quiet sidebar and the conversation beside it To try it without changing the server, open any page with ?layout=workbench (a preview for this browser tab), or pick Switch layout: Quiet Workbench in the command palette (⌘K). AIUI_LAYOUT=workbench sets it for the whole server.

s.h: Desktop and tablet (768 px and wider)
s.x: Sidebar (256 px) the site's logo and title, and a button that collapses the sidebar (⌘B; the choice is kept in this browser); New chat (⌘N); the layout's primary pages, each with its icon; the current one is highlighted. By default these are chat, agents, knowledge, runs and config; layout.primary in YAML replaces the list (at most 7 are shown, and only pages the server has); Search and more (⌘K), the one command palette; every other page through Search and more ⌘K (the palette), so nothing is out of reach and no bare "More (n)" row sits in the sidebar; Chats: a search box and your chats, newest first, each with when it was last active (Now, 2h, Yesterday, Mon, Jan 5). A chat with a reply in progress says Running; one with an approval waiting says Waiting; footer pages (if any), the connection line and the light or dark switch. Top bar (56 px) the title: the open chat's title on the chat page (New chat before the first message), otherwise the page's title; on the chat page, the agent that answers and, when the agent has a definition with a model, the model (Researcher · gpt-4o-mini); the header:actions slot, so plugins can add buttons here; Share, which copies a link to the page, and More, which opens the palette.

a header with the menu button, the title with the agent and model under it, and a new chat button (all at least 44 px); the menu opens the sidebar as a sheet with the same contents, with 44 px rows and 15 px text. Opening a page or a chat closes it.

The layout asks the chat page to present itself quietly: Setting Value Effect sessions frame the chat page draws no session list of its own; the sidebar's Chats is the list thread quiet your question sits in a full-width quiet box; the answer is plain prose; reasoning and tool steps are single ghost rows you can open approvals inline an approval request appears in the answer with Approve and Deny The top bar names the open chat, so the chat page's own title is kept for screen readers only, and its title row steps aside while the connection is open. If the server offers agents to choose from, or the connection drops, that row comes back with the agent picker or the connection badge.

The frame reads its data from the layout feeds (see Layout data) and hides the part whose feed is off; it never fails: with the chat page (builtin.chat) disabled there is no New chat button and no chat list, and the title is the page's; with approvals (builtin.approvals) disabled no chat is marked Waiting; with no agent definitions (/api/agents/definitions answering 404 or without a model), the top bar shows the agent without a model.

Keys Does ⌘N / Ctrl+N New chat (also while typing). Some browsers keep this shortcut for a new window; the button always works ⌘B / Ctrl+B Collapse or expand the sidebar (desktop) ⌘K / Ctrl+K Search pages and commands

Frame: src/frontend/src/app-layouts/workbench/ (Frame.tsx, the view model in model.ts, workbench.css), built as the lazy chunk layout-workbench. It imports only the SDK, components/ui, lib and the layout kit (app-layouts/kit); see R17 in ARCHITECTURE.md. Descriptor: src/frontend/src/builtin/layouts/workbench.ts (title and the chat presentation above). The Python record is builtin.layout-workbench (home: chat, the primary list); extensions.disabled: [builtin.layout-workbench] removes the layout from the picker. Tests: app-layouts/workbench/workbench.test.tsx (view model, shortcuts, the frame on a desktop and a phone, with feeds off) and e2e/specs/layout-workbench.spec.ts (the scripted conversation on a desktop and a phone in light and dark, an inline approval, a page in the outlet, 44 px targets, network isolation and the leak probe). Design: Main.dc.html and QuietPhone.dc.html, drawn in the PraisonAI Pro tokens (src/frontend/DESIGN.md).

pages.d: The Command Deck (command) is the keyboard-first layout of the app shell

s.x: The Command Deck (command) is the keyboard-first layout of the app shell (style: app). It has a command bar on top, an icon rail, session tabs, a run inspector beside the chat and a status bar. Every page still renders in its outlet. For layouts in general, see Layouts. Other ways to choose it: aiui.set_layout("command"), AIUI_LAYOUT=command, ?layout=command (a preview for this browser tab), Settings → Appearance, or the palette command "Switch layout: Command Deck".

Region What it does Command bar "Ask or run a command". Enter sends the text in the open chat (a new chat when none is open) and opens the chat page; a chat feed without send puts it in the composer instead. Typing / or > first opens the command palette with the rest typed in. ⌘K in the bar opens the palette with the bar's text. / anywhere outside a text field focuses the bar. The @Agent chip names the agent of the open chat. Approvals button "n approvals waiting", while any are pending. It opens the session the approval waits in, with the run panel. The layout shows approvals itself, so no approval toasts appear. Icon rail The layout's primary pages (at most seven; YAML layout.primary overrides them), each with a G-prefix key shown in its tooltip. "More" opens the palette for every other page. ⌘/ lists all shortcuts. The Runs item shows a count of active runs. Session tabs (chat page) The newest nine sessions, with the open one always included. An amber dot means the session waits for an approval; a blue dot means it is running. + starts a new chat. The right end shows the session id and the Run panel toggle. Run inspector (chat page) The open chat's latest run: status, run id and Stop; the pending approval with Approve, Deny and "Always allow"; elapsed time, tokens, cost and steps; the Steps timeline with a bar for each step; the files the run's tools touched. On a desktop it starts open, on a tablet closed. Status bar Online or offline and the host; the agent; active runs and pending approvals; today's tokens and cost; the ⌘K and ⌘/ hints. The chat page in this layout draws no session list of its own (the tabs are the list). It uses the dense thread (the question as a › prompt line, a monospace meta line with the run id, monospace tool rows) and the keyboard approval strip ("Paused: … wants to run …", A and D).

mod is ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. Single keys never fire while you type in a field. Keys Action mod K Commands and pages (the palette) / Focus the command bar mod N New chat mod 1–9 Switch to that session tab mod I Show or hide the run panel mod / All shortcuts G, then a letter Go to a rail page: G C Chat, G R Runs, G A Agents, G J Jobs, G S Config. Other pages take a free letter of their title. J / K Next or previous step in the run panel Enter Expand the focused step (its reasoning or tool result) A / D Approve or deny the pending approval F Jump to the files touched Ctrl C Stop the run (only when no text is selected) The palette also lists "Show or hide the run panel", "Keyboard shortcuts", "Stop the run" while a run is going, and "Approve: …" and "Deny: …" for the open chat's pending approval. Browsers keep some of these combinations for themselves. For example, Chrome uses ⌘N and ⌘1–9 itself. Where the browser takes a key first, use the buttons or the palette instead.

Below 768 px the deck becomes a phone frame (CommandPhone): The top row holds the menu, the command bar and New chat. The menu opens a sheet with any approvals waiting (each with Deny and Approve), the rail pages, the other pages, the sessions and the theme switch. An amber dot on the menu button means approvals are waiting. On the chat page, a switcher row shows the open session and an n/m counter. Tapping it opens the same sheet. The run inspector becomes a peek at the bottom: the run status, steps and cost, and the pending approval with 44 px Deny and Approve buttons. Tap the peek to expand it into the whole inspector. Every touch target is at least 44 px, and body text is at least 15 px.

s.h: Data and what happens when a part is off
s.x: The frame reads the shell's layout data feeds (useLayoutData): Feed Provider Without it sessions builtin.chat No tabs, no switcher, no session list in the sheet chat builtin.chat The run inspector shows "Run details appear here when chat is on"; Enter in the bar opens the palette instead approvals builtin.approvals Approvals come only from the open chat's gates. "Always allow" is hidden. run ledger builtin.run-ledger (mounted only when command or mission is offered) Tokens and cost read "—"; no usage in the status bar Tokens and cost come from the run ledger (GET /api/runs/{id}). The inspector asks for them again whenever the run changes state, because there is no wire event for usage. Steps and timings come from the chat stream itself. Files touched are read from the tools' arguments: path, file, file_path and similar keys, and shell writes (>, tee, touch, mkdir, cp, mv, rm).

Part Where Chunk Descriptor (eager, tiny) src/frontend/src/builtin/layouts/command.ts boot Frame src/frontend/src/app-layouts/command/ layout-command Command bar src/frontend/src/layout-features/command-bar/ lf-command-bar Run inspector src/frontend/src/layout-features/run-inspector/ lf-run-inspector The frame loads both features with import(). On the chat page the browser downloads layout-command, layout-kit, lf-command-bar and lf-run-inspector; on any other page, everything but lf-run-inspector. No other layout's code is downloaded. The features never import the kit: the frame passes them its typing check and platform. A feature that imported the kit would split the kit into one more chunk for every layout. Budgets (gzip, npm run size, measured plus 10%): layout-command 15.2 kB (its closure minus boot, with the kit pieces it imports; ADR cap 24 kB), lf-run-inspector 9.2 kB (cap 14 kB), lf-command-bar 1.6 kB (cap 6 kB). The frame uses only part of the kit (not BasicFrame or ShortcutHint), so Rollup splits the kit into chunks by which frames use which pieces (seven with all five frames in the build); each frame's closure holds the ones it imports. The kit's budget is 8.3 kB. The tests are app-layouts/command/*.test.ts(x) (the frame model, the render and the data helpers), layout-features/run-inspector/*.test.ts(x) (steps, files, formats, the panel and the peek), layout-features/command-bar/bar.test.tsx, and e2e/specs/layout-command.spec.ts in the browser. That spec runs in the layouts-host Playwright project, against the layouts server, with e2e/specs/layouts-host.spec.ts (whose network-isolation case allows this layout exactly lf-command-bar and lf-run-inspector):

A Files destination. The design's rail has one, but no files page exists. Files touched still appear in the inspector. Per-step tokens. The ledger records tokens per run, not per step, so the answer step shows a word count instead.

pages.d: Guided Studio (guided) is the app shell layout for people new to AI

s.x: Guided Studio (guided) is the app shell layout for people new to AI agents. It uses plain words and large buttons, and explains every step the agent takes. It is one of the selectable layouts of the React app shell (style: app); the default dashboard style is not affected. Or set AIUI_LAYOUT=guided, or preview it in one tab with ?layout=guided.

Desktop. A 280 px sidebar holds: the app name; a large Start a new chat button (⌘N / Ctrl+N); five destinations: Home, Chat, My agents, Templates and Help; Your recent chats, the newest five as cards ("Today, 2:14 pm · with Researcher"), with See all when the server has a sessions page; every other page, folded under More tools; Settings and a light/dark switch at the bottom. The header names the open chat and who it is with: "Chatting with Researcher · ready to help", or "working on it" and "waiting for your OK" while a reply runs or waits. Search ⌘K opens the command palette. Change agent opens the chat's agent picker, or My agents when the chat offers no choice of agent. Phone (narrower than 768 px). A 60 px header holds a menu button (your chats, the other pages, Settings), the chat's title and a Start a new chat button. Four bottom tabs follow the page: Home, Chat, My agents and Help. Every target is at least 44 px and the text at least 15 px. The layout paints with the PraisonAI Pro tokens. The pickable Pro accents (Settings → Appearance, or the theme presets) recolour it.

Guided changes how the chat page presents itself, not what it does. Part What you see Step tracker Above each answer: "Here is what Researcher did", numbered steps in plain words, a short result for each step, and "All done in 3 seconds". Show details lists the raw calls: the tool, what it ran, what came back, and how long it took. Approvals The explained approval card, inside the answer right under its text and before the message actions (desktop and phone): the tool and its risk with Details for the arguments, what the agent wants to do, what it will run (a $ command line for a shell command), then Approve / Deny and Why am I asked?. The card is the tool's row, so the request is shown once; the step tracker shows the step as "Waiting for your OK". Follow-up chips Under the latest finished answer, "You could ask next" offers the run's suggestions. A chip puts its text in the message box, ready to send. Empty chat "Pick a template to get started" and four templates. Thread Larger type, a labelled "You" bubble, and an avatar on each answer.

Each step gets a plain label. The first rule that matches wins: The server's own label for the step (the tool event's label). The tool's name: Tool name contains Label shell, exec, terminal, bash, command Running a command search, lookup (documents, memory, knowledge: "Searching your documents") Searching the web fetch, browse, visit, url, or a url argument Visiting python.org write, save, edit with file Saving report.csv read, open, load with file Reading report.csv anything else Using Get weather Thinking is "Understanding your question" ("thought for 2s"). The answer is "Writing the answer". An approval the agent waits on is "Waiting for your OK". A step's short result is the first line of what it returned, cut at 40 characters. Machine output (JSON) is said as a count, such as "2 hits", or left out; Show details still has the raw result.
Chips appear only when the server sends suggestions with the finished run (run_completed.suggestions). From Python: With no suggestions, no chips are shown.

Templates are the app's chat starters (GET /starters). Besides label and message, a starter may carry three optional fields: category, description and icon (an emoji). The Templates page groups starters by category, and each card shows its description and icon. A starter without a category is listed under "More ideas". With no starters configured, Guided offers a short plain-language set: summarise, draft an email, explain, compare, plan, brainstorm, write code, and look at numbers. Using a template opens a new chat with the prompt in the message box. You can change the words before you send. Nothing is sent for you.

Page Id What it shows Home start A welcome, Start a new chat, popular templates, your recent chats, and how a chat works here Templates templates Every template by category, with a search box and category filters Both are shell-only pages of builtin.layout-guided. They are never in the dashboard or /api/pages. The nav lists them only while Guided is on, but their URLs open under any layout. / opens on Home while Guided is the layout; layout.defaultPage still wins.

Key Effect layout.options.guided.helpUrl Where Help goes: an http(s) address (opens in a new tab) or a site path. Without it, Help opens the command palette. layout.primary Replaces the primary destinations (Home, Chat, My agents, Templates), at most 7.

extensions: {disabled: [builtin.layout-guided]} removes the layout from the picker and its two pages from the manifest. With other records off, Guided degrades instead of failing: with builtin.chat off, there is no chat list and no Start a new chat; with builtin.approvals off, there are no approval toasts on other pages (the chat still shows its own approval card).

Guided downloads only what is on screen: Chunk When it loads layout-guided The frame, when Guided is the layout. Its chat regions and pages are their own chunks in the same group, fetched when shown. layout-kit Shared layout pieces, with the frame. lf-step-tracker With the first answer on screen. No other layout's code is fetched. The isolation gate (npm run check:closure) and e2e/specs/layout-guided.spec.ts check this.

s.x: Mission Control (mission) is the operations view of the app shell: every agent's status, today's runs and cost, and what waits on you, before anything else. It is one of the built-in selectable layouts (ADR 0003, record builtin.layout-mission). A viewer can also pick it from the palette ("Switch layout: Mission Control") or Settings → Appearance, and ?layout=mission previews it for one tab.

Where Desktop (1024 px and up) Phone (under 768 px) Top Site title, the environment badge, search (opens the command palette), provider health, the approvals bell with its count, theme Site title with health and environment, search, the approvals bell (44 px buttons) Navigation A 216 px column: the layout's primary pages with counts (agents, runs today, waiting approvals as a warning badge), the other pages folded under 11px uppercase group headers, "More pages ⌘K"; the top bar's pill is the one status indicator ("Connected") Bottom tabs: the first four primary pages (Overview, Agents, Approvals with its badge, Chat) and More, which opens a sheet with the rest of the nav and the recent chats Home (/overview) The ops overview: approval request cards, today's KPI strip, the agents (waiting first), recent runs Approval cards first, then the KPI strip and "Tap an agent to open its chat" Chat The ops column (KPI strip, agent cards, the selected agent's sessions and New chat) beside the chat; a chat header with the session title, Running / Waiting for approval, the agent, run id and start time, Open runs and Stop run The chat, with the approval banner above it Any page The approval banner while something waits; the page renders in the frame's outlet under a title row The approval banner, then the page Tablet widths use the desktop frame without the ops column.

Mission sets meta.approvals: 'frame', so builtin.approvals stops toasting while Mission is on screen: the frame shows every pending approval itself. Banner, on every page except the overview (which lists them) and the approvals page: the oldest pending approval ("Coder needs your approval to continue", the exact call, its risk, how long it has waited, how many more wait) with Review, Deny and Approve. When nothing is listed in /api/approvals but a run is paused on a gate in the open chat, the banner shows that gate on the other pages with Open chat. The banner is a region named by its title, and only the title is live: a screen reader announces it when an approval appears, not each tick of the timer. Nav badge and bell: the number of pending approvals. Agent card: an agent with a pending approval (listed, or a gate in the open chat) shows as "Waiting for approval" with the call and a waiting timer, and is listed first. Overview: one request card per pending approval ("Needs approval · Coder wants to run a command", the call, the reason, Deny / Approve, in the banner's order). Thread: the chat draws gates as approval cards (meta.chat.approvals: 'card'). ⌘ / Ctrl J moves focus to the banner's Approve button; ⌘ / Ctrl N starts a new chat. In a browser tab most browsers keep ⌘ / Ctrl N for a new window and the page never sees it; use the ops column's New chat button there (the shortcut works in an installed app window).

Above each answer the chat shows the run's steps (meta.chat.turnHeader): Think, each tool by name, Answer, Handoff → agent and Approval pending, each as wide as the time it took, with its duration (a waiting gate counts up as 0:42). The steps are derived in the browser from the turn's own parts and their timing, so the timeline needs no server call.

Data Source When it is missing KPIs (runs today and the change, success rate, cost against the FinOps daily budget, p50 / p95 latency), agent status, recent runs The runs layout data kind. Until a browser built-in provides it, the mission board reads the run ledger's routes itself (GET /api/runs/kpis?window=today, /api/runs/agents, /api/runs?limit=10), every 5 s while the tab is visible and on approval events, and stops when Mission is switched away builtin.run-ledger off (the routes answer 404): "Run history is off on this server", no counts in the nav Pending approvals The approvals layout data kind (builtin.approvals, its own /api/approvals/stream) No banner, no badge Sessions and the open chat The sessions and chat kinds (builtin.chat) No session list or chat header details Health pill GET /api/provider/health every 30 s "Status unknown" See layout data for the run ledger's routes and gating: it is mounted while command or mission is on offer.
meta.chat Value sessions frame (the ops column draws the agent's sessions) thread dense approvals card turnHeader the run timeline (RunTimeline, from the mission board's entry)

pages.t: Layout data: run ledger and artifacts
pages.d: Two built-in records serve data that only the selectable layouts read. Each lives in

s.x: Two built-in records serve data that only the selectable layouts read. Each lives in its own feature module and mounts only while a layout that needs it is on offer: Record Module Serves layouts Routes builtin.run-ledger features/run_ledger.py command, mission /api/runs* builtin.artifacts features/artifacts.py chat-canvas /api/artifacts*

Under style: app every layout is on offer by default, so both records are on. layout.available (YAML) or aiui.set_layout(available=[...]) narrows the offer. With available: [chat-canvas] only builtin.artifacts mounts, and with available: [mission] only builtin.run-ledger does. Under any other style (dashboard, the standalone default, or chat) no layout is on offer. Both records are then disabled with the reason no layout needs it in /api/plugins?origin=builtin. Their modules are never imported and their routes answer 404. extensions.enabled: [builtin.run-ledger] mounts a record whatever the layouts are. extensions.disabled always wins. builtin.artifacts owns one page, artifacts (shell_only, kind: native, layouts: [chat-canvas]): every chat's artifacts, newest first, with their versions. The React page is layout-features/artifacts/ArtifactsPage (chunk lf-artifacts), registered lazily by the browser built-in builtin.artifacts (src/frontend/src/builtin/artifacts.ts) only while the manifest lists the page. The shell shows it in the nav while Chat and Canvas is the frame, and its URL (where Share links land, /artifacts?session=…&artifact=…&v=…) renders under any layout. Like every shell_only page it reaches the app shell manifest only, never /api/pages or the dashboard. builtin.run-ledger adds no page. Every route is authenticated in all three auth modes, like any other /api/* route. None is public.

The ledger keeps one record per chat run: its session, agent, start and end, status (running, waiting, completed, failed, cancelled), its steps (reasoning, tool, text, approval, handoff), and the tokens, cost and model of the run's usage records. It adds no wire event. A client reads the ledger after run_completed. Route Returns GET /api/runs?after=&agent=&session_id=&limit= {runs: RunSummary[], count}, newest first (limit 1–500, default 50) GET /api/runs/{run_id} RunDetail with its steps, or 404 GET /api/runs/kpis?window=today\ 24h\ 7d RunKpis; any other window is 400 GET /api/runs/agents {agents: AgentStatus[]}, running and waiting agents first The shapes are the ones in src/frontend/src/sdk/layoutTypes.ts: camelCase keys, times in epoch milliseconds. RunKpis holds: runs and runsDelta, the change against the previous window of the same length; successRate, from 0 to 1, with cancelled runs left out; cost and budget; p50Ms and p95Ms, the latency of completed runs. budget is finops.daily_cost_budget_usd from the runtime config (Settings, FinOps & Budgets), multiplied by 7 for the 7d window. It is left out when that value is unset or 0, or when finops.enabled is false. Tokens and cost per run. usage.track_usage() takes run_id=. When it is not given, it uses the run the calling task is serving, from the praisonaiui.features.chat.current_run_id context variable. The chat sets that variable for the whole run, and PraisonAIProvider passes it on. POST /api/usage/track accepts run_id in its body. A provider that records usage without a run id is joined to the run by session and time window instead, and the run then carries approximate: true. Storage. Finished runs are held in memory (the newest 1000) and appended to /runs/ledger.jsonl. The data dir is PRAISONAI_HOME, else AIUI_DATA_DIR, else ~/.praisonaiui. The append runs on a single writer thread, so the chat broadcast never waits on the disk. The file is read back the first time a /api/runs* route is called, and it is compacted once it holds more than twice the ring size.

The ledger is fed by a hook that any server-side code can use: The observer sees every event that ChatManager.broadcast sends, whether or not a client is connected. After each run it also gets one run_closed event, which clients never see. By the time it arrives, the provider has finished and its usage is tracked. Observers run inline on the event loop, so they must be quick and must not change event. An observer that raises is logged and skipped.

The browser derives artifacts from the chat: fenced code, tables, file and media elements, and A2UI surfaces. The extraction rules live only in the client. The server stores what the client sends: the index for each session, so the nav can count artifacts across sessions, and the versions the user edited. Route Does GET /api/artifacts?session_id=&limit= The latest version of every key, newest first, without content: {artifacts, count, sessions} GET /api/artifacts/{session_id} Every version, with content: {sessionId, artifacts} PUT /api/artifacts/{session_id}/{key} Upserts a derived version, or adds a user edit: {artifact} DELETE /api/artifacts/{session_id}/{key}[?version=N] Removes one key, or one version of it DELETE /api/artifacts/{session_id} Removes the whole session Deleting a chat (DELETE /sessions/{id}, which the chat, the Sessions page and aiui sessions delete use) also deletes its artifacts. The body of a PUT is an Artifact. kind is one of code, table, markdown, file, image, pdf, video or a2ui. With edited: true, or with no version, the PUT adds the next version. With a version, it replaces that version. If the user edited that version, the PUT is refused with 409. The limits are 512 KB of content for each version, 50 versions for each key (unedited versions are dropped first), and 500 keys for each session. url must be a relative or same-origin path, or an http:, https:, blob: or data:image/ URL, the same rule chat markdown uses. The server first normalises the URL the way a browser does: it drops tab, CR and LF, and strips leading and trailing control characters and spaces. So java\nscript: is refused like javascript:. The normalised form is the one stored. Each session is one JSON file under /artifacts/, named by a hash of the session id. Each write goes to a temporary file that is then renamed into place.

pages.d: The Chat page of the dashboard style (and of the app shell, which hosts the same view): real-time agent chat over a WebSocket, with markdown rendering, tool cal

s.x: The Chat page of the dashboard style (and of the app shell, which hosts the same view): real-time agent chat over a WebSocket, with markdown rendering, tool call cards and session history. The browser side is the vanilla chat.js view; the server side is the chat feature (praisonaiui.features.chat). The chat in the app shell, dark: an agent thought for two seconds, ran python3 --version, answered and now waits for approval to install numpy; the table and script it made sit under the answer
Without a @aiui.reply callback the chat runs the configured agents through the PraisonAI provider (pip install "aiui[praisonai]").
A chat message travels through 5 layers before reaching the browser:

File Layer Responsibility src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js Frontend WS connection, DOM rendering, session history src/praisonaiui/features/chat.py Backend ChatManager, _run_and_broadcast, history API src/praisonaiui/server.py Backend SSE streaming path (run_agent endpoint) src/praisonaiui/providers/__init__.py Provider SDK → RunEvent bridge, _run_direct_mode src/praisonaiui/datastore.py Storage MemoryDataStore / JSONFileDataStore src/praisonaiui/provider.py Protocol RunEventType enum definition

Agents created via YAML config, CRUD API, jobs, or channel bots automatically get tools resolved through the ToolResolver. Tool names in config are resolved to callable Python functions from 4 sources: Local tools.py file (backward compatibility) praisonaiagents.tools.TOOL_MAPPINGS (built-in tools) praisonai_tools package (community tools) Tool registry (programmatically registered tools)
Agents created via POST /api/agents also support tools:

Component Tool Resolution Gateway _create_agents_from_config() ✅ ToolResolver Integration create_gateway_from_yaml() ✅ ToolResolver Provider _get_or_create_agent() ✅ Default tools Channel bot _start_channel_bot() ✅ Default tools Jobs _execute_job() fallback ✅ ToolResolver CRUD agents _run() fallback ✅ ToolResolver CRUD agents _sync_to_gateway() ✅ ToolResolver

Assistant messages are rendered with full markdown support: Bold, italic, strikethrough Inline code and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting Ordered and unordered lists Links (auto-detected and rendered safely)

A tool call row (execute_command, Done in 0.3 s) above the answer, then an approval card for pip install numpy with Approve and Deny When agents use tools, each call is displayed as a collapsible card: Tool name and status indicator (running/completed/failed) Input arguments (JSON) Output results (rendered in code blocks) #### Tool Call Lifecycle Tool calls go through 4 stages: emit → enrich → dedup → persist. 1. Emit — The SDK fires TOOL_CALL_START / DELTA_TOOL_CALL / TOOL_CALL_END events via StreamEventEmitter. The provider maps these to RunEvent types (TOOL_CALL_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED). 2. Enrich — _run_and_broadcast() in chat.py enriches each tool call event with display-friendly fields via _enrich_tool_payload(): Field Source Example icon Mapped from tool name 🔍, 📝, 💾 description Generated from name + args "🔍 Searching for 'Django latest version'" step_number Auto-incrementing counter per run 1, 2, 3 formatted_result Truncated result string "✓ Done" tool_call_id SDK-assigned or UUID fallback "call_abc123" 3. Dedup — Both DELTA_TOOL_CALL (stream) and hook callbacks fire for the same tool call. The handler uses _seen_tool_started / _seen_tool_completed sets keyed by tool_call_id and name to suppress duplicates. A re-broadcast with has_complete_args=True is allowed to update the description with keyword-rich text. 4. Persist — After the run completes, all enriched tool calls are merged by tool_call_id into collected_tool_calls and saved alongside the assistant message: #### Reloading during a reply The React chat asks for run_attach when it opens a session. A run whose tab was reloaded comes back as the tab's own turn: the reply so far (the server keeps each live run's events, consecutive tokens merged, up to 2,000 events), the Stop button, and the composer waiting until the run ends. A run that another open tab started shows read-only, also with the reply so far; both tabs can keep sending. #### Turn order A reply is saved when its run ends, so two runs in one session (a second tab, or a question sent after a reload while the first reply is still running) finish out of order. A user message carries a turn_id and its reply a reply_to with the same value; GET /api/chat/history/{id} lists each reply right after its own question. History saved before these fields existed is shown in the order it was saved. #### Tool Call Persistence Schema Tool calls are persisted alongside assistant messages in the datastore. When a session is reloaded from history, tool call steps are reconstructed from the toolCalls array on each assistant message. Assistant message schema in the datastore: #### History Reload Rendering
New Session: Click "New Chat" to create a fresh session Session History: Switch between sessions in the sidebar Message History: Full conversation history per session via REST API

Click the Stop button (or send chat_abort with the run_id over the WebSocket) to cancel a run Only the connection that started a run may stop it or answer its prompts (or any client, once that connection is gone) The partial response is preserved in history
Upload files to include with your chat messages — see Attachments for details.

Chat history is stored through the BaseDataStore interface: by default the praisonaiagents session store, or JSON files, memory or SQL with aiui run --datastore. See Session Management. Each stored session holds its messages, with toolCalls on assistant messages:

The content field on assistant messages stores the SDK's final response from agent.chat() — the same text displayed by finalizeDelta() in the live view. This ensures the reloaded view matches what the user saw during streaming. During streaming, text tokens are accumulated in full_response. When RUN_COMPLETED arrives with event.content (the SDK's authoritative return value), it replaces the accumulated tokens for storage. This prevents intermediate narrative text from being duplicated on reload.
On a server with auth on, the browser first exchanges its key for a single-use ticket (POST /api/auth/ws-ticket) and connects with ?ticket=; see Deployment.
A frame that is not a JSON object is answered with {"type": "protocol_error", "error": ...}; the connection stays open.
All events include session_id and run_id.

Endpoint Method Description /api/chat/send POST Start a run; the reply streams to WebSocket clients /api/chat/history/{session_id} GET Get message history for a session /api/chat/abort POST Abort an active run ({"run_id": ...}) /api/chat/context-stats GET Context-window usage for a session /api/chat/ws WebSocket Real-time chat streaming
Response includes toolCalls on assistant messages:
The chat frontend is a vanilla JavaScript view, src/praisonaiui/templates/frontend/plugins/views/chat.js, shipped as-is with the package (it is not generated by the frontend build).

Function Purpose connectWebSocket() Open the WS (with a ticket when auth is on); reconnects on close handleWsMessage(data) Event dispatch — routes to rendering functions appendMessage(role, content, agentName) Render a complete message (history load) appendDelta(token, agentName) Streaming — append token to currentDeltaEl finalizeDelta(content, agentName) End streaming — replace with final content appendToolCall(data, status) Render tool call card updateToolCall(data, status) Update card with result appendReasoning(step) Render thinking step appendAskWidget(question, options, sessionId, runId) Render user-input prompt appendMemoryIndicator(text) Show memory update spinner loadSession(sessionId) Fetch history → render messages + tool calls restoreSessionHistory(sessionId) Same as above, on WS reconnect renderMarkdown(text) Custom zero-dependency markdown renderer escapeHtml(str) XSS prevention sanitizer

During streaming, all text tokens go into a single currentDeltaEl DOM element — even across tool call boundaries. Tool call cards are sibling elements inserted alongside the text element. When run_completed arrives, finalizeDelta(content) replaces the accumulated text with the SDK's final response.
The chat UI supports dark and light themes via CSS custom properties — see Theme System.
