pages.d: Inside an @aiui.reply (or @aiui.on_message) handler you can ask who is calling, keep state for

s.x: Inside an @aiui.reply (or @aiui.on_message) handler you can ask who is calling, keep state for this chat, read the chat's history in the shape an LLM wants, pop a notice, and call the UI from blocking worker code. Nothing to configure. Each API resolves to the chat being answered (two people chatting at once never see each other's data), also in tasks the handler starts and aiui.make_async threads.

Attribute Value id The chat (session) id. user The signed-in user as a dict (id, username, extra fields; never the password hash), or None. aiui.current_user() returns the same dict. client_type "webapp" (a browser), "api" (a script or HTTP client), "copilot", or the bot platform ("slack", "discord", "teams", …). chat_profile The profile chosen for this chat, or the server-wide selection. chat_settings Settings sent with the chat (dict). env Per-chat values sent by the client (dict of strings). language The best tag of the caller's Accept-Language ("fr-CA"), or None. headers Request headers, lower-cased, with credentials removed (Authorization, Cookie, and any header whose name mentions a token, key, secret, password, auth or session). It is None outside a handler. A client names itself with ?client= on the chat WebSocket or an X-Aiui-Client: header (letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters). A chat turn ({type: "chat", ...} on /api/chat/ws, or the body of POST /api/chat/send) may carry chat_profile, chat_settings and env; they stay with the chat for its later turns.

A key/value store private to the current chat, kept across its turns. Preset keys: id, user, chat_profile, chat_settings, env. Values live in memory (the last 5,000 chats), so keep what must survive a restart in your own database. Outside a handler get returns the default and set raises.

The chat's messages, oldest first, including the one being answered; each finished reply is added. After a restart the saved history is reloaded from the datastore. At most 200 messages are kept. Method Does get() A copy of the messages: [{"role", "content"}, ...]. add(content, role="assistant") Append a message (a string with a role, or a {"role", "content"} dict). Roles: system, user, assistant, tool. remove(message) Remove the latest message equal to message; returns True if one was removed. clear() Forget the history (for example on a "new topic" command). to_openai(system=None, max_messages=None) OpenAI chat messages, with an optional system prompt first and only the last max_messages. Works with any OpenAI-compatible client.

Run blocking work in a thread so the chat stays responsive, and call the UI from inside it: make_async(fn, executor=None) runs fn on a thread pool (yours, if given) with the handler's context. From that thread, run_sync(coro, timeout=None) runs the coroutine on the server's loop and waits; in a plain script it starts its own loop; in async code it raises RuntimeError (use await).

@aiui.on_chat_start runs once per chat before its first reply, as that chat, so it is the place to fill aiui.user_session; @aiui.on_chat_end runs as the chat when its last connection closes. See Chat lifecycle.

Load a model, an index or a client once and share it across every chat (@aiui.cache(ttl=3600, maxsize=8) takes options; async def works too): Option Does ttl=None Seconds an entry is kept; None keeps it until cleared. maxsize=None Keep only the most recently used entries; None for no limit. fn.cache_clear() Forget every entry. Entries are keyed by the arguments (unhashable ones, like a list, by their repr) and live in the server's memory. It is thread-safe; concurrent first calls share one computation (a caller cancelled by Stop does not cancel it). Exceptions are never cached, so the next call tries again.

type is info, success, warning or error; duration is in milliseconds. The notice is never saved with the reply or added to aiui.chat_context. Clients receive {type: "toast", session_id, run_id, message, variant, duration?} on the chat WebSocket; both built-in chats show it as a toast. Returns False outside a handler. (aiui.toast(...) builds a toast component for a page.)

pages.d: Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are

s.x: Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are read into the agent's prompt, images go to the model as multimodal input. The default limit is 10 MB per file.
The agent receives the extracted PDF text before the user message. The reply streams to WebSocket clients (see Gateway Chat).

Content type Processing What the agent sees application/pdf Text extracted with pypdf (a dependency of aiui) --- Attached PDF: name --- block before the message image/* File path passed to the agent's attachments The image, for vision-capable models Anything else allowed File read as text --- Attached File: name --- block before the message

The check is on the MIME type the client sends with the upload, not the file extension. Browsers set it; with curl, add ;type=... to the -F value, or the file arrives as application/octet-stream and is rejected: Category MIME types Text text/plain, text/csv, text/markdown Data application/json Documents application/pdf Images image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp Any other type is rejected with 400 {"error": "Type not allowed: ..."}, and a file over the size limit with 400 {"error": "File too large: ..."}. Files are stored under the system temp directory (/praisonai_attachments/), and the id registry is kept in memory: after a restart, earlier ids no longer resolve.
Add -F "index_to_knowledge=true" to the upload to also store the file in the knowledge base. The response then carries knowledge_indexed (and knowledge_error when it failed).

AttachmentManager(storage_dir=None, max_size_mb=10, allowed_types=None) takes the limits. The server creates its default instance with praisonaiui.features.attachments.get_attachment_manager(); there is no public setter for a custom one yet.

Endpoint Method Description /api/chat/attachments POST Upload a file (multipart: file, optional session_id, index_to_knowledge) /api/chat/attachments/{session_id} GET List a session's attachments /api/chat/attachments/{attachment_id} DELETE Delete an attachment /api/chat/media/{attachment_id} GET Serve a stored generated-media file
Response:
Over the WebSocket, put attachment_ids in the chat frame: POST /run (the chat's HTTP fallback when the WebSocket cannot open) takes the same attachment_ids and handles them the same way.
Text and PDF files are put before the message text. Every file of the message is also on message.attachments, so an app can read images itself:
Gateway Chat: the chat interface Sessions: session management

pages.d: A message can carry elements: images, PDFs, videos, audio, files and code

s.x: A message can carry elements: images, PDFs, videos, audio, files and code blocks shown with the message text. Each element is a dict with a type, the fields below, and an optional name and display.

These reach the chat as message_element events: aiui.audio(url) and aiui.video(url) work the same way. msg.add_image(), add_pdf(), add_video(), add_audio(), add_file() and add_code() validate their arguments and append typed elements (ImageElement and the others in praisonaiui.schema.models); they reach the chat like dicts. So does any object with model_dump() or to_dict().

Each aiui.Message(...).send() and each aiui.say(...) is its own message: the chat shows it at once, as its own block under the same answer, with its author when it is not the agent, and its elements and actions under it. A reload shows the same blocks. Copy, feedback and Regenerate act on the whole answer. The saved reply keeps content (the messages joined by a blank line) and segments ([{id, text, author?}]); elements carry the message_id of their message. msg.update() and msg.remove() change only that message while the reply runs. On the wire every piece of reply text names its message: run_content carries message_id with a token (appended) or a whole content (sets that message's text), plus author when set. message_element and message_actions carry the same message_id; message_update, message_remove and action_remove edit a message already shown. The sections below list each element's fields.

Display images with thumbnail and click-to-zoom functionality. Properties: url (required): Image URL name (optional): Display name alt (optional): Alt text for accessibility display (optional): Display mode - "inline" (default), "side", "page" width (optional): Fixed width in pixels height (optional): Fixed height in pixels

Display PDF documents with inline viewer or link to open in new tab. Properties: url (required): PDF URL name (optional): Display name display (optional): "inline": Embedded PDF viewer (600px height) "side": Smaller embedded viewer (400px height) "page": Link to open in new tab

Display videos with native HTML5 video player. Properties: url (required): Video URL name (optional): Display name controls (optional): Show video controls (default: True) autoplay (optional): Auto-play video (default: False) loop (optional): Loop video (default: False)

Display audio with native HTML5 audio player. Properties: url (required): Audio URL name (optional): Display name controls (optional): Show audio controls (default: True) autoplay (optional): Auto-play audio (default: False) loop (optional): Loop audio (default: False)

Display downloadable files with file type icons and size information. Properties: url (required): File download URL name (optional): Display name size (optional): File size in bytes mime_type (optional): MIME type for file type detection

Display syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy functionality. Properties: content (required): Code content language (optional): Programming language for syntax highlighting name (optional): Display name
All elements support three display modes: inline (default): Full width, normal display side: Smaller size, suitable for sidebars page: Full page width, maximum size
add_file() raises ValueError when size is over 100 MB and add_code() when content is over 1 MB. Dict elements are not checked.
praisonaiui.schema.models has a model per type (ImageElement, PdfElement, VideoElement, AudioElement, FileElement, CodeElement) that validates the fields above:

When an agent or tool creates an image during a chat run, the UI receives message_element events over WebSocket/SSE and renders them inline. This uses the same element dict shape as above but is driven by the RunEvent protocol, not only Message.send(). See Image Preview in Chat for the full architecture: detection (media_utils), provider bridge, persistence, and swappable backends.

Layer Module Backend-agnostic? Detection media_utils.py Yes — normalises OpenAI, URL, b64, element dicts Protocol provider.py — RunEventType.MESSAGE_ELEMENT Yes Adapter providers/__init__.py — PraisonAI bridge only No — maps SDK/callback queue → protocol Transport chat.py — broadcast + persist Yes Storage attachments.py — GET /api/chat/media/{id} Yes — reuses attachment store for b64 UI chat.js, ElementRenderer Yes — renders {type, url, alt} Detection and UI do not import PraisonAI. Only the provider adapter knows ImageAgent / OpenAI {data: [{url}]} shapes.
Defined in Python as RunEventType.MESSAGE_ELEMENT and mirrored in types.ts.

pages.d: A step is a named piece of work inside a reply: a tool call, an LLM call, a

s.x: A step is a named piece of work inside a reply: a tool call, an LLM call, a retrieval, a sub-run. The chat shows the reply's steps as a collapsible tree with each step's name, status (running, done, failed, stopped) and duration; opening a step shows its input, output and child steps. Steps are saved with the reply, so a reload shows the same tree with the same durations. @aiui.step works bare, with () or with arguments (@aiui.step("Search the web", type="tool")), on sync and async functions. The step is named after the function unless named; its input is the call's arguments (self/cls left out), its output the return value, and an exception marks it failed (and is raised as usual). aiui.Step is used as async with or with (sync code and worker threads too); in sync code step.stream_token(t) sends without await. Nesting is automatic: a step opened while another runs becomes its child, across awaits, in tasks started from it (asyncio.gather, create_task) and in aiui.make_async threads. parent= sets the parent explicitly.

aiui.Step(name, type="reasoning", parent=None, metadata={}, input=None, output=None) Field Meaning type run, tool, llm, embedding, retrieval, rerank, undefined, tool_call, reasoning, sub_agent, custom input, output Shown when the step is opened; data as JSON, text as is, each at most 1 MB metadata Extra data sent with the step's start and end id, start, end, duration, status, error Read-only: epoch ms, seconds, running/done/error/stopped, the exception text @aiui.step(name=None, type="reasoning", **metadata) wraps each call in a Step. Events (WebSocket and /run SSE, protocol 1.2), each with step_id: step_start (name, step_type, parent_id, start in epoch ms, input), step_update (token to append) and step_end (end, status, duration in seconds, error, and input/output when changed). The saved reply keeps steps: [{step_id, parent_id, name, step_type, status, start, end, input, output, error}]. A step outside a reply sends nothing but still times itself. await aiui.think("...") still shows unnamed reasoning text.

pages.d: 1. Code is submitted with a target language. A language outside the allowlist (default: python, javascript, bash) is a 400; so is any language other than Python

s.x: Sandboxed code execution with language allowlists, behind a human approval. Runs Python through the SDK's execute_code (praisonaiagents.tools.python_tools), which carries @require_approval(risk_level="critical"). Every run waits until someone approves it in the Approvals page.

Code is submitted with a target language. A language outside the allowlist (default: python, javascript, bash) is a 400; so is any language other than Python, because the SDK sandbox runs Python only. Without praisonaiagents the response is 503 with status: "degraded". Nothing runs, and nothing is simulated. Otherwise the request goes through the SDK's own approval gate on execute_code, wired to the aiui approvals queue. A pending execute_code entry (risk critical, arguments = the exact code) appears in GET /api/approvals/pending, and the HTTP request waits for the decision without blocking the server. Approve runs the code and returns 200. Deny, or no answer within the SDK registry timeout (300 s by default), returns 403 with status: "denied". One run needs one approval. Only the entry the server created for that run counts: an entry created with POST /api/approvals does not unlock a run, and approving a run with always: true approves that run only (critical tools never get a standing approval). To skip the human step on a trusted machine, opt out explicitly: add execute_code to the auto_approve_tools policy (PUT /api/approvals/policies; remove it to turn the gate back on) or set PRAISONAI_AUTO_APPROVE=true for the server process. Authentication is the server's job (AUTH_ENFORCE, require_auth, AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN): without credentials, the run and the approve/deny endpoints return 401.
Endpoint Method Description /api/code/languages GET List supported languages /api/code/execute POST Execute code in sandbox
Skills — Code execution tools in the skill catalog

pages.d: The model fallback feature (praisonaiui.features.model_fallback) lists the

s.x: The model fallback feature (praisonaiui.features.model_fallback) lists the available models and stores an ordered fallback chain that the UI can show and edit. The chain is stored, not applied Nothing in PraisonAIUI reads the chain when it sends a request: the provider still calls the agent's own model, and a failed call is not retried on the next model. The chain is also kept in memory only, so a restart clears it. Use it as a setting your own provider or @aiui.reply callback reads (see below).
The model list comes from litellm.model_list when LiteLLM is installed and has models configured. Otherwise it is a short static list: gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-5-sonnet and gemini-2.0-flash.
Use the server's shared manager, not a new ModelFallbackManager(), so you see what the API set:
Endpoint Method Description /api/models GET Available models and the current fallback chain /api/models/fallback PUT Set the chain ({"models": [...]}; 400 if not a list)
Providers: LLM provider configuration

pages.d: Visualize agent hierarchies — see which agents spawn subagents, track their status, and monitor the full execution tree.

s.x: Visualize agent hierarchies — see which agents spawn subagents, track their status, and monitor the full execution tree.

Each spawn is a record of parent agent, child agent and session in the server's SubagentManager: When praisonaiagents is installed, the manager subscribes to its handoff hook, so every agent handoff is recorded (parent, child and session id come from the hook payload; missing values become parent, child and default). Your own code can record spawns with register_spawn(). The tree for a session is built from its spawn records; an agent that is never a child is a root. Records are kept in memory and cleared on restart. Every record has status: "running"; completion is not tracked yet.
Endpoint Method Description /api/subagents GET All spawn records ({"spawns": [...]}) /api/subagents/{session_id} GET Get tree for a session
Gateway Chat: chat triggers agent execution Protocols: the feature protocol system

s.x: Synthesize speech from text using swappable backends — browser-native (zero cost) or OpenAI TTS API.

Default: BrowserTTSManager — uses the browser's built-in Web Speech API, requires no API key, runs entirely client-side. Optional: OpenAITTSManager — uses OpenAI's TTS API for higher-quality voices (alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer). Requires openai package and API key.

pages.d: Talk instead of typing. When an app turns on voice input, the chat composer

s.x: Talk instead of typing. When an app turns on voice input, the chat composer gets a microphone button. Press it, speak, and press it again: the recording is turned into text and put in the message box, after anything already typed, for you to read over and send. Voice input belongs to the realtime feature (builtin.realtime). It is off unless the app asks for it, so no other chat shows a microphone.

Give aiui a realtime manager that can transcribe speech. The bundled OpenAIRealtimeManager uses OpenAI speech to text (OPENAI_API_KEY, and OPENAI_BASE_URL for a compatible server): aiui.OpenAIRealtimeManager is the same class. There is no praisonaiui.realtime module: import it from praisonaiui or praisonaiui.features.realtime. Your own backend works too. Subclass RealtimeProtocol and implement transcribe: A manager without transcribe keeps the microphone hidden. aiui.set_realtime_manager(None) turns voice input off again.

State What you see At rest A microphone icon button before Send ("Record a voice message") Recording A red stop button and a running time; screen readers hear "Recording". Press the button again to stop and transcribe, or Escape to discard Transcribing A spinner in the button Done The text in the message box, with the caret at its end The browser asks for the microphone the first time. If access is blocked, a message says how to allow it in the browser's site settings; no microphone, or one busy in another app, gets its own message. A recording stops by itself after two minutes. The button is keyboard accessible (Tab to it, Enter or Space to start and stop, Escape to discard) and has a visible focus ring. Its code is a separate chunk that loads only for an app with voice input on.

Endpoint Method Description /api/realtime/voice GET {"enabled": bool, "max_seconds": 120, "max_bytes": 8388608}: whether the composer shows the microphone /api/realtime/transcribe POST The recording as the raw body (Content-Type: audio/*). Returns {"text": "..."} /api/realtime/transcribe answers 404 while voice input is off, 415 for a body that is not audio, 400 for an empty one, 413 over 8 MiB, 501 when the manager cannot transcribe, and 502 when the speech service fails (its message is logged by type only, never returned). Both routes need the same credentials as every other /api route.
The reply is text. Speaking it aloud (see TTS) and a hands-free, speech-to-speech session are not part of this feature.

s.x: Set the colour preset, corner radius and colour mode in YAML (site.theme) or from Python (aiui.set_theme()).

The Paper look in light and dark: the Chat and Canvas screen with the comparison table and the script the agent wrote What it changes: Docs sites (aiui build) draw in the Paper look itself: the palette in both modes, serif titles, 17px text on a 1.7 line height in a 40rem column, and the mono for code. Logo, favicon, brand colour, page background and a fixed colour mode for a site built with aiui build, all in aiui.yaml: One line is enough. logo: images/logo.svg and favicon: images/favicon.svg use one image in both modes. Files are published for you. A logo, favicon or background path relative to aiui.yaml is copied into the build at the same path, with site.basePath applied. aiui validate warns (7102) when the file is missing or outside the project folder. The logo swaps live. With logo.dark, both images are in the page and CSS shows the one for the current mode, so the theme toggle swaps them with no flash. An href on another site is a plain link. The favicon follows the browser. With favicon.dark, the built pages get two icon links with media="(prefers-color-scheme: …)", because the tab strip follows the browser's scheme, not the page's. Background. gradient (a soft wash of the accent at the top) and grid (hairlines that fade out) are drawn in CSS from the theme tokens, so they fit both modes and add no download. An image path or URL covers the page behind the content; background: {light: bg.png, dark: bg-dark.png} uses one image per mode. Strict mode. strict: true removes the theme toggle and ignores a reader's stored choice, so the site always shows mode (system still follows the OS).

Without it the family loads from Google Fonts weight 400, a range "100 900" for a variable font, or for Google Fonts a list [400, 700]. Default: Google Fonts 400 to 700; a file 400 format woff2, woff, truetype or opentype (default: from the file extension) One request for Google Fonts. Every Google family goes in one stylesheet link with display=swap, after a preconnect to both Google hosts, so text shows at once in the fallback font. Files are self-hosted. A source file is published at the same path (with site.basePath), declared with @font-face and font-display: swap, and a .woff2 body font is preloaded. Nothing loads from another host. Your font, the theme's fallbacks. The fonts set the theme's own variables in assets/theme.css, with the system stack behind them, so they win over the preset's fonts (also paper) in light and dark. aiui validate reports a source file that is not in the project (7014). A family name with quotes or braces, or a weight such as 450, is a config error.

One line picks the colours of every code block on a docs site (aiui build), from any of the 65 bundled themes: Key Value code A theme name for light and dark, or {light, dark} (each defaults to github-light / github-dark) codeLanguages TextMate grammar files (.json) beside aiui.yaml: a path, or {source, name, aliases} The theme's own background. A chosen theme draws the block on its background, with the header, hairlines and muted text mixed from its colours, so code: dracula stays readable on a light page. Without code, blocks keep the site's code background and the GitHub colours. Loaded only when used. Each theme and each grammar is its own file; a page downloads only the theme of its mode and the grammars its fences use. Your own language. A grammar is published with the site and loaded on the first fence that names it. Its fence name is name, else the grammar's name field (lowercased), else the file name; aliases defaults to the grammar's fileTypes. A grammar wins over a built-in language of the same name, and languages it embeds (embeddedLangs) highlight too. aiui validate warns with the nearest name when a theme is not bundled (7015; that mode keeps the GitHub theme), and when a grammar file is missing (7014) or is not a grammar (7015). Names are lowercased; one with spaces or other punctuation than +#._- is a config error.

Add your own stylesheets and scripts to every page of a docs build: customCss takes CSS text (anything with a {), a .css file beside aiui.yaml, a site path or a URL, one or a list. Files are published at the same path; CSS text goes into assets/custom.css. They load in the order listed, after every built-in stylesheet (at the end of , where the browser still applies them before the app paints), so a rule as specific as a built-in one wins, and theme variables such as --seed-accent or --aiui-font-sans just work. customJs takes .js or .mjs files or URLs. Each runs once per page load, after the app's own scripts, in the order listed. Local files get a ?v= content hash, so a new build is never served from a stale cache. aiui validate reports a file that is not in the project (7014). aiui run keeps applying customCss CSS text as before. Pages switch without a reload, so a script that works on the page listens for these events on window: Event detail When aiui:navigate { path } A link, the sidebar, search or back/forward moves to another page aiui:content-loaded { path, meta } The page's article is in the document, including the first page; meta holds the page's custom front matter keys To change pages from a script, push the URL and send the same event: history.pushState({}, '', '/docs/guide'); window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('aiui:navigate', { detail: { path: '/docs/guide' } })).

site.theme.mode (light, dark or system) wins over darkMode; system follows the reader's OS. The React styles served by aiui run and docs sites built with aiui build read it, and a viewer's own choice in the theme toggle wins over both. The full order is in Dark Mode.

The React UI already shows a theme toggle in its header. There is no npm package to install: inside this repository's frontend (src/frontend) the component comes from the in-repo components barrel, src/frontend/src/components/index.ts: A plugin page in the app shell (--style app) reads the current mode with useThemeMode() from @aiui/sdk instead.

Presets set CSS variables you can override with site.customCss or aiui.set_custom_css(). Each variable holds a complete CSS colour: A bare HSL triple such as --primary: 221 83% 53% no longer works (aiui validate warns, code 5001). In the app shell, set the seed instead (--seed-accent: hsl(221 83% 53%)) and the derived colours follow in both modes; see React app shell: theme seeds.
For full customization, scaffold a React project:

pages.d: The theme feature (praisonaiui.features.theme) holds the dashboard's colour

s.x: The theme feature (praisonaiui.features.theme) holds the dashboard's colour preset, mode (dark or light) and corner radius on the server, and serves them as CSS custom properties (--db-*) over /api/theme. The vanilla dashboard style and its chat page read these variables; the React app shell bridges them to its own tokens.
PUT /api/theme accepts any of preset (one of the 22 presets or a registered custom theme; an unknown name returns 400), mode and radius, and returns the full state.

Each mode sets a group of --db-* variables; the preset adds the accent and the radius setting adds --db-radius. A few of them: Variable Dark Light Usage --db-bg #18181b #fafafa Page background --db-text #ffffff #18181b Primary text --db-text-dim #a1a1aa #71717a Secondary text --db-border #3f3f46 rgba(0,0,0,0.08) Borders --db-card-bg rgba(255,255,255,0.03) rgba(0,0,0,0.02) Cards --db-hover #27272a rgba(0,0,0,0.04) Hover background --db-accent preset accent preset accent Buttons, links, highlights --db-accent-rgb preset r,g,b preset r,g,b Accent with alpha --db-accent-glow accent at 15% accent at 15% Focus and glow Sidebar, muted, popover, semantic (--db-success, --db-warning, --db-error, --db-info) and scrollbar variables follow the same pattern. Override any of them with aiui.set_custom_css().

A custom theme is an accent colour. Register one from Python: accent is any CSS colour; accentRgb is derived from a hex accent and is required otherwise. An invalid value raises ValueError. The theme then appears in the theme picker and in /api/theme/presets. Or over HTTP: A built-in preset name cannot be registered or deleted.

Endpoint Method Description /api/theme GET Full theme state and CSS variables /api/theme PUT Set preset, mode and/or radius /api/theme/presets GET All presets with accents, split into builtin and custom /api/theme/register POST Register a custom theme (name, accent, optional accentRgb) /api/theme/{name} DELETE Delete a custom theme

The page follows the OS when it changes. A static aiui build site has no server to report the app's choice, so it uses site.theme.darkMode (dark by default) unless the viewer picked a mode. pages.t: How the UI Looks Are Built
pages.d: A beginner-friendly guide to how PraisonAIUI creates its visual appearance — what controls the colors, fonts, and layout you see on screen.

s.x: A beginner-friendly guide to how PraisonAIUI creates its visual appearance — what controls the colors, fonts, and layout you see on screen.

PraisonAIUI's appearance comes from three layers working together: In plain English: You choose a theme preset (like "zinc" or "blue") in your config The system translates that into CSS variables (color codes) Every button, text, and background reads those variables to know what color to be

dark_mode=True or False fixes the app's default mode. With dark_mode=None, or without set_theme(), YAML site.theme (mode: light|dark|system or darkMode) decides, and without that the UI follows the viewer's stored choice (aiui-theme-preference), then the OS.

The preset sets your color palette — it changes the accent color used for buttons, active states, and highlights across the entire UI. Category Options Neutral zinc (default), slate, stone, gray, neutral Warm red, orange, amber, yellow Cool blue, indigo, violet, purple, cyan, sky, teal Nature green, emerald, lime Vibrant pink, rose, fuchsia
When light mode is on, all backgrounds flip to white/light gray and text becomes dark.
Value Effect none Sharp, square corners sm Slightly rounded md Medium rounded (default) lg More rounded xl Very rounded, pill-shaped buttons

For fine-grained control, override these variables in customCss: Variable Default (dark) What It Controls --db-bg #0a0a0f Page background --db-sidebar-bg #111118 Sidebar background --db-accent #6366f1 Buttons, active items, highlights --db-text #e4e4e7 Primary text --db-text-dim #71717a Secondary/muted text --db-border rgba(255,255,255,0.06) Borders and dividers --db-card-bg rgba(255,255,255,0.03) Card backgrounds --db-radius 10px Corner roundness

When the same setting is defined in multiple places: Priority Source Example 1 (highest) CLI flag --style chat 2 Python API aiui.set_theme(preset="blue") 3 YAML config site.theme.preset: blue 4 (lowest) Built-in defaults zinc, dark, md radius
PraisonAIUI includes two different chat interfaces. Understanding the difference helps you choose the right one and know what features to expect.

When it's active: style: chat, style: agents, or style: playground This is the recommended chat for most users. It's built with React and benefits from the full modern web stack. What you get: Feature How it works 🎨 Your theme colors Automatically follows your preset and darkMode settings 📋 Copy code button Click to copy any code block — shows "✓ Copied" feedback 🌈 Syntax highlighting Code is color-coded by language (Python, JavaScript, etc.) 📊 Markdown tables Tables render as proper formatted tables 🔤 Rich typography Headers, bold, italic, lists — all beautifully styled 📎 File attachments Upload files to include as context

When it's active: style: dashboard This is a lighter chat built as a dashboard plugin. It's designed for quick admin interactions within the dashboard. What you get: Feature How it works 🎨 Dashboard theme Uses the dashboard's color scheme (now follows your preset!) 💬 Basic markdown Bold, italic, headings, code blocks, links, lists 🔧 Tool call display Shows when the AI is using tools 📋 Session management Create, switch, and manage conversations 🤖 Agent selection Pick which AI agent to chat with What it doesn't have (yet): ❌ Copy button on code blocks ❌ Syntax highlighting (code blocks are plain text) ❌ Markdown tables

If you want... Use this style Best chat experience with all features style: chat Multi-agent dashboard with admin controls style: dashboard Agent profiles and switching style: agents Side-by-side prompt testing style: playground

Theming — Theme presets and YAML configuration Styles — The 6 UI styles (chat, agents, playground, etc.) Dark Mode — Dark mode toggle Dashboard — Dashboard feature overview

pages.d: A UI plugin is a Python package that adds pages, blocks, chat tool renderers,

s.x: A UI plugin is a Python package that adds pages, blocks, chat tool renderers, settings sections, sidebar groups, theme presets, HTTP routes and CLI commands to the React app shell (style: app, or AIUI_SHELL=app). Installing the package is the whole setup: the server finds it through the praisonaiui.plugins entry point. The smallest complete plugin lives in examples/plugins/aiui-hello-plugin. aiui run app.py opens the app shell (style: app) unless the app, its YAML or --style picks another style, so a plain @aiui.reply app needs no flag. AIUI_SHELL=app only switches the dashboard style to the app shell; it leaves an explicit chat or other React style alone (the server logs AIUI_SHELL=app ignored: style is 'chat'). Then open /hello (a React page) and /hello-blocks (a server-driven page). Three different things are called plugins UI plugins (this page): Python packages, entry point praisonaiui.plugins, React app shell only. Policy in YAML extensions:. Dashboard plugins: folders with a manifest.json under dashboard-plugins/, vanilla JS views (see Agent UI host). The app shell still hosts them as legacy pages. Docs plugins: site.plugins in aiui.yaml (static site compiler hooks). The default is nav-intercept; see Deploy to GitHub Pages → Legacy plugins.

The server imports each entry point once, isolates failures, and lists what the plugin contributes in the shell manifest. The shell installs window.__AIUI_SDK__ and then import()s every plugin module named in the manifest. An import map points the bare specifiers react, react/jsx-runtime, react-dom, react-dom/client and @aiui/sdk at small shims that re-export the shell's own modules, so a plugin shares the shell's single React (hooks work, nothing is bundled twice). A module registers what it provides through @aiui/sdk, or default-exports a component that the shell registers under the page id / block type / tool name. The app's own React pages and blocks use the same mechanism. The shell and the SDK are a small core that names no page: the chat page and its "New chat" command are the first-party plugin builtin.chat in src/frontend/src/builtin, registered with registerPage and registerCommand when the manifest lists the page; the approval toasts are builtin.approvals (on notify and navigate); and the core block types are registered with registerBlock. A test in the frontend (shell/core-purity.test.ts) fails if the core imports a feature module or names a built-in page.

The value names a plugin object, a class (instantiated with no arguments) or a zero-argument factory. The entry-point name becomes a URL segment, so it must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*. Every member except name is optional: Member Returns Effect name str Plugin id (/api/plugins/, /_plugins/ /, aiui) version str Shown by aiui plugins list sdk int Browser SDK major the plugin targets (default 1); a mismatch marks it incompatible pages() PageSpec or dicts Sidebar pages blocks() BlockSpec Renderers for block types tool_renderers() ToolRendererSpec Chat renderers for tool calls routes() Starlette routes Mounted under /api/plugins/ static_dir() Path Served at /_plugins/ / features() feature protocols Registered like built-in features (an enabled built-in's names win) cli_commands() typer.Typer or click command aiui … and aiui plugins … setup(ctx) None Called once per create_app() with {"style", "config"} settings() SettingsSectionSpec or dicts Sections of the shell's settings dialog (below) nav_groups() NavGroupSpec or dicts The sidebar groups your pages use, with their position themes() ThemeSpec or dicts Theme presets made of seed tokens layouts() LayoutSpec or dicts App shell frames (ADR 0003) the viewer can pick (below) PageSpec, BlockSpec, ToolRendererSpec, SettingsSectionSpec, SettingsField, NavGroupSpec, ThemeSpec, LayoutSpec and get_plugin_settings are importable from praisonaiui (or praisonaiui.plugin_registry). Dicts with the same field names work too.

kind Renders Needs react The component from module (default export, or export) module blocks A server-driven block tree (see below) api_endpoint, default /api/plugins/ /pages/ iframe module in a sandboxed iframe (no same-origin access) module These three are the only kinds a plugin can use. native and legacy are first-party only (the shell never imports a plugin's legacy view): a plugin page with another kind, or a misspelt one, is dropped with a warning and aiui plugins doctor fails on it. A relative module ("hello.js") resolves into static_dir(); the server then serves /_plugins/ /hello.js and adds its sha384 integrity to the manifest and the import map. The integrity is a cache-consistency check, not tamper protection: the server hashes the file it is about to serve (re-hashed when the file changes, so a rebuilt bundle keeps loading), which guards against a stale or partly written file between the page render and the module fetch. Someone who can change files in the plugin's static_dir can also change what is hashed. Declare integrity= on the PageSpec to pin a hash you computed at build time. When auth is enforced the page carries no manifest (and so no import-map integrity) before login; the shell loads plugin modules afterwards. When two sources use the same page id, the first wins: pages registered by the app (aiui.register_page), then built-in pages, then entry-point plugins (in discovery order), then dashboard-plugin folders. aiui plugins doctor warns about shadowed ids.

s.h: Settings, nav groups and theme presets
s.x: Three hooks contribute to the shell itself rather than to a page. They were added under SDK 1; a shell that has them lists the features settings, nav-groups and theme-presets in SDK_FEATURES, and an older host simply never calls them. Nav groups. NavGroupSpec(name, order=None, folded=False) names a group that your pages use in PageSpec.group. order places it among the groups: the groups the app lists in layout.groups.order (Agent, Work, Control by default) sit at 100, 200 and 300, groups without an order follow them, and layout.groups.last (Settings) stays last. So order=250 puts the group between Work and Control, and order=50 puts it first. folded=True starts the group collapsed until the viewer opens it. The app's own configuration wins: a plugin cannot move a group that layout.groups (or set_dashboard(groups=...)) names. Every frame lists a declared group. The classic frame shows all groups in its sidebar; the built-in layouts, which keep the app's own groups in More (⌘K), still show the groups plugins declared, in this order and folded as declared: under the primary pages in chat, chat-canvas, workbench and mission, in the rail in command, and under More tools in guided. Settings. A SettingsSectionSpec(id, title, fields, description="", order=100) becomes a section of the shell's settings dialog, which opens from "Plugin settings" (the sliders button in the classic header, a "Plugin settings" row or rail button in every built-in layout, shown only while some plugin has a section) or from "Plugin settings" in the command palette. Each SettingsField(key, label="", type="string", default=None, description="", options=None) is drawn from its type: type Control Default value string One-line text input "" text Multi-line text area "" number Number input 0 boolean Switch False select Select from options (strings or {"value", "label"} dicts) the first option The values are stored per plugin in $AIUI_DATA_DIR/plugin-settings/ .json (default ~/.praisonaiui). The server serves each section at /api/plugins/ /settings/: GET returns {"values": {...}} with the defaults filled in, and PUT {"values": {...}} validates every key against its field (unknown keys, wrong types and options not in the list answer 400 with {"error", "fields": {key: reason}}, and nothing is written). That path is reserved for a plugin that declares settings(): it is matched before the plugin's own routes. It sits under the same mount as routes(), so it is authenticated like every route and default-deny for entry-point plugins on remote or auth-enforced servers unless they are named in extensions.enabled. get_plugin_settings(name, section) returns the same values to Python; a stored value that no longer fits its field (an option you removed) falls back to the default. Theme presets. A ThemeSpec(id, label, light={}, dark={}) sets L0 seed tokens per colour mode: --seed-* (--seed-accent, --seed-tint, --seed-paper, --seed-ink …), --radius, --tint-mix and --accent-mix. Every surface, text and accent colour is derived from the seeds (see DESIGN.md), so a preset never names a shadcn variable. Values are plain CSS values; anything else (another property, ;, braces, url(...)) is rejected. The viewer picks a preset in the command palette ("Sunrise theme", "Default theme"); the choice is kept per browser. Invalid entries of all three hooks (and of layouts()) are dropped one by one with a warning, and one hook that raises does not drop the others. The warning is printed once per start in the aiui run terminal (and on the Logs page), and aiui plugins doctor runs every entry through the same checks and fails on each one it would drop. The contributions travel on the plugin's record in the shell manifest (plugins[].settings, plugins[].navGroups, plugins[].themes), only for plugins whose browser surfaces the viewer may load.

The pages and features that ship with PraisonAIUI use the same mechanism. Each domain is a first-party plugin record in praisonaiui.builtin: for example builtin.chat holds the Chat and Chat + Canvas pages with the chat and attachments features, and builtin.work holds Work Hub, Kanban and Jobs Board with the kanban feature. Features with no page of their own have a record each (builtin.tts, builtin.pwa, builtin.video …). The server reads pages and features through the plugin registry, so the extension policy can switch a whole domain off: or aiui.set_extensions(disabled=["builtin.training"]). A disabled built-in contributes no pages: they leave GET /api/pages, the shell manifest and the sidebar. Its feature routes are not mounted (/api/training/... returns 404), the server does not load its feature modules, and a bundled dashboard-plugin folder that belongs to it (kanban belongs to builtin.work, video-studio to builtin.video, the sample-board demo page in the Examples group to builtin.examples) is not served either. The same holds for the routes the host itself serves for a built-in: builtin.mcp owns /api/mcp/*, builtin.debug owns /api/debug, builtin.overview owns GET /api/overview, builtin.feedback owns GET /api/feedback and builtin.jobs owns the optional /api/jobs proxy (set_jobs_proxy), so disabling them returns 404 there. builtin.logs serves GET /api/logs and /api/logs/* from its feature, and installs its log handler only while it is on. With the built-in off, an entry-point plugin may use its page ids and feature names. A few host routes stay mounted whichever built-ins are off, because the host, several pages or the CLI use them: GET /api/status (aiui status, the same data as /api/overview), POST /api/feedback (the chat thumbs), /api/config, /api/gateway/status, /api/provider*, the chat protocol (/agents, /sessions, /run, /cancel, /teams, /starters, /profiles, /welcome, /api/actions/*, thread sharing), /health*, auth, /api/pages, /api/features, /api/shell/manifest and /api/plugins. Disabling builtin.config removes its page only. Where a page id is also a JSON path (/agents, /sessions, or an app page named like an API), a browser navigation to / gets the page and fetch() gets the JSON, under the dashboard and app styles. tests/unit/test_route_table_snapshot.py pins the default route table. Some features are required: the server itself depends on auth, theme, chat, usage, config_runtime and sessions_ext. Disabling their record (builtin.auth, builtin.theme-picker, builtin.chat, builtin.usage, builtin.config, builtin.sessions) removes its pages and its other features, keeps the required feature mounted and logs a warning. Disabling builtin.auth therefore never turns authentication off. Built-ins are trusted and on by default. extensions.enabled is an allowlist for third-party plugins only, so it never hides a built-in page. Only the builtin. name disables a built-in: disabled: [logs] means a third-party plugin called logs. A builtin. name that matches no record logs a warning. The page-level controls still apply on top: aiui.set_pages([...]), pages.enabled / pages.disabled in config.yaml and aiui.remove_page() hide single pages (their APIs stay mounted), and aiui.register_page() with a built-in id replaces that page. register_feature() before the server starts replaces a built-in feature of the same name, as before. GET /api/plugins?origin=builtin (or origin=all) lists the built-in records with their status (and required: true where the host needs one of their features). Without the parameter the endpoint lists third-party plugins only, as before.

A plugin module is plain ESM. Write it by hand (the example uses react/jsx-runtime directly) or build it with React and the SDK as externals: Only those five bare specifiers are mapped. Anything else must be bundled into the plugin file or imported by full URL.

Registration: Export Use SDK_VERSION 1 SDK_FEATURES List of capability names, for feature detection registerPage(id, Component) Component receives { page } (its manifest entry). A zero-argument arrow function is treated as a lazy loader: registerPage('x', () => import('./X.js')) registerBlock(type, Component, options?) Component receives { node, page }; node is { type, props, children }. It also overrides a core block type of the same name. { fallback: true } registers a default that anything else overrides registerToolRenderer(toolName, Component) Chat tool call UI; receives assistant-ui tool part props (toolName, args, argsText, result, status, …) registerSlot(name, Component, options?) Add a component to a slot of the shell registerCommand(command) Add an entry to the command palette. Returns a function that removes it. Groups list before the pages, in registration order; the groups Preferences, Layout and Theme list after them registerView(pageId, render, cleanup?) A vanilla view for a legacy page (same as window.aiui.registerView in custom.js) registerSettingsSection(section) Add a section to the shell's settings dialog: { id, title, description?, order?, fields, load(), save(values) }, fields as in settings(). A save rejection whose error has body.fields shows those messages next to the fields. Returns a remover registerNavGroup(name, { order, folded }?) Declare the sidebar group your pages use, like nav_groups(). Returns a remover registerThemePreset({ id, label, light?, dark? }) Offer a seed-token theme preset, like themes(). Returns a remover registerLayout(id, meta, Frame \ loader) Add a layout (the frame around every page). getLayouts(), useLayout(), setLayout(id), provideLayoutData(kind, feed) and useLayoutData(kind) go with it. Returns a remover onActivate(fn) Run fn({ manifest }) once the app is ready getPage, getBlock, getSlot, getToolRenderers Registry lookups subscribe(fn), useRegistryVersion() React to later registrations Shell services and components: Export Use navigate(pageId, { replace }?) Go to a page of the app: navigate('logs') notify(message, options?) Show a toast. Options: type (info, success, warning, error), description, duration, id, action: { label, onClick } fetchJson(url, options?) fetch for JSON APIs. It sends the session's gateway token to same-origin URLs only, JSON-encodes a plain-object body (the method then defaults to POST), decodes the response, and rejects with an error carrying status, url and body on a non-2xx status useManifest() React hook returning the shell manifest (pages, plugins, site, layout) getPageId(), usePageId() The id of the page on screen ('' at /), read the way the shell's router reads the URL; the hook re-renders on navigation. Never parse location yourself useThemeMode() React hook returning 'light' or 'dark', updated when the viewer or the OS switches dismiss(id?) Close a toast raised with notify(message, { id }) (all toasts without an id) Markdown The shell's Markdown renderer: {text} Style with the theme's CSS variables (var(--foreground), var(--border), var(--primary), …). The shell's Tailwind build only contains the classes the shell itself uses, so Tailwind classes in a plugin may not exist.

Use the services instead of globals such as window.fetch or the history API. They work the same in every page kind and they are part of the SDK contract. A command that throws, or whose promise rejects, is reported as a toast. An onActivate hook that throws is logged and does not stop the other hooks.

A slot is a place in the shell that renders components from plugins. Slot Where Extra props header:actions The header bar, before search and the theme toggle. Not shown when the app hides the page header sidebar:footer The bottom of the sidebar, on desktop and in the phone menu collapsed page: :toolbar Above the body of page , for example page:logs:toolbar Every slot component receives { slot, pageId, page }: the slot name, the id of the page on screen and its manifest entry. Pass { id, order } so that several plugins can share a slot. id is the identity of your contribution (use the plugin name), and a lower order comes first (default 100). Registering the same id again replaces only that contribution. Without options, the call sets the slot's single default contribution and replaces an earlier one. This is the original behaviour. Each contribution renders inside its own error boundary. One that throws is removed and logged; the others and the shell stay. A slot nobody contributes to renders nothing.

A layout owns the frame of the app shell: the navigation, the session list, the top bar, side panels and the phone chrome. The page stays the page: every page renders inside every layout, in the outlet the shell hands the frame (ADR 0003). aiui ships six layouts (chat, what aiui run opens; chat-canvas, the app shell's default; plus workbench, command, guided and mission); the core's own frame is called classic. A plugin adds a layout with the same call the built-ins use. Which layout is on screen. The server's manifest lists the layouts it offers (layouts.available) and its default. The browser takes the first of: a ?layout= preview (kept for the tab, never saved), the viewer's own choice (the palette's "Switch layout: …" commands or Settings → Appearance, saved in this browser, only when the server allows a user choice), the server default, the classic frame. A layout the server does not offer is never chosen. Declare it in Python with a layouts() hook, which returns LayoutSpecs (or dicts with the same field names), like pages(): LayoutSpec field Meaning id Lower-case letters, digits and -, starting with a letter, at most 40 characters; classic is reserved title, description Shown in the picker (palette and Settings → Appearance) order Picker position (default 100; the built-ins use 10 to 50) module Required for a plugin layout: the ESM file that registers the frame. A relative path resolves into static_dir() (/_plugins/ /) and gets an SRI integrity hash, which the import map carries like a page module's css Optional stylesheet, resolved the same way (its hash is cssIntegrity in the manifest and on the ), added when the layout first loads home The page / opens while this layout is on screen primary Page ids of the primary nav, in order (at most 7 shown; YAML layout.primary wins) look Optional: the meta.look your frame registers (an id such as paper). When the layout is the server's default, the server sets from the first byte, so the look's fonts load instead of the Pro ones. It is not sent in the manifest The first plugin (or built-in) to declare an id keeps it; a later one is ignored with a warning, as is a malformed or classic id. On a remote or auth-enforced server an entry-point plugin's layouts follow the same default-deny rule as its pages. Configuration (which layouts are offered, the default) is in Layouts → Plugin layouts. Register the frame in the browser. The shell imports the module only when the layout is first rendered, never with the other plugin modules, so an inactive layout costs nothing. The module either calls registerLayout(id, meta, Frame)while it is evaluated (itsmeta then replaces the manifest's title and description) or default-exports the frame: The complete example is src/frontend/e2e/fixtures/layout-plugin/ (the suite e2e/specs/layouts-host.spec.ts runs it). What the frame receives (LayoutProps): Prop What it is Outlet The routed page, with its error boundary, toolbar slot and loading state. Render it once, inside your main pageId, page, fullBleed The page on screen, its manifest entry, and whether it asked for no padding (chat, iframes): then give the outlet the full height and no scroll nav primary (at most 7, the layout's own list), groups (every other page, by sidebar group, with folded), footer, activeId, go(pageId). Items carry id, title, href, active, navIcon, icon, group chrome siteTitle, siteLogo, openPalette({ query? }) (the one command palette, optionally prefilled), toggleColorMode(), Slot (the shell's slot host: ), mainId (give your main this id: the skip link and the palette focus it) viewport 'phone' (< 768 px), 'tablet' (< 1024 px) or 'desktop'; draw your phone frame from it layout id, available (the offered layouts), switchTo(id) useLayout() returns { id, meta } of the layout on screen (null for the classic frame), setLayout(id, { persist }?) switches live ('' or 'classic' is the classic frame), and getLayouts() lists the registered ones. meta.chat tells the chat page how to present itself in your frame (who draws the session list, the thread style, lazy regions such as aside, turnFooter and composerTool); see the ADR. meta.look names a look of the Pro tokens the frame paints with (the shell ships paper; DESIGN.md "Looks"). Frames read data such as the session list with useLayoutData('sessions'), which returns null while nothing provides it: render without it. The chat feed (builtin.chat) also acts on the open chat: prefill(text) fills the composer, send?(text) sends (optional: check for it, and fall back to prefill), cancel() stops the reply, and resolveApproval(id, approved, { always? }) decides a gate in the thread. Failure. A layout whose module fails to import, or whose frame throws, is replaced by the classic frame with one toast and an aiui:plugin-error event (detail.layout is its id). Other layouts are not affected. Keep a frame self-contained: import React and @aiui/sdk only, style with the theme's CSS variables, give icon-only buttons an aria-label, and make phone touch targets at least 44 px.

The SDK grows without a new major version, so SDK_VERSION stays 1. A named import of an export that an older shell lacks fails when the module loads. When a plugin must also run on older shells, use the default export and ask before you call a newer function: Feature names: pages, blocks, tool-renderers, slots, views, markdown, navigate, notify, fetch-json, manifest, commands, activate, slots.multi (the { id, order } options and the slot hosts), blocks.fallback, page-id (getPageId, usePageId), theme-mode (useThemeMode), notify.dismiss, settings (registerSettingsSection and the settings() hook), nav-groups (registerNavGroup, nav_groups()), theme-presets (registerThemePreset, themes()), layouts (registerLayout, getLayouts, useLayout, setLayout, manifest layouts), layout-data (provideLayoutData, useLayoutData) and slots.dispose (registerSlot returns a remover). A shell older than the services has no SDK_FEATURES.

@aiui/sdk is not an npm package: the shell provides it at runtime. Its types are in src/frontend/src/sdk/aiui-sdk.d.ts, the frontend build also writes dist/aiui-sdk.d.ts, and the installed package ships the same file at praisonaiui/templates/frontend/aiui-sdk.d.ts (find it with python -c "import praisonaiui, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(praisonaiui.__file__).parent / 'templates/frontend/aiui-sdk.d.ts')"). Copy the file into a plugin project and include it in tsconfig.json (or jsconfig.json with checkJs) to type-check the plugin. It depends on @types/react only.

Each module is imported once. If one fails to load (network error, syntax error, no component to register), the shell logs it, shows a toast, fires an aiui:plugin-error window event, and loads everything else. The page shows "unavailable" instead of crashing. A block that throws while rendering is replaced by an inline error; the rest of the page still renders.

A docs site can use a block whose type is named like a component (HelloCard): in a page of an aiui build site renders it, and the build publishes the plugin's static folder with the site (your own components).

A blocks page is data, not code: its endpoint returns a component tree and the shell renders it with built-in React blocks. Page handlers already written for the dashboard (aiui.register_page(handler=…) with aiui.ui.* helpers) render unchanged. The payload may be {"_components": [...]} (also components, blocks, or a bare list), and each item is a flat dict ({"type": "card", "title": …}) or {"type", "props", "children"}. A button with action and every form POST JSON to the action endpoint: page.actionEndpoint (set for aiui.register_page_action), else /action for plugin pages, else /api/pages/ /action. A response with a component list replaces the page; message is shown as a toast; error (or a non-2xx status) as an error toast. Resolution order for a block type: a block registered with registerBlock(type, C), a window.aiui.registerComponent renderer from custom.js, a block registered with { fallback: true } (the core blocks are registered this way), then the legacy dashboard renderer, so every existing _components type keeps working. Text is always rendered as text, never as HTML. Links and images only accept relative, http(s), mailto: and tel: URLs (images also data:image/*). Core block types: text, caption, header/heading, markdown_text/markdown, code_block/code, json_view/json, card, metric/stat, stat_group, progress_bar/progress, columns/grid, row, container, separator/divider, tabs, expander, accordion, table, key_value_list, list, badge, alert, callout, empty, spinner, skeleton, toast, image_display/image, link, button/action, button_group, form_action/form, text_input, number_input, date_input, time_input, textarea_input, select_input, checkbox_input, switch_input, radio_input, slider_input.

Installing a plugin means trusting it: its Python runs in the server process and its JavaScript runs in the page with no sandbox (use kind: iframe for untrusted content). Because any installed package, including a transitive dependency, can declare the entry point, the browser parts of entry-point plugins (pages, blocks, tool renderers and /_plugins/ /) and their HTTP routes (/api/plugins/ /*) are default-deny when the server requires auth or is reached from a non-loopback address. They are listed as disabled-by-default (and answer 404) until you enable the plugin by name. The plugin's Python code still runs (setup(), features()): to keep an installed package from being imported at all, put it in extensions.disabled. extensions: [hello] is shorthand for enabled. From Python: aiui.set_extensions(enabled=["hello"]) (it beats YAML). A plugin object registered with aiui.register_plugin(obj) was chosen by the app author and is always trusted: the enabled allowlist does not apply to it, so extensions: {enabled: [hello]} never switches your own plugin off. Only extensions.disabled (its name) does. AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 skips the entry-point group entirely (the test suite sets it).

Command Does aiui plugins list [--json] [--config aiui.yaml] The built-in records (builtin.: status ok or disabled, whether the host requires part of it, its pages), then installed plugins with version, status (ok, error, disabled, incompatible, disabled-by-default) and load error. --json puts the built-ins under builtins aiui plugins doctor [--config aiui.yaml] [--no-builtin] Loads each plugin and checks SDK version, static_dir(), every module file and its sha384 (pages, blocks, tool renderers, layouts), page kinds, every settings(), nav_groups(), themes() and layouts() entry, routes, CLI name clashes and page ids shadowed by built-in pages or other plugins. A page shadowed by a built-in names the builtin. to add to extensions.disabled; a builtin. name that matches no record is a warning. Exits 1 on any failure aiui …, aiui plugins … The plugin's own commands aiui --help and built-in commands never import plugins; discovery runs only when a command name is not a built-in one.

Symptom Check Page says "unavailable" aiui plugins doctor; the browser console shows the import error Plugin listed as disabled-by-default Remote or auth-enforced server: add it to extensions.enabled Invalid hook call The module bundled its own React: mark react and react/jsx-runtime external does not provide an export named … The shell is older than the SDK export the module imports: see feature detection A slot component does not appear Check the slot name, and that the page header or sidebar is not hidden by the app aiui shell not booted The module was loaded outside the app shell (style must be app) Integrity error after editing a file The manifest hashes the file on every request; hard-reload the page so the browser drops its cached copy

pages.t: How to Add a Feature to PraisonAIUI
pages.d: This guide explains every way a user can extend PraisonAIUI — and which approach fits your use case.

s.x: This guide explains every way a user can extend PraisonAIUI — and which approach fits your use case.

I want to add… Use Side Effort A new dashboard page @aiui.page() Server 5 lines A form that saves data aiui.form_action() + @aiui.register_page_action() Both 15 lines A brand-new UI component type window.aiui.registerComponent() + dict type Both 20 lines A page rendered entirely in the browser window.aiui.registerView() Client 10 lines Ship client-side JS from Python aiui.set_custom_js(path) Server 1 line A typed contract for a component aiui.register_component_schema(type, schema) Server 5 lines A custom theme aiui.register_theme() Server 1 line A new AI backend Subclass aiui.BaseProvider Server ~50 lines A whole new feature module (routes, state) Subclass BaseFeatureProtocol + register_feature() Server ~100 lines Persistence backend Subclass aiui.BaseDataStore Server ~50 lines

Goal: Show a new page in the sidebar with custom content. What happens: The page is registered in the server's page registry. It appears in the sidebar at /api/pages. When the user clicks it, the frontend fetches /api/pages/analytics/data. Your handler returns a dict; aiui.layout() wraps it in {"_components": [...]}. dashboard.js loops over _components and calls renderComponent(comp) on each. See Dashboard for the full @aiui.page() signature.

Goal: Let users submit data from the UI back to your Python code. What happens: The form renders with all inputs. On submit, the frontend POSTs to /api/pages/contact/action. The server invokes handle_contact(data) with the form values keyed by label. The returned dict is sent back to the browser as JSON. Note: Input labels become dict keys. Use distinct labels per input.
Goal: Add a new UI widget that doesn't exist in the 48 built-ins.

s.h: Step 1 — Python side: return a dict with your new type
s.x: If you stop here, the component renders as formatted JSON (graceful fallback).

s.h: Step 2 — Client side: register a renderer
s.x: Put this in a plugin.js file (or paste into DevTools Console): What happens: renderComponent(comp) checks COMPONENT_REGISTRY[comp.type] before the built-in switch. Your renderer takes priority and returns a DOM element.

Use aiui.set_custom_js(path) to ship client-side extensions directly from your app: The script runs after the plugin loader, so window.aiui.registerView and window.aiui.registerComponent are ready when it executes. No DevTools workaround needed.

Docs tags are driven by one table, DOCS_TAGS in src/frontend/src/markdown/docsTags.ts. A new tag is three small changes: An entry: the aiui-* element it becomes (el), the lower-case attributes the sanitizer keeps (attrs), an optional map from the author's attributes, and inline: true for a tag inside a sentence: Badge: { el: 'aiui-badge', attrs: ['color'], inline: true }. slots: ['caption'] renders an attribute as Markdown (an aiui-slot child; slots() in docs/DocsWidgets.tsx). Its React component under the same element name in DOCS_TAG_COMPONENTS (src/frontend/src/docs/DocsBlocks.tsx): those attributes are its props. The name in KNOWN_DOCS_TAGS (src/praisonaiui/compiler/docs_tags.py) so aiui build stops warning; tests/unit/test_docs_tags.py checks the lists. Placement (own line, one line, list items, self-closing, code left alone) and the sanitizer allowlist come with the table. Rebuild the bundle and document the tag in docs/features/writing-docs.md. A tag whose body is code is not a table entry: is listed in PASSTHROUGH and turned into a fence (codeBlockFence, docs/codeMeta.ts), so it renders through the same code frame (docs/DocsPre.tsx) as a fence. A new code option goes in parseCodeMeta and DocsPre. Content for the page's right-hand column is an aiui-panel block (, and / , which convertMkdocsBlocks turns into a panel around a code group): splitPanels (docs/panels.ts) moves every top-level one out of the article, and Content.tsx draws them in a sticky column in place of "On this page".

Goal: A page rendered entirely in the browser — no server round-trip on navigation. Still register a placeholder page in Python so it appears in the sidebar: What happens: registerView takes priority over the built-in + server-side rendering. Navigation calls your render(container) function. When the user navigates away, your cleanup() function runs.
See CSS Architecture for all variables.
See Providers.

Features live in praisonaiui/features/*.py and implement BaseFeatureProtocol: name and description are abstract on BaseFeatureProtocol; omitting either raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Optional hooks: cli_commands(), health() (kept cheap: it runs on every /api/features request) and on_config_reload() (drop what you cached from config.yaml; see Config Hot-Reload). See Protocol Architecture.

Clean separation — Python returns dicts, client renders DOM. You can mix and match server/client work per-feature. Graceful degradation — Unknown component types render as JSON (no crashes). Zero build step for Python users — No webpack/TS compile required for server-side pages. Single source of truth — Every feature has a protocol ABC. Hot-swap friendly — window.aiui.registerView/Component updates live without server restart.

Gap Resolution No aiui.set_custom_js(path) Implemented — serves the file at /custom.js and injects a tag after the plugin loader. Unit tests: tests/unit/test_custom_js.py (10 tests). form_action uses input labels as keys Implemented — every form input now accepts an optional name= kwarg that becomes the submit-key. Tests: tests/unit/test_form_input_names.py (18 tests). No typed Python ⇄ JS contract Implemented — aiui.register_component_schema(type, schema) + GET /api/components/schemas. Built-in schemas are auto-derived from ui.py signatures. Tests: tests/unit/test_component_schemas.py (9 tests). /api/features cold-start slow Mitigated — info() calls are parallelized via asyncio.gather. Warm calls are now instant; cold starts are dominated by LiteLLM import (out of scope). pygments 2.20 mkdocs build crash on providers.md Fixed — scripts/docs_hooks.py patches pymdownx.BlockHtmlFormatter.__init__ to coerce filename=None → "".

s.h: When NOT to use this approach
s.x: You need a full SPA with routing: Use the Next.js adapter or scaffold a React project with aiui init --frontend. Your UI needs TypeScript types: Use the TypeScript SDK (@praisonaiui/runtime). You need server-sent events beyond chat: Extend BaseFeatureProtocol with a WebSocket route.

[ ] Decide: is it a page, a component, or a backend module? [ ] Write the Python side first (returns a dict / routes). [ ] If you added a new component type: implement the JS renderer. [ ] Write a unit test (see tests/unit/test_form_action.py as an example). [ ] Add a runnable example under examples/python/. [ ] Update the docs under docs/features/ or docs/api/. [ ] Run mkdocs build --strict. [ ] Run pytest tests/unit -v.

@aiui.page() registers a page with the server dashboard.js fetches /api/pages and /ui-config.json once each on load, builds the sidebar automatically When a page is selected, it fetches /api/pages/{id}/data If the data contains _components, they render as real UI elements (cards, tables, etc.) The Chat page highlights code with highlight.js, which it loads from cdnjs.cloudflare.com the first time a reply contains a code block. A chat with no code never contacts the CDN; without internet access, code shows unhighlighted.
Pages without component layouts render as formatted JSON.

Pages are grouped in the sidebar by the group parameter: Parameter Type Required Description page_id str ✅ Unique identifier (URL-safe) title str ✅ Display name in sidebar icon str ❌ Emoji or icon character group str ❌ Sidebar group name description str ❌ Subtitle below the title
Build dashboard UIs entirely from Python — no HTML needed. 54 components are available across 7 categories. See the full Component API Reference for all components and parameters.
Arrange components side-by-side in a responsive grid:
Data tables with headers and rows:
Organize content in tabs or collapsible sections:
Wrap all components in a layout container: The layout() function adds the _components key that tells the frontend to render structured components instead of raw JSON.

When style is set to dashboard, 16 built-in pages are auto-registered from the feature system: Page Group Description 🤖 Agents Agent Configured AI agents ⚡ Skills Agent Agent tools and skills 🖥️ Nodes Agent Execution nodes 📊 Overview Control System overview 📡 Channels Control Messaging channels 📋 Sessions Control Active sessions 📻 Instances Control Connected instances 📈 Usage Control Token usage analytics ⏰ Cron Control Scheduled jobs 📋 Jobs Control Async job queue ✅ Approvals Control Pending approvals 🔌 API Control API documentation ⚙️ Config Settings Runtime configuration 🔐 Auth Settings Authentication 📜 Logs Settings Real-time log viewer 🐛 Debug Settings Debug information Custom pages added via @aiui.page() appear alongside built-in pages.
Each agent card on the Agents page includes a ▶ Run button. Clicking it navigates to the Chat page with that agent automatically pre-selected in the agent dropdown.

The Run button reads the agent name from its data-id attribute It pushes /chat?agent= to browser history and dispatches popstate The dashboard's popstate listener calls selectPage('chat'), loading the Chat view Chat's render() calls loadAgents(), then checks URLSearchParams for ?agent= If found, it sets the dropdown value and currentAgentName, then cleans the URL

Every dashboard includes a Test All Features link at the bottom of the sidebar. It auto-discovers all registered features from /api/features and tests each endpoint, showing pass/fail results in a grid.

Endpoint Method Description /api/pages GET List all registered pages /api/pages/{id}/data GET Get page handler response /api/features GET List all registered features /plugins/plugins.json GET Style-aware frontend plugin list
The dashboard provides a JavaScript API for registering custom views from the client side.

Register a custom view renderer for a page ID. Parameter Type Description pageId string Page ID to handle (e.g. "my-custom-page") renderFn async (container: HTMLElement) => void Async function that renders into the container cleanupFn () => void Optional cleanup function called when navigating away

When a page is selected, the dashboard resolves views in this order: Custom registered views — window.aiui.registerView() (highest priority) Built-in view modules — views/ .js for built-in pages, from /api/shell/manifest: a page whose source is builtin (kind legacy or native) loads .js. A page an app (register_page / @aiui.page), a plugin or a dashboard-plugin folder provides never gets a built-in view, even under a built-in id: it renders its own content, in the dashboard style too. When the manifest cannot be read, every page /api/pages lists is tried by the same file name. Generic JSON viewer — Falls back to rendering _components or raw JSON
Access the view registry directly:

A built-in page's view is the file named after its page id (views/ .js); there is no list in dashboard.js. Some of them: Page ID View Module Description chat chat.js Chat interface overview overview.js Dashboard overview agents agents.js Agent management sessions sessions.js Session management memory memory.js Memory viewer knowledge knowledge.js Knowledge base logs logs.js Real-time logs cron cron.js (re-exports schedules.js) Scheduled jobs config config.js Runtime config approvals approvals.js Tool approvals usage usage.js Token usage channels channels.js Messaging channels skills skills.js Agent skills nodes nodes.js Execution nodes guardrails guardrails.js Safety guardrails eval eval.js Agent evaluation telemetry telemetry.js Performance metrics traces traces.js Distributed tracing security security.js Security monitoring runs, cron, work and training are one-line modules that re-export run-recorder.js, schedules.js, work-hub.js and training-lab.js under the page id.

The dashboard picks its colour mode in this order: the viewer's choice, stored under aiui-theme-preference (light, dark or system; the Theme page and the app shell write the same key); the app's default: aiui.set_theme(dark_mode=True|False), else YAML site.theme.mode (light, dark, system) or site.theme.darkMode; the OS (prefers-color-scheme), when neither chose a mode (/ui-config.json then sends site.themeDefault: "system"). A change of the OS scheme or of the stored choice in another tab applies at once.
