pages.d: at what cost. It works for finished runs and for runs that are still going.

s.x: PraisonAI Replay shows a recorded agent run as a story: who did what, when, why, and at what cost. It works for finished runs and for runs that are still going.

s.h: Record a run, then open it
s.x: or from Python: Every recorded run is a file .jsonl in the traces folder. Replay reads it from the first of these that applies: $PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR $PRAISON_HOME/traces /traces, when a data directory is configured with $PRAISONAI_HOME (checked first) or $AIUI_DATA_DIR ~/.praison/traces, where the PraisonAI CLI writes runs The PraisonAI CLI always records to ~/.praison/traces. A server started with AIUI_DATA_DIR or PRAISONAI_HOME (Docker with AIUI_DATA_DIR=/data, for example) reads its own /traces instead and does not show those CLI runs. To show them, set PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR=~/.praison/traces. To open aiui on Replay yourself: /#/replay?run= works too. In a full dashboard, Replay is in the sidebar under Control.

s.h: Watch a run live: the Run button
s.x: For learning, demos and debugging, open a page with a Run button. Each click records a new run, and the page draws it as it happens: On the Map, each step and agent shows where the run is: dashed means not reached, blue (pulsing) means running now, green means done and red means failed. After a run, ▶ Play moves through it again one step at a time, and the map rewinds with it. One run goes at a time. Each run of a team starts its tasks afresh; an Agent keeps its chat history between runs.

s.h: Show progress inside your own app
s.x: create_replay_app() is the same view as a small ASGI app, without the dashboard. Mount it in any FastAPI or Starlette app: Then show one run, live, in your page, for example in an : URL Shows /replay/ The run list and the selected run /replay/?run= Only that run, no list. A run that has not started yet is waited for. replay_app(team) adds the Run box to the mounted page. Without the PraisonAI wrapper, pass any run(input, run_id) callable to praisonaiui.features.replay.create_replay_app; it must record the run under run_id. For a page you build yourself, the view is one module: render() options: base (where the API is mounted), run (show only this run), runner ({input, placeholder, ask} to show the Run box) and approve (false hides the approve and deny buttons; the embedded app has no approvals API, so answer approvals where your app asks for them). Anyone who can reach the mounted app can read the runs, and with a runner can start one. Keep it on localhost or behind your app's login. POST /api/replay/run only accepts Content-Type: application/json, so another website cannot start a run from a visitor's browser.

Part What it shows Runs Recorded runs, newest first. A run that is still being written has a Live badge. Timeline (default) One lane per agent, plus Manager and You. Time runs left to right. LLM calls and tool calls are blocks in their agent's lane. Arrows show hand-offs, delegation, routing and approval requests. Parallel branches get their own sub-lanes. A call or step repeated back to back is one block marked ×N. Tasks and steps run across the top. Map The team or flow as a graph, drawn from the graph recorded at the start of the run and fitted to the page (−, Fit and + zoom; drag to pan). Agents that took part but are not in the graph, for example after a hand-off to an agent outside the team, appear in an Outside the team group with their hand-offs. Older recordings without a graph get a "who talked to whom" map built from the events. Each node shows its state at the cursor: dashed means not reached, blue means running, green means done (×N when it ran more than once) and red means failed; the node the cursor is on has a bold outline. What happened One plain sentence per step, for example "Researcher asked web_search for 'solar sail facts' — 1.2 s, $0.002." Hovering or focusing a sentence highlights its block, and the other way round. Details Three tabs for the selected step. What happened: when, who, how long, cost, tokens, output. Why: only what the recording holds, such as the input given to a tool, the context passed in a hand-off and its reason, the manager's task snapshot, the route a step chose, and an approval's decision and where an automatic approval came from. Raw JSON: the events themselves. Cost & latency Adds a bar under each block (taller and darker means more cost, or more time) and per-agent totals in the lane labels. Shapes always carry meaning as well as colour: agents are circles, tools are rounded rectangles, you are a diamond and the manager is a square. In each lane, LLM calls sit on the top row and that agent's tool calls on a thinner row under them, so a long LLM call never hides its tools. Labels that do not fit end in "…"; hover or focus a block to see the whole label. The Theme menu follows your system's light or dark setting by default; choose Light or Dark to override it. On a phone the run list, timeline and steps stack in one column.

Replay opens at the end of the run, so you see everything. Move the cursor to replay it: anything after the cursor is drawn as an outline. Key Action ← → Previous / next step ↑ ↓ Previous / next step in the step list; previous / next node in the map Home / End First / last step Enter or Space Open the focused block or node ← → in the tabs Switch between What happened, Why and Raw JSON The scrubber under the timeline does the same with a mouse or touch, and ▶ Play steps through on its own. On a live run the cursor follows new events; if you step back, Jump to live takes you to the latest.

When an agent asks for approval and the run uses aiui's approval store, a Waiting for you card appears above the timeline: Approve or Deny, with an optional reason. Edit arguments… opens the arguments as JSON (taken from the server, not the redacted recording when the server has them). The JSON must be an object; mistakes are shown as you type. Approve with these arguments sends them as modified_args. These buttons call POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve and /deny. The agent waits until you answer, and is denied if nobody answers before the approval timeout.

s.h: Sharing a run as one file
s.x: praisonai replay export RUN --format html writes a single HTML file with the run and this viewer inside. It needs no server and no network. Approvals cannot be answered from an exported file.

Endpoint Returns GET /api/replay/runs [{run_id, session_id, path, started_at, ended_at?, status, kind, name, agents, events, cost_usd, live}], newest first GET /api/replay/runs/{id}/events?after_seq=N {events, graph, run}; after_seq keeps only events with a larger sequence_num; wait=1 answers {events: [], graph: null, run: null} instead of 404 for a run that has not started yet GET /api/replay/runs/{id}/stream Server-sent events: event: ctx per trace event (with id: = sequence_num), ping every 15 s, end once the run has finished and gone quiet for 2 s. Honours after_seq and Last-Event-ID. With a runner (create_replay_app(run=...)), POST /api/replay/run with {"input": "..."} starts a run and returns {run_id} (409 while one is going). Run ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$. Replay never writes trace files itself. Half-written last lines, unknown fields and unknown event types are skipped safely, and schema 1.0 recordings still open. The Traces page reads the same files: each run is a trace, and its spans come from matching start and end events.

pages.d: The Video Studio integrates PraisonAI Video as an external Node render engine. PraisonAIUI provides the dashboard shell, project files, YAML editor, job UX, and

s.x: The Video Studio integrates PraisonAI Video as an external Node render engine. PraisonAIUI provides the dashboard shell, project files, YAML editor, job UX, and HTTP proxying. The video engine handles parse, compile, lint, and MP4 export. Agents live in PraisonAI (Chat + tools), not inside the renderer.

Install PraisonAI Video CLI (praisonai-video) or run from the monorepo. Start the engine sidecar (recommended): Run the example app: Open the Video tab, create a project, edit scene.yaml, and use Lint / Render. For Chat to edit scenes, install praisonaiagents and set OPENAI_API_KEY. Optional: VIDEO_STUDIO_PROJECT_ID to target a specific project.

Variable Default Purpose VIDEO_ENGINE_URL http://127.0.0.1:3921 HTTP API base URL VIDEO_ENGINE_TOKEN (none) Optional Bearer token forwarded to the engine PRAISONAI_PROJECTS_DIR /projects when PRAISONAI_HOME or AIUI_DATA_DIR is set, else ~/.praisonai/projects On-disk project roots PRAISONAI_VIDEO_CLI (auto-detect) Path to praisonai-video or dist/cli.js for subprocess fallback VIDEO_STUDIO_PROJECT_ID (auto) Active project for agent tools when not passed explicitly PRAISONAI_MODEL gpt-4o-mini LLM for Video Editor agent in the example app Python API:

Each project is a directory containing: scene.yaml — scene definition scene.visual-test.yaml — optional visual regression spec .praisonai/project.json — metadata exports/ — rendered MP4 artefacts A project id is one folder name inside the projects folder: an id holding /, \ or .. is answered like an unknown project (404). A projectPath passed to /lint, /compile or /preview/start must be a project folder inside the projects folder, and the out name for /render must be a plain file name (400 otherwise).

All routes are under /api/video/: GET /health — sidecar status POST /lint, POST /compile — scene validation GET /preview-url, POST /preview/start — preview iframe URL (CLI; dashboard preview hidden) POST /render — async render job (type: video_render); optional backend (playwright | remotion) overrides scene.yaml render.backend GET /jobs/{id} — job status and download URL GET|POST /projects — list and create projects GET /projects/{id}/studio-refresh — poll after agent tool updates (refresh: true once) When the HTTP sidecar is unavailable, lint and render fall back to subprocess calls to praisonai-video.

The UI lives in dashboard-plugins/video-studio/ (built-in) or ~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins/video-studio/ for overrides. It uses window.aiui.sdk.fetchJSON. Frame-by-frame composition preview is hidden in the dashboard (SHOW_COMPOSITION_PREVIEW = false) until serve preview + seek are reliable. Use Render MP4 and the Your video player for output. Set the flag to true in index.js to re-enable the optional iframe scrubber. After agent tool writes, the editor reloads via video-studio:refresh (custom event) or polling studio-refresh.

Open Chat with the Video Editor agent (example app registers tools when praisonaiagents is installed). Agent calls video_get_scene / video_update_scene / video_lint_scene / video_render_project (same outcomes as UI buttons). Video Studio tab picks up changes automatically. Tools are defined in praisonaiui/video_agent_tools.py. For Cursor/Codex outside the UI, use the skill at skills/praisonai-video/SKILL.md in the PraisonAI Video repo.
Default is Playwright (no render: block in scene.yaml). Use Remotion only when required: video_render_project(backend="playwright") overrides YAML for one agent run. Hyperframes is deferred.

The text box edits the same scene.yaml the CLI uses. Equivalent commands (from the video repo): Lint editor text without saving: praisonai-video lint --stdin < scene.yaml See docs/integrations/praisonaiui.md in the PraisonAI Video repo for the full mapping table.

Agent UI host — extension patterns (registerView, plugins, @aiui.page) PraisonAI Video integration doc: docs/integrations/praisonaiui.md in the video repo PraisonAI Video skill: skills/praisonai-video/SKILL.md — YAML-first invariants for agents and CI

s.x: Bridge channel bot conversations (Slack, Discord, Telegram) into the Chat UI in real-time.

_attach_chat_bridge(channel_id, bot, platform) is called in _start_channel_bot() right before the bot task is launched: on_message hook — Captures incoming platform messages and broadcasts channel_message events with sender name, platform, and icon _session.chat() wrapper — Wraps the agent's chat method so responses are also broadcast as channel_response events Persistence — All messages saved to the datastore under session channel-{channel_id} for history on reload

Function Purpose _handleChannelMessage(data) Renders incoming platform user messages; auto-switches to channel session if on fresh chat _handleChannelResponse(data) Renders agent responses from channel bots _appendChannelMsg(role, data) Creates message DOM with platform badge, icon, sender name _markSessionUnread(sessionId) Adds unread dot to sidebar for inactive channel sessions

Every broadcast is dispatched via asyncio.create_task() — the original bot message handling is never blocked. Errors in broadcasting are logged at debug level and swallowed — the bot continues normally even with zero Chat UI clients connected.

pages.d: A running server can reload its runtime config file without a restart. The

s.x: A running server can reload its runtime config file without a restart. The server keeps the state of its CRUD features (agents, skills, channels and others) in one YAML file, config.yaml in the data directory (AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui/). The config watcher polls that file and, when it changes, reloads it. The watcher belongs to builtin.config: it is created with the server while that built-in is on, and does not start on its own.

The watcher reads the file every 3 seconds and compares its MD5 hash with the previous one. On a change it reloads the config store, then calls on_config_reload() on every registered feature. The agents, skills and channels features use it to re-read their part of the file; a disabled built-in is not registered, so a reload never imports it. A feature of your own that caches config-store data overrides the hook: A YAML site config (aiui.yaml) or app.py is not watched; for those see Hot Reload.
ConfigWatcher watches any file and calls your callbacks (sync or async, with no arguments) when it changes. start() must run inside an asyncio event loop, for example in an @aiui.on_startup handler:

Endpoint Method Description /api/config/watcher GET Watcher status /api/config/watcher/start POST Start the watcher /api/config/watcher/stop POST Stop the watcher /api/config/reload POST Reload on the next poll, even if the file did not change
YAML Configuration: config file format, including runtime persistence Protocols: the feature protocol system

pages.d: Knowledge / RAG search uses vector embeddings. The default embedding model is

s.x: Knowledge / RAG search uses vector embeddings. The default embedding model is text-embedding-3-small. Many OpenAI keys or projects do not have access to that model (organization tier, model allowlist, or regional restrictions), which caused knowledge search to silently degrade to local substring matching. PraisonAIUI now makes this failure mode configurable and observable.
The knowledge store embeds through praisonaiagents, whose adapters read OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL: The /v1/embeddings endpoint reads AIUI_EMBEDDING_MODEL first, then OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL.

The OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint tries the requested (or default) model first, then each model in the fallback chain if the primary returns a model_not_found / 403 access error: If every candidate is inaccessible, the endpoint returns 503 with an actionable model_not_found error instead of a generic 500.

The praisonaiagents adapters do not raise when an embedding fails: search returns no hits and a write returns a failed result. So the store embeds one word when it starts, and reads the result of every write. While embeddings are unavailable, GET /api/knowledge/status says so: POST /api/knowledge still keeps the entry (in memory, searchable by keyword) but no longer claims it was saved: the response has "persisted": false, "sdk_synced": false and the same warning. A file upload while embeddings are down is indexed as text in memory when it is a text file, with that warning as knowledge_warning; other files are refused with it. POST /api/knowledge/search indicates whether results came from vector search or a degraded local fallback: search_mode is vector only when the hits came from the vector store; a keyword match on a healthy store is local. A dashboard can show a warning banner whenever search_mode == "fallback" or embedding.available == false.

Model Notes text-embedding-3-small Default — best cost/quality when available text-embedding-3-large Higher quality — may also be restricted text-embedding-ada-002 Legacy — widely available on older projects

pages.d: Every block a docs page can use, with its Markdown and a live example, and the look the site draws them in.

s.x: A docs site is a folder of Markdown and one YAML file. This page lists every block a page can use: the Markdown you write, then the block as this site draws it. Pages that aiui build publishes also exist as plain Markdown (/docs/ .md, components converted) and in llms.txt, so assistants read the same content (AI-ready docs).

site.theme.preset picks the colours. paper is the look of this site: warm paper, a navy accent, serif titles, 17px text on a 1.7 line height and a measure of about 75 characters. mode: system follows the reader's OS. The other presets and what each changes are in Theming.

YAML at the top of a page sets its title in the sidebar, the browser tab and search results, and its description for search engines and llms.txt. Every key is optional, and the common MDX page metadata keys work as they are. Key Type What it does title string The page title: the # heading when the body has none, the browser tab, search, llms.txt. Default: the first # heading, else the file name. description string Shown under the title (unless the first paragraph already says it), and the meta description, llms.txt and search snippet. Default: the first paragraph, for those but not shown again. sidebarTitle (or nav_title) string A shorter label in the sidebar. icon string Before the sidebar label: a lucide name (rocket, terminal, book-open, …), an emoji, or an image URL (https://… or /icons/x.svg). tag string A badge after the sidebar label, such as NEW or BETA. deprecated true/false true: a Deprecated badge, the label struck through, and a notice above the page. mode string wide: no "On this page", a wider column. center: no sidebar either. custom: only the article, full width (no breadcrumb, footer or pager). frame: custom with the sidebar. assistant: the page's text, then Ask AI under it. url string An https:// URL makes the page a sidebar link that opens that site in a new tab. The page itself is not published (no route, sitemap, llms.txt or search entry). hideFooterPagination true/false true: no previous / next links under the page. noAnchor true/false true: no copy-link icon on the page's headings. order number Position inside its folder (default: a number prefix such as 01-). hidden true/false Routable, but not in the sidebar, pager or indexes (Navigation). noindex true/false Tells search engines not to index the page (and leaves it out of the sitemap). searchable true/false false leaves the page out of the site's own search. keywords list of words, or one comma-separated string Extra search terms, matched but never shown; also the keywords meta tag and JSON-LD. canonical string The page's canonical URL (and og:url), for a page whose original lives elsewhere. robots string The robots meta, such as noindex, nofollow; a value with noindex also leaves the page out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search. og:*, twitter:*, article:* string That head tag for this page (quote the key: 'og:image': /images/card.png); see SEO. boost number Search ranking weight (2 ranks the page higher). openapi string "GET /users", "spec.yaml POST /users" or "webhook name": the page shows that operation, its endpoint bar, Try it, fields and examples around your text (OpenAPI). api string "POST /v1/users": an endpoint page without a spec, Try it from the page's s (OpenAPI). playground string interactive, simple, none or auth: the Try-it display of an openapi: or api: page; site-wide: api.playground.display (OpenAPI). timestamp true/false Turns the "Last updated" date off or on for this page (see Page footer). lastUpdatedDate date (2026-05-01) The "Last updated" date, instead of the last commit's. related list of pages or URLs, or false The "Related pages" under this page, instead of the suggested ones; false shows none (Related pages). pageActions list of page actions, or false This page's page actions menu, in order, instead of the site's; false shows none (Page actions). rss true/false true on a changelog page: the build writes its entries as an RSS feed at /rss.xml and links it (Changelog). public true/false On a site with sign-in: true opens the page to everyone, false keeps it behind sign-in when a public pattern would open it. groups list of group names, or one name On a site with sign-in: only readers in one of these groups can read the page; to everyone else it does not exist. layout, hero, features The docs home page (Home page layout). any other key string, number or true/false Custom data, such as product: cloud: a data-fm-product="cloud" attribute on the article (for CSS) and meta in the aiui:content-loaded event (for custom JS). The front matter never shows on the page as text. aiui validate checks these types and reports the line of a wrong one (hidden: "yes" is a string, so the page would stay in the sidebar), front matter that is not valid YAML, images without alt text, two files that publish the same page, two sidebar entries with the same title in one folder, headings that skip a level, empty pages and a theme.accent with too little contrast. Each finding names file:line and how to fix it; --strict makes them errors for CI. See the codes. A nav group can also list a link among its pages:

## and ### headings build the "On this page" list beside the article (above it on narrow screens), which follows the reader as they scroll. Every heading gets an id from its text, so writing-docs#callouts links straight to a section, and a link with a section opens the page scrolled to it. Hover a heading (on a phone, look beside it) for its link icon: one click puts the section in the address bar and copies its URL. Keep one # title per page; the paragraph right under it is the lede and reads larger. To pin an anchor that survives a reworded title, end the heading with {#id}: ## Install the CLI {#install} links as #install, the search index uses the same id, and the braces never show.

Use a callout for what a reader must not miss. Each tag sets the colour and the icon: and (blue), and (green), (amber), (red). A title is optional. A tag can sit on lines of its own or share one with its text: Saved. works (see Component tags). aiui serve serves the output of aiui build. mode: system follows the reader's light or dark setting. The site rebuilt without warnings. Plugins built for SDK 1 keep working; check aiui plugins doctor after an upgrade. Never put an API key in aiui.yaml; it ships with the site. Pages written for MkDocs keep working: !!! note "Title" with an indented body draws the same callout (note, info, tip, success, warning, danger and the other MkDocs types).

For a procedure the reader follows in order. Each step gets a number on a rail; its body is ordinary Markdown, code blocks included. Reply to every message with @aiui.reply. aiui run app.py, then open the address it prints. hides detail the reader opens on demand: long output, edge cases, FAQs. defaultOpen starts it open. Wrap several in to stack them as one list. The entry files keep fixed names; aiui build adds a content hash to their URLs, so a hard refresh is never needed. Yes. See Deploy to GitHub Pages. description="…" adds a line under the title, icon="code" an icon before it, and id="…" an anchor: writing-docs#accordion-faq opens the page with that accordion open. A link to a heading inside a closed accordion opens it too. Link to #accordion-faq; the accordion opens and scrolls into view. with one per choice: the same task in different tools, languages or operating systems. Arrow keys move between tabs. Run export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... before aiui run. Run setx OPENAI_API_KEY sk-..., then open a new terminal. Tabs sync by title: pick "Windows" once and every set of tabs on the page with a "Windows" tab shows it, code groups included. The pick is remembered, so the next page opens on it as well, and "On this page" lists only the headings of the tabs shown. Options: Option What it does sync={false} on This set keeps its own selection. defaultTabIndex={1} on The tab shown first (counted from 0) until the reader picks one. borderBottom on A rule under the tab content, to set it apart from the text below. icon="terminal" on An icon before the title. id="…" on An anchor: #windows-setup in the URL opens that tab. export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... setx OPENAI_API_KEY sk-... Tabs that each hold one code block draw as a code group (below). The MkDocs form, consecutive === "Label" blocks with indented bodies, works too.

After the language, name the file with title="…" (or just the name) and pick lines to highlight with {…}: single lines and ranges, separated by commas. Without title=, every word after the language up to the first option is the title: python Reply handler {3-4} shows "Reply handler". highlight={3-4}, hl_lines="3 4" and highlight="3-4" work too, so fences written for MkDocs or in MDX syntax carry over.

The name is that link, and opening it opens the around the field. id="…" sets the link yourself. The user to fetch. Only users with these tags. The user. Display name. Use emails. folds nested properties behind "Show …" (default "Show properties"); defaultOpen starts it open. Nest them as deep as the object goes.

and hold code fences, labelled like a code group (several fences become tabs; dropdown picks one from a menu instead). Write a block once and use it on many pages. Put it in docs/snippets/ (that folder is never published as pages) and include it where it should appear: docs/snippets/install.md, where {pkg} takes the value passed in: Site-wide values go in one key of aiui.yaml, and {{name}} in any page or snippet becomes the value, in text, code and front matter (title, description): Snippets nest, and take any number of props. A missing snippet, a path outside the project folder, or a snippet that includes itself fails the build (7008), and aiui validate names each {{name}} that has no value (7007). To publish a docs folder that is really called snippets, add "!snippets" to content.docs.exclude.

A changelog page is a list of entries, newest first. Add rss: true and readers can subscribe: label (a date or version) is the entry's section heading: it gets an anchor (#2026-11-18, or id="…"), a copy-link icon, a line in "On this page" and its own result in site search. From 768px wide it sits in a left column that stays in view while the entry scrolls. description shows under the label, tags ({["A", "B"]} or "A, B") as chips. A page with tagged entries gets a tag filter above the first entry. Choosing tags shows the entries with any of them and keeps the choice in the address (?tags=API,Fix), so a filtered view is a link you can share. rss: true: aiui build writes /rss.xml (RSS 2.0, one item per entry: the label and description as its title, the entry's anchor as its link, its tags as categories and its body as HTML; a label that is a date, such as 2026-11-18 or November 18, 2026, becomes its date). The page's head gets , so browsers and feed readers find it, and the filter row shows an "RSS feed" link. Links are absolute when the site URL is known (seo.siteUrl or a CNAME file), base path included. The entries are ## label sections in the page's .md and llms-full.txt.

Tags work the way MDX reads them: on lines of their own, on one line with their text, inside a list item (indent the tag with the item's text), or self-closing (). Attributes take quotes or braces (cols={3}) and may run over several lines. A body indented under its tag is text, not code, as in MDX. A tag the site does not know (say ) keeps its text as plain Markdown, and aiui build and aiui validate name it: Warning: docs/guide.md:12: is not a docs component; its content shows as plain Markdown. / for="agents" shows its content only on the page / only to agents (AI-ready docs).

Write a React component once and use it on any page as a tag. Point the site at one ES module beside aiui.yaml: The module registers each component with registerBlock from @aiui/sdk, or exports it under the tag's name. It imports React and the SDK as bare names: the build maps them to the page's own copies, so no bundler is needed for plain JS, and hooks work. Props. A quoted attribute is a string; {…} is a value: a number, true or false, an array or an object ({{ calls: 10 }}, JSON or JS-style); a bare attribute () is true. The component gets them as props, and as node.props like any block. Children. The tag's body is Markdown, rendered and passed as children. A self-closing tag that shares its line with text sits inside the sentence. Loading. The module loads only on a page that uses one of its tags, after the page has painted; until then, and if the module fails or the component throws, the page shows the tag's body. A built-in tag name (, ) keeps its built-in meaning. Tags. The build finds them in the module (registerBlock('Name' and export function Name). A minified bundle hides them: list them with site.components: {src: ./components/index.js, tags: [Counter, Price]}. Declared tags are not reported as unknown; a missing module, or one with no tag the build can find, is a 7021 warning. Security. The module is your site's own code, served from the site (script-src 'self'); the build adds the import map's hash to the Content-Security-Policy. Only same-site modules load. In the .md copy for agents the tag's body stays and the tag goes. Styles. Use the theme's CSS variables (var(--primary)), or add a stylesheet with site.customCss. An installed UI plugin whose blocks() include a type named like a component (HelloCard) provides that tag too, with no config: when a page uses a tag nothing else knows, the build asks the plugins and publishes the plugin's static folder with the site.
and never show on the page, in search or in llms-full.txt; inside a code block they stay as written.

Show one image in light mode and another in dark mode. They follow the site's theme toggle, not only the system setting. Any of these forms works, so the same Markdown also reads well on GitHub:

Add className (or class) to a component tag or to raw HTML to adjust one block: its spacing, width, text, colour or layout. The classes use the site's theme tokens, so they follow light and dark mode and any theme preset: Only these classes work ({a,b} means either). Any other class is dropped, and aiui validate and aiui build name it with its file and line, with the nearest allowed class (finding 7022). Nothing on a page can move the site's header, sidebar or search, or cover them, so there is no fixed, absolute, z-* or arbitrary [...] value. A mermaid fence draws a diagram (loaded only on pages that have one), and $$ … $$ typesets math.

Readers press ⌘ K ( Ctrl K ) or the search field. Search covers page titles, every ## and ### heading and all the text under it, and a result opens the page at its section with the words marked. It forgives typing: plurals and verb forms match ("themes", "theming"), a word matches as you type it ("inst"), one typo in a longer word still matches, and question words drop out ("how do I deploy"). Titles rank first, then headings, then text, each BM25 style. While the dialog is open the address bar carries the query, so a link such as /docs?q=api+keys opens search filled in. On a site with header tabs (Navigation), chips filter results by tab: search starts in the reader's tab, and one row offers the other tabs' results when it has none. A navigation group's boost: applies to its pages (a page's own wins). Site settings (search.provider is ignored and aiui validate says so): aiui build writes the index (search-index.json, up to 6,000 characters per section) and the same index in parts under search-index/, so the dialog downloads only what a query needs: Part Holds Fetched search-index/meta.json each page's path, keywords, boost and section headings with their word counts, and the sorted list of every word the first time a reader opens search search-index/ /w .json for a run of those words, the sections each appears in and how often when a query has a word in that run (by stem, prefix or one typo) search-index/ /p .json page i's section text when the page is in the results, for its snippets Ranking is the same as over the whole file: BM25, stems, prefixes, typos, keywords, boost and the tab chips. On this repository's 99 searchable pages the first open downloads 35 KB gzipped instead of 181 KB, and a first query about 13 KB more. is a hash of the index, so a page cached from an older deploy never mixes parts; a missing part, or a site built before the parts existed, makes the dialog read search-index.json whole, which every other reader (the MCP server, Ask AI, older pages) still uses. A site with sign-in gets no parts: its search-index.json is cut per reader.

Link to another page by its file: Theming. The build turns it into the page's URL, so links work on GitHub and on the site. A folder's README.md or index.md is served at the folder's URL (protocols/adp/README.md at /docs/protocols/adp), and a number prefix is dropped (adr/0003-selectable-layouts.md at /docs/adr/selectable-layouts). List such a page in the nav by its file path (protocols/adp/README); the header still opens the tab that lists it.

aiui docs check-links finds every link that leads nowhere, before readers do: It checks Markdown links and images, reference links, href and src on components and HTML (, , ), the docs home hero and features links, the nav page entries and the navbar and footer links in the YAML. A #section link is checked against the ids the site gives its headings (## The aiui CLI is #the-aiui-cli). Links in code are skipped. Paths outside the docs (app routes such as /chat) are not judged. --external also requests every http(s) URL, and --json prints the result for scripts. The exit code is 1 when a link is broken, so a CI step needs one line. aiui validate --strict and aiui build --strict fail on broken links too; without --strict they print them as warnings.

Above every page's title, Copy page copies the page's Markdown, ready to paste into an assistant. Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac) does the same when nothing is selected and the cursor is not in a text field. Its menu also has: Action Id What it does Copy page copy The page's agent-ready Markdown on the clipboard View as Markdown view Opens /docs/ .md, the page as plain Markdown for assistants Download as PDF pdf The browser's Print dialog; pick Save as PDF Listen to page listen The browser reads the article aloud, with pause and stop; hidden where the browser has no speech Open in ChatGPT chatgpt A new ChatGPT chat that reads the page and takes questions Open in Claude claude The same, in Claude Copy MCP server URL, Connect to Cursor / VS Code mcp On a site aiui serve runs (MCP server) Nothing to configure: they use the Markdown aiui build already publishes. Try it on this page. To pick and order the actions, list them. Besides the ids above there are perplexity, grok, google (Google AI Mode), copilot, mistral (Le Chat) and cursor, and links of your own: In href, {url} is the page's address, {md} its Markdown, {title} its title and {prompt} the "read this page" prompt the assistants get, each URL-encoded. pageActions: false turns the menu off. One page can have its own list, or none, in its front matter:

A printed page (Download as PDF, or the browser's own Print, Ctrl+P / ⌘P) is the article alone, on light paper even when the reader uses dark mode: The header, sidebar, "On this page", page actions, previous / next, footer and feedback are left out. Breadcrumbs and "Last updated" stay. Everything a click would reveal is shown: accordions, field lists and file trees open, every tab of and prints under its own title, and expandable code blocks print every line. Code wraps instead of running off the page; code blocks, callouts, cards, steps, table rows and images are not split across pages. External links print their address after the link text: link (https://example.com/docs). Site chrome added by custom JS (site.customJs) or a plugin can opt out of print with data-print="hide". The PDF comes from the reader's browser: no build step, no server-side renderer.

Under each page: "Was this page helpful?" (on by default, see Page feedback) and two optional parts, turned on in aiui.yaml: Edit this page links to pattern with :path replaced by the page's file under the docs folder (getting-started/quickstart.md). Last updated is the date of the last commit that changed the page. aiui build reads it from git. In a shallow clone, pages changed inside the cloned history keep their date; older ones get none rather than the clone's date. In GitHub Actions, check out with fetch-depth: 0 to date every page. A page's lastUpdatedDate: 2026-05-01 sets the date by hand, and timestamp: false (or true) turns it off (or on) for that page alone. Was this page helpful? keeps the vote (next section). With issues, a "No" also offers a new issue there with the page's title and address filled in. The footer of this page shows all three.

Under each page, "Related pages" lists the three pages closest to it. Nothing to configure: aiui build compares the words of every page (title, keywords, description and headings count most, then the text) and favours pages in the same sidebar group. Hidden, noindex and searchable: false pages and the home page are never suggested. The list is part of docs-nav.json, so it works on any static host and offline, and each page's agent-ready .md ends with it too. Pick the list for a page in its front matter, or turn it off: related: false shows none on that page. Site-wide, content.docs.related: 5 shows five (at most 10) and content.docs.related: false only the lists pages set themselves. aiui validate reports a target that is no page (7013). The block is left out when the page prints.

Nothing to configure: under aiui serve and aiui dev every docs page asks "Was this page helpful?". A vote is stored at once; the reader can then add a comment (up to 1,000 characters), which joins that vote. Read them with: Votes are lines of docs-feedback/feedback.jsonl in the data directory ($AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui). POST /api/docs/feedback takes same-origin requests only (plus --cors-origins, AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), checks the Host header, takes 4 KiB and 20 posts a minute per client, and stops at 20 MB. Nothing is readable over HTTP; the export is the CLI. Agents report through the docs MCP server's submit_feedback tool into the same store and limits (MCP server). A code flag is a -1 vote with kind: "code" and block, the block's index on the page, plus an optional comment. aiui serve and aiui dev say in the ui-config.json they serve where they keep votes (docsFeedback.url); a static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) serves the built file, which has no such entry, so with no endpoint the page sends no request at all and the question is shown only if issues is set. endpoint receives the vote as JSON, sent as text/plain when it is on another origin so the browser makes no preflight request: {"id", "path", "value", "kind", "block", "comment"}. A comment arrives as a second post with the same id. Every vote, wherever it goes, also fires a browser event your own script can send to analytics:

s.x: File What it holds /llms.txt every page with its description, by nav group (llmstxt.org) /llms-full.txt every page's agent-ready Markdown in one file /docs/ .md one page's agent-ready Markdown (AI-ready docs) /docs/ .source.md the page source the site renders /search-index.json headings and text per page, for the site's own search /search-index/ the same index in parts, fetched as a query needs them (Search) /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt for search engines Each page's HTML also carries that page's source (a JSON script, id="aiui-initial-doc"), so the first visit renders without a second request for it. Pages over 200 KB of Markdown are fetched as before. It also carries docs-nav.json and route-manifest.json (id="aiui-boot-data", each up to 100 KB; not the navigation of a site with sign-in) and preloads ui-config.json; see Deploy to GitHub Pages → How pages load.

The path is relative to the config file.

include patterns are globs relative to dir. An exclude pattern matches the path relative to dir, a folder holding it (drafts, drafts/) or, with no /, any file or folder name (*.tmp). A leading / anchors it to dir; !pattern brings back a file an earlier pattern left out. Excluded files are not published at all: aiui build copies neither the pages nor the images next to them, and it lists what it left out. The same patterns can live in an .aiuiignore file next to aiui.yaml, one per line (# starts a comment); they add to exclude:

index.md and README.md (any case) are the page of their folder: guides/index.md is served at /docs/guides. indexFiles is accepted in the config, but other file names are not treated as index pages yet.

Field Description title Page title in the navigation; default: the first # heading, then the slug order Sort order within the folder (lower first); 0 or missing falls back to a number prefix description Meta description; default: the first paragraph of 20 or more characters, cut at 160 noindex true adds robots: noindex, nofollow and leaves the page out of the sitemap layout home on docs/index.md draws the home page layout The frontmatter block is not shown on the page.

Frontmatter layout: home on the docs home page (docs/index.md) puts a hero and a feature grid above the page's own Markdown, the way VitePress does: The hero image keeps a 16:10 box until the file arrives, so nothing below it jumps as it loads; once loaded it takes the image's own shape. Screenshots at 16:10 (1600 × 1000, say) never move the page. Only the image for the colour mode on screen downloads at first; the other one waits until the reader switches. aiui build adds for the hero to the home page's HTML, so the download starts with the page instead of after the app has drawn the hero. With site.theme.mode: system (or no mode) each image gets the matching prefers-color-scheme media query; a fixed light or dark preloads only that image. A reader whose saved light/dark choice differs from the system setting downloads both. Links and images resolve against the home page like Markdown links, and links to other sites open in a new tab. icon is one of message-square, panels-top-left, layout-dashboard, book-open, plug, shield-check, code, terminal, bot, zap, rocket and palette (lucide line icons); any other name shows no icon. Up to 4 actions and 12 features are kept. Every value is plain text. Only the docs home page reads layout: home; on other pages it does nothing.

A leading number gives the order when the frontmatter sets none, and the NN- prefix is stripped from the URL. Only a prefix at the start of a folder or file name counts: digits inside a name stay (ui-reset-2026-11.md is served at /docs/ui-reset-2026-11). A link that names the file (01-introduction.md) opens the page at its URL.
