s.x: aiui build turns the docs folder into the sidebar (docs-nav.json). YAML navigation.tabs then splits that sidebar into tabs.

Each folder becomes a section and each Markdown file an entry: Inside a folder, pages sort by frontmatter order, then by file name (see Content Sources). A folder's section takes the title of its index.md (or another indexFiles name) and links to it; a folder without one is titled with its name, title-cased. Link a folder's index page by the folder (notes/). An entry's title is the frontmatter title, else the first # heading. The generated tree looks like this: content.docs.nav.mode picks between this generated sidebar (auto, the default) and one you list in YAML (below). Options for the generated sidebar: Frontmatter order wins over sort. A folder's index page is its section's own page (the label links there).
navigation.pages and navigation.groups list the sidebar in order, with no tab or nav.mode needed: These group keys work in tab groups too.

Every group folds: click its label, or the chevron beside a label that links to a page. Each reader's choice is remembered across reloads and visits. The group holding the current page always opens. interaction.drilldown: true makes a group label with no page of its own open the group's first page.

directory: card (a card grid) or accordion (a row per page) lists a group's pages with their descriptions at the end of the group's page. A group with no root gets a generated page at /docs/ (Guides is /docs/guides), or uses the page already there. content.docs.nav.directory does this for every folder of the generated sidebar.

The line above a page title is the page's group. styling.eyebrows: breadcrumbs shows every group above it, each with a page of its own linked. Every page's HTML carries a schema.org BreadcrumbList for search engines.

aiui validate and aiui build warn about a listed page name that matches no page (code 2101, with the closest name; aiui validate --strict fails), a tab, anchor or dropdown with nothing to open (2102) and about keys that do nothing yet (1004: nav.maxDepth, i18n.fallbackLocale, translationsDir).

With content.docs.nav.mode: manual the sidebar comes from the tab groups: each group is a section holding the pages it lists, in that order, whatever folder they live in. A pages entry may itself be a group, which nests a section (one level is the usual choice). A page is named by its URL path under the docs base (features/layouts), its file path without .md (adr/0001-replay-view, adr/index) or index for the home page. A name that matches no page is skipped (and reported, see Checks). A page listed twice appears once, where it is first listed. Frontmatter nav_title gives a page a shorter sidebar title than its heading (nav_title: CLI on a page titled "CLI API Reference"). Pages no group lists are still built and reachable by URL, but hidden: not in any sidebar, search, sitemap.xml or llms.txt (see Hidden pages). Leave a page out of the site with content.docs.exclude (see Content Sources). hidden: true on a group hides its pages the same way; on a tab it also drops the tab from the header. boost: 2 on a group ranks its pages higher in site search (0.1 to 10; a page's own boost wins; see Search). With tabs, search results can be filtered by tab. The active tab is the one whose groups list the page; for a page no group lists, the folder prefix decides as in auto mode, then the first tab.

A group's icon: in the navigation YAML, or a page's frontmatter icon:, puts a 16px line icon before its title in the sidebar and the phone drawer. Any lucide icon name (flag, house, or an old name such as home), an emoji (icon: "🚀") or an image URL (https://… or /icons/x.svg). See Icons. aiui validate warns (7009) about a name that is not an icon. Page icons work in both modes; group icons need mode: manual.

navigation.tabs groups the sidebar sections into tabs in the header. A section belongs to the first group whose group name matches its title, whose prefix is its folder, or whose pages list one of its pages. The sidebar shows only the active tab's sections, in the order of its groups; the active tab follows the URL. A section that no group of any tab claims is not shown while tabs are set. In manual mode the groups are the sections, so each one belongs to its tab. Clicking a tab opens its first page; the active tab follows the page you are on. On phones the tabs move into the navigation drawer, where tapping one shows its sidebar without leaving the page.

Key On Does icon tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown an icon before the name href tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown a link instead of a sidebar (url still works on a tab) pages tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown pages listed straight in it (before its groups) groups tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown its sidebar sections hidden tab, menu item, anchor, dropdown leaves the header and sidebar; its pages stay routable menu tab items, each with its own sidebar or href; the tab opens the list description menu item, dropdown a second line under the name tabs dropdown header tabs shown while that dropdown is open

Anchors are links pinned at the top of the sidebar on every page. An anchor with href links out; one with pages or groups opens its own sidebar, like a tab. navigation.global.anchors takes the same entries and lists them first.

navigation.dropdowns (also spelled products, with product: names) puts a switcher at the top of the sidebar. Each entry opens its own sidebar, or brings its own header tabs, so one site can hold several products. Tabs, menu items, anchors and dropdowns share one rule: each part with pages or groups gets its own sidebar, and the page you are on decides which one is open. aiui validate warns about one with no pages, groups or href (code 2102) and about a listed page that does not exist (2101).

navigation.versions publishes several versions of the docs side by side. The default version is served at the docs root; every other version comes from its own folder, with no page list needed: Key Meaning version the name in the switcher; also the folder and URL segment (v1, 2.x) default the version at the docs root (default: the first one) tag a badge after the name (Latest, Beta, Deprecated), up to 24 characters index true keeps an older version in the sitemap and llms.txt (default: only the default version) groups, pages, tabs the version's own sidebar and header tabs (with nav.mode: manual); without them the folder's pages form the sidebar hidden left out of the switcher; its pages stay routable A switcher at the top of the sidebar (and of the phone drawer) names the open version. Picking another one opens the same page in it (/docs/guide/setup and /docs/v1/guide/setup), or that version's first page when it has no such page. The sidebar, the pager, the header tabs and the site search show the open version only; the top-level tabs and dropdowns belong to the default version, and anchors show in every version. An older version's page names the default version's same page as its canonical URL and carries robots: noindex, so search engines send readers to the current docs; its pages stay out of sitemap.xml and llms.txt unless the version sets index: true. A page's own canonical or robots front matter wins. aiui validate reports two versions with one name, more than one default, and a version that lists a page from another version's folder (code 7018).

navigation.languages publishes translated docs. The default language is served at the docs root; every other one comes from its own folder, named by its code, with no page list needed: Key Meaning language the language code (fr, pt-BR); also the folder and URL segment label the name in the switcher (default: the language's own name, Français) default the language at the docs root (default: the first one) index true lists its pages in llms.txt too (default: only the default language) groups, pages its own sidebar (with nav.mode: manual); without them its folder's pages form the sidebar hidden left out of the switcher and the translation links; its pages stay routable A switcher in the header (an icon on phones) opens the same page in the other language (/docs/guide/setup and /docs/fr/guide/setup), or that language's first page when the page is not translated yet. The sidebar, the pager and the site search show the open language only. The reader's pick is remembered, and on a first visit to the docs home the reader's browser language (fr-CA finds fr) opens its translation; crawlers and other automated browsers always get the default language. navigation.languageRedirect: false turns that redirect off. Every page carries and, when it has translations, a for each (with x-default on the default language's page); sitemap.xml lists the same alternates. llms.txt and llms-full.txt hold the default language, and each other language gets its own llms- .txt. With navigation.versions too, a language folder sits inside its version's folder: docs/v1/fr/ is served at /docs/v1/fr/..., and both switchers keep the page. aiui validate reports two languages with one code, more than one default, and a version folder inside a language folder such as docs/fr/v1/ (code 7020).

navbar adds links and one primary button to the header. On phones they move into the navigation drawer. A link with type and no label shows the network's mark alone, named for screen readers. Links to another site open in a new tab. The star count needs no setup: the browser asks the public GitHub API once and keeps the answer for six hours. If it cannot get one, the button shows the mark and the label.

footer.socials maps a network to a URL and draws its mark; footer.links adds columns of links above the bottom line. Known keys: github, gitlab, x (or twitter), discord, slack, linkedin, youtube, bluesky, mastodon, reddit, telegram, facebook, instagram, threads, medium, hacker-news, npm, website, email (a mailto: URL), rss and podcast. Any other key whose URL is on one of those sites gets that mark (community: https://discord.gg/x shows Discord); the rest get a globe. Each mark is a link named for its network.

banner puts a strip above the header on every docs page: banner: "Version 2 is out." is the short form. A closed banner stays closed for that reader until its content changes, so a new announcement shows again with no key to bump.

pages.d: Point the docs site at an OpenAPI spec; aiui build loads, bundles and checks it.

s.x: Name your spec in aiui.yaml; aiui validate and aiui build load and check it. A file (relative to aiui.yaml) or an http(s) URL; http://localhost:8080/openapi.json works with no flag. JSON or YAML, OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2. Swagger 2.0 is an error. A $ref to another file (paths/pets.yaml, ../common.yaml#/components/schemas/Error) resolves relative to the file naming it, URLs too, and is bundled in: no pre-bundling. Recursive schemas, across files too, stay finite. 3.0 specs are normalised to 3.1 rules for rendering (nullable, boolean exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum, schema example); the published file keeps your version. openapi also goes on a navigation tab or group: a path or URL, {source, directory} or a list of either. A spec named twice loads once. directory: the URL folder of its endpoint pages (default api-reference).

Each problem names its file, line and JSON pointer (openapi.yaml:42: $ref '#/x' does not resolve (at #/components/schemas/Pet/properties/owner)). Errors failvalidate and build: an unreadable file or URL, YAML/JSON syntax, a missing or unsupported openapi version, info without title/version, a $ref that does not resolve, a path not starting with /, a duplicate operationId. Warning: a {param} with no path parameter.

aiui build writes openapi/ .json (the spec bundled into one file, x-excluded operations removed; : file name, -2 on a clash), openapi/index.json ({"specs": [{source, file, title, openapi, version, operations}]}), an "OpenAPI specs" section in llms.txt and an RFC 9727 API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog (each API's base URL, spec and first endpoint page).

Every operation and 3.1 webhook gets a docs page, generated at build time as Markdown with the API field components: the endpoint bar with Try it, server URL, deprecation notice, path / query / header / cookie parameters, request body, each response (schemas with oneOf/anyOf tabs, constraints and conditional requirements), request examples in several languages, response examples, callbacks and a link to the spec. They publish like hand-written pages: agent .md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, sitemap and site search (which also matches METHOD /path, the operationId and every parameter and body field name). Spec Result api.openapi only an "API Reference" group at the end of the sidebar openapi on a tab its tag groups join the tab ("API Reference" for untagged operations) openapi on a group its tag groups go inside that group tags one sidebar group per operation's first tag; label: x-group, x-displayName, summary, then name; 3.2 parent nests groups; a tag with another kind (badge) makes no group untagged webhook a "Webhooks" group x-hidden: true page built and routable, not in the sidebar or indexes x-excluded: true no page, and removed from the published spec deprecated: true a deprecation notice URL: /docs/ / /, the slug from the operationId (listPets -> list-pets, so rewording a summary keeps the URL), else the summary, else method and path (get-pets-id). x-aiui: {href: /reference/pets} sets the whole path (kebab-cased, .. dropped; see page settings). A slug already taken (by a hand-written page or another endpoint) gets -2, -3. The title is the summary as written, else the operationId in words. aiui validate warns about a duplicate tag, an unknown parent and a parent cycle.

Each field shows what the schema says, at build time, in the page Markdown (so agents and search see it too): Schema On the page $ref, allOf followed and merged into one field list oneOf / anyOf tabs, one per choice, titled by its title, else its $ref name, else its type, else "Option n"; at the top of a body or response too nullable: true, type: [x, "null"], anyOf: [X, {type: "null"}] x \ null in the type; the field still expands to X's properties object[], nested objects properties nested under "Show properties", a recursive schema stops one level down enum, const "Available options: card, bank", "Allowed value: card" minimum/maximum (exclusive too), minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems, pattern "Required range: 1 = 1 elements", "Pattern: ^[0-9]+$" examples / example on a field "Example: 5" (short values) additionalProperties, not "Additional properties: string", "Must not match: integer" if/then/else, dependentRequired, dependentSchemas (also inside allOf) a pill on each affected field: "required if method = card", "required unless method = card", "required if owner is set"; an if that tests more than sibling const / enum / required shows "conditionally required"

The side column's response example has one tab per status code, content type (when a response has several) and named example (its summary, else its key). This gives the tabs 200 · application/json · A small cat, 200 · application/json · big and 200 · application/xml: Per content type: the examples map (value, 3.2 dataValue / serializedValue, or the externalValue URL), else example, else for JSON an example built from the schema. JSON is pretty-printed (a JSON string too); XML, HTML, YAML and CSV are highlighted; other types are text.

The side column shows the request as code, one tab per language: cURL, Python and JavaScript by default. A pick is remembered, so every endpoint page opens on the reader's language. Each sample is built at build time from the spec: the server URL (variables set to their defaults; a relative or missing server is joined to https://api.example.com), path parameters (their example, else a {name} placeholder), required query, header and cookie parameters and any with an example, the first security requirement as a placeholder (Bearer, Basic, an API key in its header, query or cookie) and the body (its first example, else one made from the schema without readOnly fields). JSON, form-urlencoded and plain-text bodies work in every language; multipart/form-data in cURL, Python and JavaScript (a format: binary field is sent as a file). Languages: curl, python, javascript, go, java, ruby, php, csharp, rust, swift (also shell, node, js, py, c#, dotnet, ...). aiui validate names an unknown one. Your own samples, from an SDK say, go in the operation's x-codeSamples (or x-code-samples). They come first, in their order; one in a generated language replaces that sample, any other language adds a tab. label is the tab title (default: the language's name). The agent .md export, llms-full.txt and the page source keep every sample as a fence.

Under the title, every endpoint page has an endpoint bar (method, path, copy) and Try it: a request form with a server menu (operation, path, then spec servers) and an input per server variable, an input per path, query, header and cookie parameter (enum and boolean as menus, arrays comma-separated, empty required ones named before sending) and the body to edit (multipart/form-data as a JSON object of its fields). Inputs start with x-default, else the example (example, examples, default, const, first enum value); the body with its first example, else one made from the schema. Beside them: the curl command for exactly what will be sent, live, with copy, and after Send the status, time, size, headers and body (JSON pretty-printed). A relative or missing server URL means the site the docs are served from. With auth, the bar asks GET /api/auth/status once per page load and shows Try it only when it answers authenticated: true (an aiui serve or create_app site whose reader is signed in; without sign-in configured, every reader counts as signed in). On a static host it acts like simple. Webhooks have no Try it. Front matter playground: (same values) sets the display of one openapi: or api: page, x-aiui metadata.playground of one generated page. The request goes straight from the reader's browser to your API: no proxy, so it works on a static host and keys never pass through a third party, and the browser's CORS rules apply. The API must allow the docs site's origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin; for custom headers or a JSON body, a preflight OPTIONS with Access-Control-Allow-Headers). A blocked request says it "did not reach the API" (the curl command still works in a terminal). Response headers other than the CORS-safelisted ones show only when listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers; a cookie parameter goes only into the curl command (a browser sends just the cookies it holds). aiui build writes each page's form data to openapi/try/ .json; the form is a lazy chunk loaded on the first hover, focus or click of Try it. In the page source the bar is (without src, the bar alone, usable on a hand-written page); the agent .md keeps `GET` `/pets`. #### Authentication An operation's security (else the spec's) becomes an Authorization section on its page (a field per scheme, required when every alternative needs it, OAuth2 scopes listed) and inputs in Try it: apiKey in a header, query or cookie, http bearer (and any other scheme name), http basic (username and password, base64-encoded for you), oauth2 and openIdConnect (paste an access token; sent as Bearer). With several alternatives a menu picks one ({} in the list adds "None"); security: [] turns it off; mutualTLS is left out (a browser cannot send it). A scheme's x-default prefills its input. Values are kept in the browser tab's sessionStorage per docs site (gone when the tab closes, never localStorage) and sent only with the request itself. The curl command shows them as ******** until Show values; the request examples on the page keep placeholders (Bearer). #### Files and streams multipart/form-data: a file input per part with format: binary / byte or a contentMediaType; the chosen file replaces that field (curl --form 'photo=@cat.png'). A body that is a file (application/octet-stream, image/*, audio/*, video/*, PDF, or a format: binary schema): one file input, sent as the body (curl --data-binary). A JSON field with format: byte or contentEncoding: base64 / base64url: a file input that writes the file's encoding into the body. A text/event-stream, NDJSON or JSON Lines response is shown as it arrives: server-sent events as a list (event name, id, data with JSON pretty-printed), other streams as text. Stop ends it; reading stops at 10 MB; a broken connection says "Stream interrupted." (planned): method and kind: badge pills in the sidebar, a choice picker for any fields, api.optional, and showing image, audio and video responses inline.

Name an operation in a page's front matter and the page shows it: the endpoint bar and Try it under your # title, your Markdown, then the generated parameters, body, responses and request and response examples. "GET /users" looks in every spec the config names; "admin.yaml POST /users" in that file (its name is enough; a file only pages name is loaded, relative to aiui.yaml, and published); "webhook user-created" names a webhook. title, description and search keywords come from the operation unless the page sets them; the spec's description shows only when the page has no text of its own. The operation gets no generated page of its own: your page replaces it. playground: simple (or none) on the page changes its Try it display.
api: makes an endpoint page from the page alone: the bar, and Try it with an input per (placeholder, else default, as the example), per {param} in the path, and a JSON body of the body fields.

A pages: entry can be an operation: "GET /users", "admin.yaml POST /users" or "webhook user-created". Without a file it comes from the nearest group or tab with openapi, else api.openapi, else any spec. When a spec's own group (or api.openapi) lists operations, only the listed ones get pages, each where it is listed, and no tag groups are added. An entry for an operation a page shows (openapi: front matter) links that page. aiui validate names a reference that matches no operation (7012).

An operation's x-aiui sets its generated page: metadata is front matter (title, sidebarTitle, description, playground, tag, og:*, ...), content is Markdown shown above the description (any docs component works) and href the page URL. The x-mint key other docs tools write is read too; x-aiui wins where both set a value. From Python, praisonaiui.compiler.openapi.load_spec("openapi.yaml") returns an ApiSpec (ok, issues, document, operations, dereference(node)).

pages.d: One line in a docs page and aiui build writes the reference for a Python module, class or function from its docstrings.

s.x: Write one line in a docs page and the build turns it into the reference for that Python module, class or function: No extra tool or build step. The source is read as text (Python's ast), so the package does not have to be installed and nothing is imported. aiui dev rebuilds the page when you save a .py file. The reference goes in where the line is, in the same pass as snippets, so the page, its agent .md, llms-full.txt, search and aiui validate all see it.

You write You get ::: mypkg.client The module docstring, then its public members: __all__ in order when there is one (re-exports followed), else every public class and function ::: mypkg.client.Client The class: constructor signature and parameters, bases, attributes (annotated or documented, properties, Field(default=, description=)), then its public methods ::: mypkg.client.connect One function or method Each object gets a heading anchored by its dotted path with dashes (#mypkg-client-Client-fetch) and its signature with type hints and defaults. Names starting with _ are left out. From the docstring: Parameters: rows with the type and default from the signature, required when there is no default, and the text; documented **kwargs keys get rows too. Attributes: rows. Returns, Yields, Raises: lists of types with their text. >>> examples, :: blocks and .. code-block::: highlighted code. Notes, Warnings, .. note::, .. warning::: callouts. Google (Args:), NumPy (Parameters over ----------) and reST (:param x:, :type x:, :returns:, :rtype:, :raises E:) styles all work. reST roles become code, and < is escaped so text never turns into a tag.

YAML on the indented lines under the block (an options: mapping works too): Option Default What it does members all public Only these members, in this order; false: the object alone private false Also _name members (not __dunder__) show_source false A collapsed "Source code" block under each object heading_level 2 Heading level of the block's own object (1 to 6)
mypkg.client is mypkg/client.py, mypkg/client/__init__.py or a .pyi, in src/, then the project folder. Change the folders, searched in order:

A block naming no module or member, a file that is not valid Python, or an unknown option is 7016 in aiui validate and fails aiui build with the page and line. A ::: line inside a code fence is left alone.
The class behind this page, from ::: praisonaiui.compiler.python_api.PythonApi with members: [markdown] and heading_level: 3:

Finds and renders the objects ::: blocks name. Parameters The project folder. Folders under root searched in order for a module's file. #### PythonApi.markdown() {#praisonaiui-compiler-python_api-PythonApi-markdown} The Markdown for one ::: target block. Parameters A dotted module path, optionally followed by a class, function or method. The block's options (members, private, show_source, heading_level). Returns str: Headings, signatures and field rows for the docs Markdown pipeline. Raises ApiReferenceError: When target names nothing, or a listed member does not exist.

pages.d: Learn how templates and layouts work in PraisonAIUI.

s.x: Learn how templates and layouts work in PraisonAIUI.

A template, used by the docs site (aiui build), combines: a layout: the structure around the page content slots: the components for the header, footer and table of contents (see Slots & Components) optional zones: widgets around the content (see Widget Zones) Routes pick the template for a URL (see Configuration). These are docs-site layouts; the layouts of the React app shell are a different thing (see Layouts).

Every layout sits between the site header and footer. Layout Description ThreeColumnLayout Sidebar + content + TOC (the default) TwoColumnLayout Sidebar + content (no TOC) CenteredLayout Centered content, no sidebar; hero zone FullWidthLayout Sidebar when there is navigation, wide content; hero zone FlexibleLayout Sidebar (or leftSidebar widgets), content, TOC, and widget zones
The classic documentation layout with sidebar and TOC.
Sidebar + Content without the right TOC column.
Centered content with no sidebar, ideal for articles/blogs.
The content takes the remaining width; the sidebar shows only when the site has docs navigation.
Slots can be assigned in two ways:
Point to a component defined in the components section:
Use a component type directly:
right: null hides the table of contents (the only slot the renderer hides):

pages.d: A template names a component for each slot of its layout. In the docs site that

s.x: A template names a component for each slot of its layout. In the docs site that aiui build produces, the React renderer reads three slots; the others are validated and compiled into the manifest but do not change the page.

Slot Effect in the docs site header Its component's props (logoText, logoImage, links, cta) fill the header. YAML navbar links and CTA win over links/cta, but logoImage wins over YAML logo.light/logo.dark footer Its component's props (text, links) fill the footer bottom row, next to YAML footer right null hides the table of contents; any other value shows it left, main No effect: the sidebar is always the generated navigation and the main area the page's Markdown Without a header or footer slot, the components named header and footer are used. aiui validate checks that every ref names a component.
These name the generated navigation, the page content and the table of contents. They take no props the renderer reads.

The docs site renderer has no hook for your own slot components. The separate TypeScript runtime in the repository (src/praisonaiui-ts, see TypeScript) has a SlotRegistry for apps that render the manifests themselves. Pages in the React app shell are added with plugins instead (see Plugins).

pages.d: Widget zones place small built-in widgets (stats cards, links, banners) around

s.x: Widget zones place small built-in widgets (stats cards, links, banners) around the page content of a docs site (aiui build, style: docs or custom), configured per template in YAML.
FlexibleLayout renders these zones:
Use the zones property in your template configuration:

Zone Location Notes hero Above the content Banners, announcements leftSidebar Left column Replaces the docs navigation when set rightSidebar Right column Below the table of contents bottomNav Below the content Related links footer Bottom Footer widgets, above the site footer header, topNav, main Accepted by the schema; no layout renders them yet A Toc entry in rightSidebar is skipped: the table of contents is always drawn there when the page has headings. When the config defines a component named sidebar, header or footer and a template leaves the matching zone (leftSidebar, header, footer) empty, the build fills the zone with that component.
Display metrics and statistics.
Navigation links widget.
Email subscription form.
Landing page hero section.
Social media links.
Copyright notice.

Widget Props Progress label, value (0 to 100), showPercent (default true) Announcement title, message, type (info, warning, success) RecentPosts title, posts (list of title, href, date) BadgeList title, badges (list of strings)
Layout Zones rendered FlexibleLayout hero, leftSidebar, rightSidebar, bottomNav, footer ThreeColumnLayout (default) rightSidebar CenteredLayout hero FullWidthLayout hero TwoColumnLayout none

pages.d: Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

s.x: Built-in SEO for documentation sites — sitemap, robots, llms.txt, per-page meta tags, and crawlable static HTML.

Top-level seo block in aiui.yaml: Every key is optional; the defaults are what most sites want. siteUrl is needed for absolute canonical URLs and sitemap.xml. Without it the build falls back to a CNAME file next to the config (or in docs/), and without either there is no sitemap and llms.txt / llms-full.txt use root-relative links. What the build publishes for agents (agent-ready .md pages, llms.txt by nav group, markdown.instructions): AI-ready docs.

aiui build automatically generates: File Purpose sitemap.xml All doc URLs with lastmod dates robots.txt Crawl rules + sitemap pointer llms.txt AI crawler index (llmstxt.org), one section per nav group llms-full.txt Every page as agent-ready Markdown, in one file docs/**/*.html Per-route HTML with meta tags + crawl nav .nojekyll GitHub Pages Jekyll bypass No extra flags are needed: the files are written whenever content.docs is configured (the site-URL ones only when a site URL is known, see above). A robots.txt or sitemap.xml next to aiui.yaml is published as it is, instead of the generated one.

One rule decides the sitemap, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, site search and the page's robots meta, so they never disagree: Page Sidebar Sitemap, llms, search normal yes yes index, follow noindex: true yes no noindex hidden no no (yes with seo.indexing: all) noindex (index, follow with all) any, with seo.robots.index: false as above no sitemap or llms files; search kept noindex searchable: false yes sitemap and llms yes; site search no index, follow Each page has exactly one robots meta tag. noindex does not add nofollow: crawlers still follow the page's links to the pages that are indexed. With seo.robots.index: false, robots.txt says Disallow: /, and no sitemap.xml or llms*.txt is written (one left from an earlier build is removed).

A hidden page is built and reachable by its URL (share the link), but it is not in the sidebar, the previous / next links or search, and not indexed. In content.docs.nav.mode: manual, hidden: true on a group or tab hides all its pages, and pages no group lists are hidden too (Navigation). A folder without an index.md is a sidebar section only, never a page: it gets no route and no sitemap entry.

seo.contentSignals writes a Content-Signal line into robots.txt, saying how crawlers may use the pages: search (search results), aiInput (answers grounded on the page) and aiTrain (model training). Keys you leave out are left out of the line; with no contentSignals there is no line.

Use frontmatter on any markdown page: If description is omitted, the first paragraph is used automatically. Component and HTML tags are left out of it: a page that opens with or a multi-line gets its first sentence of prose. Any Open Graph, Twitter or article tag, the canonical URL, the robots value and keywords can be set per page (quote keys that have a colon): Each tag is decided once, in this order (later wins): the built defaults, seo.metatags, seo.paths (shorter paths first), the page's frontmatter. Then og:url follows the canonical and twitter:image the og:image (unless set themselves), and twitter:card is summary_large_image when the page has an image. Root-relative URLs (/images/x.png) become absolute. A noindex page keeps noindex whatever the overrides say, and a robots value with noindex (from frontmatter or a seo.paths folder) also leaves the page out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search, so they never disagree. Open Graph keys (og:, article:) are written as property=, the rest as name=; every value is HTML-escaped. aiui validate rejects a seo.metatags key that is not a tag name.

Install Pillow and every docs page gets its own share image, with no config: The build draws a 1200x630 PNG per page and publishes it at /og/ .png (/og/docs/guide/install.png). Each card shows the page title (sized to fit, up to three lines), its sidebar group, as much of the description as fits, the site name with its logo and the site's host, in the theme's accent and colour mode (site.theme.preset, accent, accentDark, mode; preset paper gets the paper colours). A PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF logo is drawn as is; an SVG or emoji logo becomes the site's initial on an accent tile. Latin text uses the UI's own font; other scripts use a system font (Noto Sans CJK, Arial Unicode, Noto Sans or DejaVu Sans). The card becomes the page's og:image and twitter:image, with a summary_large_image card, in the built HTML and when the docs app moves between pages, and the site root shares the docs home's card. Which image a page gets, first match wins: Set by Image 'og:image' in the page's frontmatter or a seo.paths folder that image, no card drawn og:image in seo.metatags that image on every page, no cards drawn seo.ogImages: false, or Pillow not installed seo.defaultImage otherwise the page's generated card Cards are cached by a hash of what they show (in $AIUI_DATA_DIR/og-cards, else ~/.praisonaiui/cache/og-cards), so aiui dev and repeat builds only draw the pages that changed, and new cards are drawn in parallel. Without Pillow, aiui build prints one note saying how to turn them on.

Each route HTML file contains: (absolute HTTPS) Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type, og:site_name, og:image: the page's social card by default), each once Twitter Card tags (summary_large_image with an image) Your seo.metatags, seo.paths and frontmatter tags One JSON-LD @graph: Organization, WebSite (with a SearchAction: ?q= opens site search), TechArticle (publisher, dateModified with content.docs.lastUpdated, keywords, image) and a BreadcrumbList from the sidebar groups Static with links to every doc page (for non-JS crawlers) pre-rendered page content

When users navigate via the sidebar, React updates title, canonical, OG, Twitter, robots, and JSON-LD to match the current page, with the same tags, overrides and order as the built HTML (docs-nav.json carries each page's seo map). The built page's JSON-LD graph stays while it is the page shown.
See GitHub Pages for publishing the build. Submit your sitemap in Google Search Console:

pages.d: Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and

s.x: Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and choose what readers see on a URL with no page.

List moved pages under redirects: at the top level of aiui.yaml: Key Meaning source A site path starting with /. :name matches one path segment; a final :name* matches the rest of the path, including nothing (/docs/v1/:slug* matches /docs/v1 and /docs/v1/a/b). destination A site path or a full URL. It can reuse the names from source. permanent true (default) answers with 301, false with 302. The first matching rule wins. Leave out the --base-path prefix: rules use site paths and the build adds the base path.

s.h: Where each kind of rule works
s.x: aiui build publishes every rule whose source is not a published page: Host Exact source (/docs/old) Wildcard source (/docs/v1/:slug*) aiui serve 301 / 302 301 / 302 (a file at the path wins) Netlify, Cloudflare Pages 301 / 302 from the _redirects file 301 / 302 from _redirects GitHub Pages, any static host A stub page at the old URL (meta refresh, a canonical link, a script redirect) The docs app follows the rule from the page-not-found view The query string and the #section carry over unless the destination sets its own. A stub never replaces a real file; it has noindex and a canonical link to the new URL. The link check treats every source as a valid link.
aiui validate warns when an exact rule loops or ends at a docs path with no page (7010), or when a page is still published at its source (7011).

A URL with no page shows "Page not found", a link home, the search, and up to three pages from the sidebar whose names are close to the URL (a typo such as /docs/instalation offers Installation), unless a redirects: rule matches first. pages.d: A docs site built with aiui build ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy

s.x: A docs site built with aiui build ships with a strict Content-Security-Policy and needs no configuration. The policy allows the scripts the site runs and nothing else, so injected markup cannot run a script, and only your own site can show the docs in a frame.

aiui build works the policy out from what the site actually loads: Source Directive The site's own files (app, chunks, fonts, customCss/customJs files, the site.components module and its import map's hash) 'self' The small inline scripts the build writes (theme, URL, redirect stubs) script-src 'sha256-…', one hash each The JSON the build inlines in each page (its Markdown, the navigation and route manifest) nothing: type="application/json" is data the browser never runs Google Fonts and font, stylesheet and script URLs in site.theme.fonts, customCss, customJs style-src, font-src, script-src Integrations (analytics, support chat) each provider's hosts YouTube, Vimeo and Loom embeds on a page frame-src (the privacy-friendly player) The servers of your OpenAPI specs (Try it) connect-src assistant.endpoint, feedback.endpoint on a static host connect-src A navbar primary button of type: github (the star count) connect-src https://api.github.com Everything else stays strict: no 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' for scripts, object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self'. Images and media load from 'self', data:, blob: and any https: host, so Markdown images and badges keep working. Styles allow 'unsafe-inline': the app's code highlighting, diagrams and dialogs set inline styles. The policy goes out three ways: Every built page carries it as , right after . This works on any static host, GitHub Pages included. _headers in the build folder sends it as a header on Netlify and Cloudflare Pages, with frame-ancestors 'self' added (a meta tag cannot carry frame-ancestors). aiui serve and aiui dev send the /* headers of _headers, so the preview behaves like the host. The aiui dev reload script is a file (/__aiui/dev.js), so it runs under the same policy. On another host (nginx, S3 with CloudFront, a CDN), copy the header line from _headers into its configuration.

site.csp Effect unset On for a docs build (reported only when integrations.gtm is set, see below); off for other builds true On, enforced false Off: no meta tag, no _headers report-only Only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only in _headers and from aiui serve: the browser logs what the policy would block, and blocks nothing a map On, with extra sources per directive (a string or a list). A list with 'none' replaces the directive (frame-ancestors: ["'none'"] forbids every frame). report-only: true in the map reports instead of enforcing. report-uri sets where the browser posts reports Directive names are lower-case words (script-src, connect-src, ...) and sources contain no spaces, ; or ,: anything else is a config error, so the value is always a valid header.

customJs that calls another server (fetch, a WebSocket, a widget): add its origin under connect-src, frame-src or script-src. Raw HTML in a page needs no sources: the page renders YouTube, Vimeo and Loom players, and (all allowed above), shows any other as a link and removes , and similar elements before the policy is ever involved. aiui validate names each one (finding 7019; see raw HTML). Inline event handlers (onclick="…") never run. Tag Manager (integrations.gtm) runs whatever tags the container holds, which the build cannot see, so the default there is report-only. Add the hosts of your tags and set site.csp: true to enforce. Legacy site.plugins: mermaid and syntax-highlight load from their CDN, which the policy allows when they are listed. Other dashboard plugins are not meant for docs pages. To find what a page needs, open the browser console: every blocked load or script is logged with the directive that blocked it. report-only shows the same messages without blocking anything.

With consent, nothing loads until the reader accepts. A small banner at the bottom of the page offers Decline and Accept, the same size and style, so declining is as easy as accepting. The choice is remembered in the browser's local storage (aiui-consent: granted or denied). The banner uses the site's theme colours in light and dark mode and fits a phone screen. Your own consent tool. Set banner: false and tell the page the reader's choice from the tool's callback:

s.x: for="humans" shows on the page and in site search only; for="agents" only in the .md and the llms files.
aiui serve answers a page URL with its Markdown when Accept ranks text/markdown at least as high as text/html (browsers still get the page):

aiui serve and aiui dev also run an MCP server for the site at /mcp, so an editor's agent can search and read the docs while it works, and tell you when a page let it down. Nothing to install or configure: Tool What it returns search_docs(query, limit=10) the best matching pages and sections (ranked as the search dialog ranks them), each with its path, URL and a snippet read_page(path) one page's agent-ready Markdown; path is a page path (/docs/guide/install) or URL list_pages() every page by nav group (llms.txt) submit_feedback(path, helpful, comment?) stores a vote on a page, like a reader's "Was this page helpful?", with source: agent The first three are read-only. submit_feedback lets an agent report a page that is wrong, outdated, unclear or missing what it needed, so docs problems reach you from the agents reading them. Reports land in the same store as readers' votes, so aiui docs feedback counts them together (in the CSV and JSON exports source tells them apart), under the same limits as the page's vote button: 20 a minute per client (shared with /api/docs/feedback), 4 KiB, a 1,000-character comment, and only for pages that exist. The tool is not listed when page feedback is off (feedback: false) or posted to your own endpoint. Connect from the page menu (Copy MCP server URL, Connect to Cursor, Connect to VS Code), or add it by hand: Agents also find it on their own: /.well-known/mcp (also mcp.json and mcp/server-card.json) serves a server card with the endpoint and the tools, and llms.txt ends with an "MCP server" section linking it. The transport is Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC over POST, protocol versions 2025-03-26 to 2025-11-25) and stateless. Requests whose Host is not a name the server answers to (DNS rebinding; behind a reverse proxy on the same machine list the public name in AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS) or that come from another site's page (Origin; allow one with --cors-origins or AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) are refused. To turn the server off: A static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) runs no server, so it has no /mcp and the menu shows no MCP items; the .md pages and llms files above still work there.

aiui serve and aiui dev also answer questions about the docs, with the sections each answer came from. Set a model key in the environment and serve; there is nothing to configure: The server ranks the build's sections for the question (the same ranking as search, widened so a long question still finds its pages), sends the best six to the model and streams a Markdown answer that cites them as [1], [2]. Your key stays on the server: it is read from the environment and never logged or sent to the browser. Key Default What it does starters none up to six questions offered before the reader asks instructions none extra rules for every answer (tone, names, scope); up to 4,000 characters model see above the model endpoint none on a static host, the ask URL of an aiui serve running the same build assistant: false turns it off. The build writes these settings into ui-config.json, which is public: keep secrets out of instructions.

When the server has a model, the docs header shows Ask AI. It opens a side panel with your starter questions; answers stream in, cite their sections as [1] links that open the page at that section, list the sections under the answer, and can be copied or stopped. Follow-up questions keep the conversation. Other ways in: Entry point What it does ⌘I / Ctrl+I opens the panel ?assistant= on any page URL opens the panel and asks; the parameter leaves the address bar select a passage in a page an Ask about this chip quotes it in the question search (⌘K) an Ask AI: row under the results a page with mode: assistant the page's text, then the panel inline: a full "Ask the docs" page window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('aiui:docs-ask', { detail: { question, context } })) from your own JavaScript A server without a key shows none of this (the API above still returns the best sections). The endpoints are public like the site, so they are guarded: 10 questions a minute per client, a 32 KiB body, a 2,000-character question, the same Host and Origin checks as the MCP server, and application/json or text/plain bodies (a static site on another origin posts text/plain, allowed with --cors-origins or AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS). pages.d: Two commands reload during development: aiui dev for a docs site and

s.x: Two commands reload during development: aiui dev for a docs site and aiui run --reload for an app.

Run it in the folder that holds aiui.yaml: It builds the site, serves it and opens it in the browser. Save a page, a snippet or aiui.yaml and the site rebuilds and the open tab reloads by itself, at the same scroll position (the URL keeps the #heading). No configuration needed to start. A folder with only a docs/ folder of Markdown files works: the site is built with the defaults and titled after the folder. A broken edit never takes the preview down. The error is printed in the terminal and shown over the page, and the last good build stays up until you save a fix. Warnings from the build (content checks) print once each in the terminal. Production output is untouched. Each build goes to a temporary folder, removed on exit. The few lines of script that listen for rebuilds are added to pages as they are served, so aiui build output never contains them. The preview is served the way aiui serve serves the build: the same routes, cache rules and base path. The tab listens on /__aiui/dev (Server-Sent Events) with a script served from /__aiui/dev.js, so the preview runs under the site's Content Security Policy. It only answers on this machine unless you pass --host; build errors include file paths, so expose it only on a network you trust. Every option is in the CLI reference.

aiui serve --watch rebuilds the site into the output folder on every change in the configuration's folder, without reloading the browser. Use it when you want the built files on disk; aiui dev is the writing loop.
Uvicorn restarts the server when a file in the folder of app.py changes, and the restarted server loads app.py again with the same style, datastore and config.
aiui dev --examples serves a small dashboard (default port 9000) that switches between the example projects in a folder (each a directory with an aiui.yaml, or the old name aiui.template.yaml):
Config Hot-Reload: reloading the runtime config of a running server CLI

pages.d: PraisonAIUI uses a provider protocol — a simple abstraction that lets you plug in any AI backend.

s.x: PraisonAIUI uses a provider protocol — a simple abstraction that lets you plug in any AI backend.

The provider protocol is the only contract between the frontend and any AI backend. All dashboard pages (/api/overview, /api/config, /api/logs, etc.) are provider-agnostic — they always work regardless of which backend is active. The provider only handles agent execution (run()), agent listing (list_agents()), and health checks (health()).

The user sends a message: a chat frame on the WebSocket /api/chat/ws (the default for the chat page and the app shell), or POST /run (SSE) The server calls provider.run(message) on the active provider The provider yields RunEvent objects (start, content, tool calls, reasoning, completion) The server sends each event as an SSE data: frame (RunEvent.to_dict()) or as a WebSocket message, and stores the finished turn in the datastore. The WebSocket adapter forwards only selected fields per event type (for example, reasoning events carry step but not action, confidence or next_action), so only SSE clients receive every serialized field The frontend renders the events as they arrive

PraisonAIProvider is the default. When the app registers a @aiui.reply callback, it runs the callback and turns its aiui.say(), aiui.think(), aiui.image() and other calls into RunEvents: Without a callback it runs a praisonaiagents Agent (install aiui[praisonai]): the agent named in the request when one is defined through the agents API or config.yaml, else a default assistant. Without praisonaiagents it echoes the message.

The default provider resolves tools for agents using ToolResolver from the praisonai package. Agents created via the CRUD API or ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml get their tool names (strings) automatically resolved to callable Python functions: When an agent has no tools configured, the provider gives it the tools of the SDK's autonomy profile (file operations, command execution, web search). The default assistant runs with reflection off.
Implement BaseProvider.run() — that's it:

Any provider can attach rich media to chat messages using MESSAGE_ELEMENT events. The UI renders them inline and persists them in session history. Tool results from PraisonAI agents are also detected automatically when they match OpenAI image shapes ({"data": [{"url": "..."}]}) or explicit element dicts — no provider code required. Callback handlers can use await aiui.image(url) (or dict entries in Message.elements) and the default PraisonAIProvider maps those to MESSAGE_ELEMENT events. Typed elements from Message.add_image() are not forwarded yet; see Message Elements. Full architecture, data flows, and tests: Image Preview in Chat.

Every event has a type field and optional payload fields: Field Type Used By type RunEventType All events content str RUN_COMPLETED, RUN_CONTENT token str RUN_CONTENT (streaming) name str TOOL_CALL_* args dict TOOL_CALL_STARTED result any TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED tool_call_id str TOOL_CALL_* (pairs start and completion) step str REASONING_STEP (also action, confidence, next_action) query, references, time_ms str, list, float REFERENCES (RAG sources) error str RUN_ERROR agent_id, agent_name, team_id str Multi-agent events extra_data dict Custom payload (includes element for message_element)

Agent Events Type Description run_started Agent run begins run_content Streaming token or content chunk run_completed Agent run finished run_error Error occurred run_cancelled User cancelled tool_call_started Tool invocation started tool_call_completed Tool returned result llm_content Narrative text between tool calls reasoning_started Thinking begun reasoning_step Individual reasoning step reasoning_completed Thinking finished memory_update_started Memory write begun memory_update_completed Memory write done updating_memory Memory being updated run_paused Run paused (e.g. waiting for user) run_continued Run resumed references RAG source chunks for the answer message_element Inline media element (image, video, file, etc.) — see Image Preview in Chat Team Events Type Description team_run_started Team run begins team_run_content Team streaming content team_run_completed Team run finished team_run_error Team error team_run_cancelled Team cancelled team_tool_call_started Team tool call started team_tool_call_completed Team tool call done team_reasoning_started Team reasoning begun team_reasoning_step Team reasoning step team_reasoning_completed Team reasoning done team_memory_update_started Team memory update started team_memory_update_completed Team memory update done

Subclass and implement run() to create a custom provider. Method Description run(message, *, session_id, agent_name, **kw) Required. Async generator yielding RunEvent objects list_agents() Optional. Returns list of available agents run_team(...) Optional. Multi-agent run health() Optional. Returns health check dict message_element_event(element) Static helper: a MESSAGE_ELEMENT event for an element dict
Structured event with type: RunEventType and optional payload fields (see the table above). to_dict() serialises it to the JSON the frontend reads.
30 string values matching the frontend types.ts; see the Agent Events and Team Events tabs above.

When hosted via praisonai.integration.host_app.configure_host(), the wrapper calls praisonaiui.backends.set_backend() for: Backend key Feature area hooks Hooks dashboard workflows Workflow runs usage_query / usage_sink Usage analytics approvals_pending / approvals_policies HITL approvals jobs_store / jobs_executor Async jobs (optional) channel_bot Channel bots (optional) tool_resolver Agent tool name resolution (optional) Detect integrated mode in code: praisonaiui.backends.is_integrated_mode().

These features work standalone with in-memory stores. Health responses include sdk_gap: true: Feature Gap Standalone behaviour nodes No cluster API in praisonaiagents In-memory node registry auth No SDK auth module In-memory API keys / sessions channels Bot runtime via praisonai wrapper In-memory channel registry; bots need praisonai[bot] jobs Mock success only when standalone and agent missing Integrated mode fails job instead of fake success realtime WebRTC needs OPENAI_API_KEY Mock stream standalone; degraded error when integrated without key media / code SDK paths optional status: simulated standalone; status: degraded integrated on failure View gaps in the dashboard sidebar footer (GET /api/health → sdk_gaps array).

Session/data handling: standalone uses UI datastore fallback; integrated aligns with SDK-backed stores. Feature backends: standalone keeps in-memory/mock behaviour; integrated routes through injected factories. Lifecycle hooks: integrated mode can subscribe to SDK hooks (handoff, MCP lifecycle, tracing/eval stores).

Use standalone mode for local UI-only workflows. Use integrated mode when you need shared runtime state with PraisonAI agents, tools, tracing, approvals, and schedules. See also backend-integration.md and praisonai-package-integration.md.

pages.d: PraisonAIUI supports a four-layer integration model so standalone mode and SDK-integrated mode can share the same feature APIs.

s.x: PraisonAIUI supports a four-layer integration model so standalone mode and SDK-integrated mode can share the same feature APIs.

Feature API layer Endpoints live in feature modules and expose stable HTTP/CLI behaviour. Feature manager layer Each feature manager keeps local fallback logic for standalone operation. Backend factory layer praisonaiui.backends provides optional injected factories (get_workflow_runner(), get_hooks_lister(), get_usage_query(), etc.). SDK/runtime layer PraisonAI or praisonaiagents implementations are used when injected or importable.

Injected backends are optional and must be callable. Features must keep local fallbacks when injected backends are absent or fail. Backend call signatures should remain minimal and dict/list based. Integration should not introduce hard imports in feature modules when a fallback already exists.
When integrated, wrappers should inject backend callables at startup; when standalone, features should run without any backend injection.

pages.d: Production deployment guide for AIUI — covering Docker, environment variables, configuration, and security.

s.x: Production deployment guide for AIUI — covering Docker, environment variables, configuration, and security.

Variable Default Description AIUI_DATA_DIR ~/.praisonaiui Data directory for config, sessions, logs, and feature data (see below) AIUI_PORT 8082 Server port (Docker only) AIUI_HOST 0.0.0.0 Server bind address (Docker only) AUTH_ENFORCE false Enforce Bearer token auth on every route except the public surface (see below) AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS — Comma-separated origins allowed to call the server from another site (CORS and cross-site requests); * allows any AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS — Comma-separated host names the server answers to when reached on a loopback or private address (.example.com also matches subdomains); * turns the check off AIUI_KNOWLEDGE_ROOTS — Folders (os.pathsep-separated) that POST /api/knowledge/add-file may read, in addition to the chat attachments folder; any other file_path is refused with 400 AIUI_MAX_BODY_MB 25 Largest request body in MiB; a bigger one gets 413 before it is read. 0 turns this cap off. Paths that need no credentials (login, sign-up, protocol negotiation) always take at most 64 KiB AIUI_PUBLIC_STATIC_DIR — 1 serves every file in a static_dir without credentials (see Auth Enforcement); by default only code, styles, fonts, images and the HTML shell are public OPENAI_API_KEY — OpenAI API key for LLM provider

s.h: Feature data and the data directory
s.x: When AIUI_DATA_DIR or PRAISONAI_HOME is set (PRAISONAI_HOME wins when both are), feature data lives under that directory, so two servers with different data directories never see each other's data: Data With a data directory Without one (default install) Explicit override Recorded runs (Overview, Replay, Runs) /traces ~/.praison/traces PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR, then PRAISON_HOME/traces Memory /memory ~/.praisonai/memory and ./.praisonai/memory — Knowledge store /knowledge ./.praisonai — Training sessions /train ~/.praison/train PRAISON_TRAIN_DIR MCP server list /mcp.json ~/.praisonai/mcp.json — Video projects /projects ~/.praisonai/projects PRAISONAI_PROJECTS_DIR, set_video_engine(projects_dir=) Setting AIUI_DATA_DIR to its default, ~/.praisonaiui, counts as not set. The PraisonAI CLI always records runs to ~/.praison/traces. A server with a data directory does not show those runs unless you also set PRAISONAI_TRACES_DIR=~/.praison/traces.

When AUTH_ENFORCE=true, every route requires a valid Bearer token in the Authorization header: /api/*, and also /sessions, /run, /cancel, /agents/{id}/runs, /teams/*, /v1/* (OpenAI-compatible), /agui and any route a plugin adds. Only the public surface answers without one (deny by default): Public paths (always accessible without auth): /health, /health/live, /health/ready, /api/health — health checks /api/auth/login, /login — login endpoints /api/protocol, /api/protocol/negotiate — protocol discovery the HTML page for a browser navigation (/, /chat, …; under style: app /sessions and /agents too, but only as the page, never their JSON) static code: /assets/*, /plugins/*, /_aiui/externals/*, /_plugins/*, /icon.svg, /manifest.json, /sw.js, /custom.js, /ui-config.json OAuth sign-in: GET /api/auth/oauth/{provider} and its /callback (they only redirect) A static_dir folder (create_app(static_dir=...), aiui run --config) is not public as a whole. Its code, styles, fonts and images (.js .mjs .css .map .woff .woff2 .ttf .otf .eot .svg .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .ico) answer without credentials. So do its HTML pages, but under AUTH_ENFORCE and require_auth they are served as the app shell only: the page's inlined markdown and copy are removed. Markdown, JSON (a search index) and any other file need credentials, under AUTH_ENFORCE, require_auth and URL-token mode alike. The docs app sends the stored access token with every request it makes (pages, manifests, search). A reader who has not signed in sees the sign-in prompt, and after entering the token reads the site as on an open server. Page titles and descriptions stay visible: /docs-nav.json lists them for the sidebar. To keep the folder public in front of a private API, set AIUI_PUBLIC_STATIC_DIR=1. A built docs site served by aiui serve takes a password, open pages and reader groups from content.docs.auth instead (docs sign-in). WebSocket handshakes are gated too (all of them). Browsers cannot send an Authorization header on a WebSocket, so the UI first exchanges its key for a single-use ticket (POST /api/auth/ws-ticket, valid 60 s) and connects with ?ticket=. Clients that cannot do that may still send ?token=; it is redacted from the server's access log. The other auth modes gate WebSockets as well: URL-token mode (AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN=1) accepts its session cookie, a Bearer header, ?token= or a ticket; create_app(require_auth=True) / YAML auth.requireAuth checks session tokens on every route and socket except the public surface above.

A token from POST /register passes the requireAuth check, so registration is closed by default. POST /register is accepted only: for the first user: while no account exists (and no login, password, header or OAuth callback is registered), the first registration creates it; from a signed-in user (Authorization: Bearer), to add an account; for anyone when the config opts in: (create_app(config={"auth": {"requireAuth": True, "allowSignup": True}}) from Python.) Otherwise it returns 403 {"error": "Registration is closed"}. Accounts live in memory, so after a restart the first-user window is open again until someone registers; create the admin in your app at startup (praisonaiui.auth.register_user("admin", password)) to close it. Under AUTH_ENFORCE and URL-token mode /register already needs the API key or URL token, as before; with no auth mode it stays open.

Signing in (POST /login, POST /register, OAuth) returns a session token in the JSON body and also sets it as an httpOnly cookie. The token is signed (HMAC-SHA256), not held in server memory, so a session survives a restart and works on every worker that shares the secret. With no config the first sign-in generates one into /auth_secret (mode 0600, never logged). For several hosts set the same secret everywhere: export AIUI_AUTH_SECRET=$(aiui auth create-secret). Sliding. Under requireAuth the cookie signs in HTTP and WebSockets, and a request past half its lifetime gets a fresh one: active users stay signed in, idle ones are signed out after sessionLifetime. A Bearer token lasts sessionLifetime from sign-in. SameSite and the cross-site guard keep other sites from riding the cookie. Sign-out. POST /logout revokes the Bearer token and the cookie and deletes the cookie. Revoked token ids stay in /auth_revoked.jsonl until they would have expired, so every worker on that data directory honours them. Session.clear_tokens() (in @aiui.on_logout) signs the user out on every device. Rotation. AIUI_AUTH_SECRET=new,old: the first secret signs, all verify. Drop old after sessionLifetime. A single new secret (or deleting auth_secret) signs everyone out. Trade-off: hosts that do not share the data directory verify sessions but do not see each other's sign-outs, so a signed-out token stays valid there until it expires. Keep sessionLifetime short in that setup, or rotate the secret.

With a provider configured (AIUI_OAUTH_ _CLIENT_ID and _CLIENT_SECRET), a browser starts sign-in at /api/auth/oauth/ ?return_url=/chat. Both that route and the callback are public in every auth mode. return_url must be a path on this server (starting with a single /). Anything else, such as an absolute URL or //host, returns to /. The callback sends the browser to #token=. The token is in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to a server, a log or a Referer. The dashboard stores it and removes it from the address bar. A client that sends Accept: application/json gets {"user", "token"} instead. OAuth tokens are session tokens, so they sign in under require_auth / auth.requireAuth.
The config file is located at AIUI_DATA_DIR/config.yaml (default: ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml).
The site title is configurable via site.title in config.yaml: This affects: HTML tag Dashboard header /ui-config.json response
Use the fast liveness endpoint for probes to avoid timeouts:
The Dockerfile includes a built-in health check:

AIUI supports multiple authentication modes: Mode Description none No authentication (default) api_key API key in X-API-Key header or api_key query param session Session token in Authorization: Bearer header password Username/password login

By default the server only serves its own pages: responses carry no CORS headers, and a page on another site can neither open a WebSocket to it nor send it a state-changing request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, including text/plain "simple" requests that skip the CORS preflight). The check uses the browser's Sec-Fetch-Site header, so it works behind a reverse proxy that rewrites Host; without that header the Origin is compared with Host and X-Forwarded-Host. Requests with neither header (curl, SDK clients) are not affected. A local dev server (Vite on another port) talking to a local server is allowed. To let another site call the server (an embedded widget, a separate frontend), list its origin:

A server reached on a loopback or private address (127.0.0.1, 192.168.x.x, a Docker bridge) only answers requests whose Host is an IP address, localhost / *.localhost, a *.local name, the machine's own hostname, or a name listed in AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Anything else gets 400 Host not allowed (a WebSocket is closed with code 1008). This stops DNS rebinding, where a website points its own domain at 127.0.0.1 so that the browser treats it as same-origin with your local server. If a reverse proxy on the same machine forwards a public name to the server (nginx → 127.0.0.1:8082 with proxy_set_header Host $host), list that name: A server reached directly on a public IP address is not checked.

Internal networks: Use AUTH_ENFORCE=false if behind a trusted reverse proxy Public exposure: Always set AUTH_ENFORCE=true and use HTTPS Load balancers: Health check path is /health/live (fast, exempt from auth)

Hosting platforms should expose these endpoints: Endpoint Purpose /health/live Fast liveness probe (returns {"status": "ok"}) /health/ready Readiness probe (parallel feature checks) /health Deep health (parallel feature checks; ?deep=false for liveness) /api/protocol Protocol version and capabilities /api/protocol/negotiate Capability negotiation /api/features List of registered features
For a minimal AIUI deployment: Required: OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable Recommended: Persistent volume for AIUI_DATA_DIR Optional: AUTH_ENFORCE=true for multi-tenant environments

pages.d: PraisonAIUI provides multiple health endpoints optimized for different use cases:

s.x: PraisonAIUI provides multiple health endpoints optimized for different use cases: /health/live - Fast liveness check (<500ms) /health/ready - Readiness check with optional deep checks /health - Legacy endpoint (backward compatibility)

Fast endpoint to verify the server is running. Returns immediately with minimal processing. Use for: Load balancer health probes Kubernetes liveness probes High-frequency monitoring Response time: <500ms (typically <100ms) Example: Response:

Verifies the server is ready to handle requests. Performs parallel health checks on all features with timeout protection. The provider check runs concurrently and is bounded by the same 0.5s timeout, so a slow provider cannot hang the response (or a cold /api/health). Use for: Kubernetes readiness probes Pre-deployment validation Detailed diagnostics Query parameters: ?deep=false - Skip feature checks for faster response Response time: With deep checks: <1s (parallel execution) Without deep checks: <200ms Example: Response with deep checks:

Cached version of readiness check for dashboard polling. 30-second TTL to reduce load. Use for: Dashboard health indicators Frequent client polling Status pages Response: Same as /health/ready but cached for 30 seconds

If you're upgrading from a version using only /health: Update monitoring: Change health checks to use /health/live for liveness Update readiness: Use /health/ready?deep=false for readiness probes Update dashboards: Point status indicators to /api/health (cached) Backward compatibility: The /health endpoint remains available but may be slow

Endpoint Cold Start Warm (p50) Warm (p95) Use Case /health/live <100ms <20ms <50ms Liveness probes /health/ready?deep=false <200ms <50ms <100ms Basic readiness /health/ready <1s <500ms <800ms Full diagnostics /api/health (cached) <1s <20ms <50ms Dashboard polling First request only, then cached for 30s

If you're seeing slow responses on the legacy /health endpoint: Switch to /health/live for fast checks Use /health/ready?deep=false if you don't need feature health Enable caching with /api/health for frequent polling
Features that timeout in /health/ready will show: This indicates the feature took longer than 500ms to respond. The server is still operational, but that specific feature may be experiencing issues.
Under high load, use /health/live exclusively for monitoring. It has minimal overhead and won't impact performance.
