pages.d: Every aiui command and option. aiui --help prints the same

s.x: Every aiui command and option. aiui --help prints the same information from the installed version. The wheel also installs the command as praisonaiui. For a short tour of the commands you will use most, see CLI Usage.

Run the server for a Python app (app.py) or a YAML chat agent (chat.yaml). Option Default Description APP_FILE required A Python file that registers callbacks, or a .yaml/.yml chat config --port, -p 8000 Port. If it is taken, the next free port (up to 10 further) is used and printed --host 127.0.0.1 Address to bind to --reload, -r off Restart when files change --style, -s detected app (the React app shell), chat (the classic chat), docs, agents, playground, dashboard or custom --backend, -b standalone standalone, or praisonai to use the PraisonAI WebSocket gateway --datastore, -d sdk Session storage: sdk (shared with PraisonAI Agents), sdk:/path, json, json:/path or memory. Without the flag, a chat YAML's datastore: key is used --config, -c none A docs-site YAML to build before serving (optional) --output, -o aiui Folder the UI files are written to; by default next to APP_FILE Style: for a Python app --style wins, then aiui.set_style(); for a YAML app its style: key wins over --style. Without any of them aiui run detects one: @aiui.profiles plus registered agents gives agents, @aiui.page gives dashboard, anything else app. In app, aiui run opens the chat layout (the chat without a canvas) unless AIUI_LAYOUT, aiui.set_layout() or YAML layout: picks another. See UI Styles and Layouts. A chat YAML's top-level keys: name, instructions, model, welcome, goodbye, starters, profiles, tools, features, datastore, style, theme, branding, dashboard, pages, layout and extensions. layout: takes a layout id (layout: command) or the same block as aiui.yaml (default, available, user_choice, primary, options); extensions: takes enabled: / disabled: lists, as in aiui.yaml. Any other key prints a warning naming it, since it would otherwise be ignored without a word. aiui run loads ~/.praisonai/.env and then ./.env before starting, without overriding variables that are already set.

Write a starter aiui.yaml in the current folder. It refuses to overwrite an existing aiui.yaml or aiui.template.yaml unless --force is given. Option Default Description --template, -t minimal minimal, docs or marketing --force, -f off Overwrite existing files --frontend off Also scaffold a Vite + React + shadcn frontend project The file's first line, # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json, gives autocomplete and hover docs in editors (Editor setup). init writes only the YAML file. Create the folder it points to (for the docs template, ./docs with at least one .md file) before aiui build.

Check a docs-site configuration and its pages. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --strict off Unknown keys, broken links, nav entries without a page and content issues (7xxx) become errors (exit 1) --format text json prints {valid, errors, warnings}, each with code, file, line, message, suggestion Each finding prints as [category] code file:line: message with a fix hint under it: Code Finding 1003 unknown key (ignored); in a $ref file the file is named 1004 key accepted but has no effect; unknown component tag in a page 2101 a nav entry names no docs page 2102 a navigation tab, menu item, anchor or dropdown with no pages, groups or href 5001, 51xx, 5201 theme, layout and search settings that are ignored 6001, 6002 broken link or missing image (aiui docs check-links); OpenAPI spec problems 7000 page front matter is not valid YAML (the page loses its title) 7001 front matter key has the wrong type (keys) 7002 image without alt text (`, with noalt;alt="" marks a decorative image) 7003 two files publish the same page URL (intro.md and 01-intro.md) 7004 two sidebar entries in one folder have the same title 7005 heading skips a level (## then ####) 7006 page has nothing beyond its headings 7007 {{name}} with no value under variables: (variables) 7008 snippet not found, outside the project folder, or including itself (fails aiui build) 7009 icon (front matter, navigation, a component's icon="…") that is not a lucide name, an emoji or an image URL, with the nearest name 7010 a redirect loops, or ends at a docs path with no page (redirects) 7011 a page is published at a redirect's source, so the redirect never runs 7012 front matter openapi: / api: or a navigation METHOD /path entry that names no operation in the loaded specs (OpenAPI) 7013 front matter related names a page that does not exist (related pages) 7014 a site.customCss, site.customJs, site.theme.fonts or site.theme.codeLanguages file that is not in the project folder (fonts and custom files) 7015 site.theme.code names a theme that is not bundled (with the nearest name), or a site.theme.codeLanguages file is not a TextMate grammar (code blocks) 7016 a ::: module block names no module or member, or has an unknown option (fails aiui build; Python API reference) 7017 content.docs.auth is set, and only aiui serve / aiui dev enforce it (aiui build); front matter public / groups without content.docs.auth, or a group no reader is in (docs sign-in) 7018 two navigation.versions with the same name, more than one marked default: true, or a version that lists a page of another version's folder (versions) 7019 raw HTML a page shows differently than written: an that is not a YouTube, Vimeo or Loom video (shown as a link; the host is named), or , , , , , , (removed). Also an aiui build warning (raw HTML) 7020 two navigation.languages with the same code, more than one marked default: true, or a version folder inside a language folder (docs/fr/v1/; languages) 7021 site.components is not a .js / .mjs file in the project folder, or the build finds no component tag in it (your own components) 7022 a class on a component tag or raw HTML that docs pages drop (not a docs utility class; the nearest allowed one is suggested), or a style attribute (always removed). Also an aiui build warning (styling with classes) 7101 site.theme.accent under WCAG AA 3:1 contrast on the light or dark background, with a shade that passes 7102 logo, favicon or site.theme.background image that is not a file in the project folder (branding) Without --config, validate, build and serve read ./aiui.yaml. The old name aiui.template.yaml still works: when it is the only one there it is used, with a one-line hint on stderr to rename it, and the exit code is unchanged. When both files exist, aiui.yaml wins. An explicit --config always wins and prints no hint. See Config file name.

Print the JSON Schema of aiui.yaml, generated from the Config model of the installed version; --output, -o writes it to a file. The schema is also published at https://ui.praison.ai/aiui.schema.json; see Editor setup.

Build a static docs site from the configuration. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --output, -o aiui Output folder --minify off Minify the JSON manifests --strict off Stop with exit code 1 on a broken link (without it, broken links are warnings) The output holds index.html, 404.html, the UI bundle (assets/, aiui-manifest.json), the manifests (ui-config.json, docs-nav.json, route-manifest.json), one HTML file and the Markdown source per page, robots.txt and .nojekyll. sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt are added when the site URL is known (seo.siteUrl, or a CNAME file next to the configuration or in docs/).

Find broken page links, #anchors, images, component hrefs and nav entries before you deploy. Prints file:line: target: reason (did you mean X?) and exits 1 when a link is broken. See Writing docs pages → Check links. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file --external off Also request every http(s) URL (HEAD, then GET; 16 at a time) --timeout 10 Seconds to wait for each external URL --json off Print {"checked", "pages", "broken": [{file, line, target, reason, suggestion}]}

Build (unless --no-build) and serve a docs site. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --output, -o aiui Folder to serve --port, -p 8000 Port (next free port if taken) --host 127.0.0.1 Address to bind to --no-build off Serve the existing output without building --watch, -w off Rebuild when a file in the configuration's folder changes (reload the page yourself; aiui dev reloads it for you) --cors-origins empty Comma-separated allowed origins; empty means same-origin only --ssl-certfile none Certificate file for HTTPS --ssl-keyfile none Private key file for HTTPS --open / --no-open auto Open the site in a browser. Auto opens it only when run from a terminal; never in CI, under a test runner or from a script (when a browser opens) Paths without a file extension fall back to the single-page app. Paths that try to leave the output folder are refused. Every response carries the /* headers of the build's _headers file, which holds the site's Content Security Policy. #### When a browser opens aiui serve, aiui dev and aiui dev --examples open a browser tab only for a person at a terminal. With neither flag, the tab opens when standard output is a terminal and no CI or test runner is detected (CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, BUILDKITE, PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST). --open forces it, --no-open skips it, and AIUI_NO_BROWSER=1 turns it off everywhere, for scripts and coding agents that start these servers.

Preview the docs site while you write it: build, serve, and reload the open browser tab on every save. A failed build is shown in the terminal and over the page while the last good build stays up. Run it in the folder that holds aiui.yaml, or in a folder with only a docs/ folder. See Hot Reload. Option Default Description --config, -c aiui.yaml Configuration file (lookup) --port, -p 8000 Port (next free port if taken) --host 127.0.0.1 Address to bind to --open / --no-open auto Open the preview in a browser; auto as for aiui serve (when a browser opens) --base-path as aiui build URL path to preview the site under --examples, -e none Run the examples dashboard for this folder instead (default port 9000) aiui dev --examples examples is the older dashboard that lists the example projects in a folder and switches between them. In a folder with no configuration and no docs/ but an examples/ folder, plain aiui dev still opens it.

Command Options Description aiui doctor --server, -s (default http://127.0.0.1:8000), --json Structured diagnostics against a running server aiui health-check --server, -s, --detailed, -d Server health; --detailed shows each feature aiui health same Alias of health-check aiui test --server, -s (default http://127.0.0.1:8082) Integration tests against a running server: chat, memory, sessions, endpoints, features, all. See API Testing

--config applies the extensions: policy from that YAML. doctor checks the entry point, the SDK version gate, static_dir and SRI hashes, and (unless --no-builtin) page ids that a built-in page shadows. A plugin's own commands run as aiui ... or aiui plugins ...; AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 turns that lookup off. See UI plugins.
These talk to a running server over HTTP. Every one takes --server, -s URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8000).
Runtime configuration (stored in config.yaml under the data directory).
A2UI surfaces for the agent canvas; see A2UI canvas.
aiui auth create-secret prints a new session secret (offline; see Sessions); aiui auth create-key --name my-app creates an API key on the running server and prints it once.
Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Invalid configuration, failed request or other error 2 File or folder not found, or an unknown --style 3 Build failed 4 No free port near the requested one

Variable Effect AIUI_DATA_DIR Data directory (default ~/.praisonaiui): sessions, runtime config.yaml, plugin state AIUI_SHELL app turns the dashboard style into the React app shell; legacy turns app back into dashboard AIUI_LAYOUT Default app-shell layout id; see Layouts AIUI_TEMPLATES_DIR Serve or build with another frontend bundle folder AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Origins allowed for cross-site requests and WebSockets (comma-separated, or *) AIUI_ALLOWED_HOSTS Extra host names a loopback or private-address server answers AIUI_REQUIRE_TOKEN Require the URL token on every request AUTH_ENFORCE true gates every route and WebSocket behind auth AIUI_AUTH_SECRET Session signing secret (comma-separated to rotate: first signs, all verify); default a generated /auth_secret AIUI_SESSION_LIFETIME How long a sign-in lasts while unused (14d default, 12h, 3600); overrides YAML auth.sessionLifetime AIUI_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD 1 stops loading plugin CLI commands PRAISONAI_MODEL Default model for built-in agent features (default gpt-4o-mini) OPENAI_API_KEY Used by agent features and examples that call OpenAI The security variables are described in Deployment.

pages.d: Reference for import praisonaiui as aiui.

s.x: Reference for import praisonaiui as aiui.
These functions configure the server. Call them at module level in your app.py, before the server starts.

Set the UI style. Parameter Type Values style str "app" (the React app shell), "chat" (the classic chat), "dashboard", "agents", "playground", "docs", "custom" Priority under aiui run: CLI --style, then set_style(), then auto-detection (a plain chat app gets app). See UI Styles.
Whitelist which built-in sidebar pages to show (dashboard mode). Custom pages registered via @aiui.page() always appear. Use aiui pages ids to see all available page IDs.

Configure the sidebar branding (title text and logo). Parameter Type Default title str "PraisonAI" logo str "" (no logo: the PraisonAI brand glyph) logo is an image URL or path (/static/logo.svg, https://…, data:image/…) or a short text mark. Left empty, every UI draws the PraisonAI glyph on the accent tile. Also configurable via config.yaml:

Set the persistence backend for sessions and messages. Without a call, the server uses the SDK store shared with PraisonAI Agents (SDKFileDataStore, from praisonaiui.datastore_sdk), falling back to JSONFileDataStore. aiui run --datastore sets the same thing from the command line.
Set the AI provider for chat completions.

Register an agent object (for example a PraisonAI Agents Agent) under a name. Together with an @aiui.profiles callback, registered agents make aiui run pick the agents style. Agents created in the dashboard's Agents page are a separate store (/api/agents/definitions).

Handle incoming chat messages. This is the core callback. Annotate the parameter as str (async def on_reply(message: str)) to get the text only. Otherwise the callback gets a MessageContext with: message.text (alias message.content): the user's text message.session_id: the session id message.agent_name: the selected agent, if any message.attachments: the files sent with the message, [{id, name, content_type, path}] (see Attachments) How a reply ends: If the callback raises, the run ends with one run_error frame carrying the exception text. The chat shows the error under whatever was streamed, the reply is saved with status: "error" (so it is still there after a reload), the run ledger counts it as failed, and the traceback is logged. Stop (chat_abort, POST /api/chat/abort, POST /cancel) cancels the callback task: the callback gets asyncio.CancelledError at its next await, so an LLM call or tool it is waiting on stops too. A callback that sends nothing (no token, message, step or tool event) for AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT seconds (default 600) is cancelled and the run fails with a timeout. Set AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0 for no limit.

The greeting on a new, empty chat. The chat runs it through POST /welcome once per page load and shows what it says (aiui.say, or streamed tokens) as plain text on the empty thread: in the app shell's chat and every layout, the chat style and the dashboard's chat. In a layout's new-chat hero (the site's mark and name) the greeting takes the place of the generic "Ask anything…" line, with the starters below it. It is not saved to the conversation. A chat YAML's welcome: key registers one for you.

Runs when a chat's last browser connection closes, after any reply still running there finishes, as that chat (aiui.user_session is readable): use it for clean-up. Nobody is listening any more, so what it sends is dropped.

Each moment of a chat has a handler. The names are aliases: @aiui.on_message and @aiui.reply register the same handler (the last one registered wins). Decorator Runs Same as @aiui.on_message For each message the user sends; gets the MessageContext (message.content). @aiui.reply @aiui.on_chat_start Once per chat, right before its first reply (again after on_chat_end ran for it). @aiui.on_stop When the user presses Stop, as the stopped chat. @aiui.cancel @aiui.on_chat_end When the chat ends (above). @aiui.goodbye @aiui.author_rename Maps an author (agent) name to the name the chat shows. @aiui.welcome The greeting on an empty chat, once per page load (no chat yet). Every handler may be async def or a plain def. on_chat_start runs in the reply's task (so aiui.say and aiui.Message work) and needs a reply handler; if it raises, that turn fails with the error and the next turn runs it again. author_rename is called once per name per reply (a failing handler keeps the name); the display name goes on every frame of the reply (agent_name) and the saved reply, never on the agent the user picked. @aiui.resume is not called yet (below).

pages.d: The aiui.yaml schema: what aiui validate checks and aiui build

s.x: The aiui.yaml schema: what aiui validate checks and aiui build compiles. The source of truth is schema/models.py (Config). The runtime state file of a running server is a different file; see Runtime Persistence below.

aiui validate, aiui build and aiui serve find the file in this order: --config, when given. It always wins and prints nothing extra. ./aiui.yaml. ./aiui.template.yaml, the old name. It still works; the command prints one dim line on stderr and its exit code does not change: Using aiui.template.yaml; rename it to aiui.yaml (the old name keeps working). When both files exist, aiui.yaml is used and the command says so in one line (Using aiui.yaml; aiui.template.yaml is also here and is ignored.). With neither, the command stops with Configuration file not found: aiui.yaml. aiui init writes aiui.yaml and refuses to overwrite either name without --force. aiui dev reads either name, and aiui dev --examples accepts either name in each example folder. aiui.yml is not looked up; pass it with --config.

Any mapping can live in its own file. $ref names a YAML (or JSON) file, relative to the file that holds the $ref: Included files can include others; keys written next to $ref override the included ones. Paths stay inside the folder of aiui.yaml; a file that includes itself, directly or through others, is an error ($ref cycle: aiui.yaml -> config/nav.yaml -> aiui.yaml). Errors name the file and line of the $ref (aiui.yaml:6: $ref './config/nav.yaml' not found); a YAML error or an unknown key inside an included file names that file. validate, build, serve, docs check-links and the server all read includes.

aiui init starts aiui.yaml with this line: Editors that run the YAML language server (VS Code with the Red Hat YAML extension, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, Zed) then complete keys, show each key's description on hover and underline wrong values as you type; add the line to an existing aiui.yaml for the same. The schema is generated from the Config model, so it never drifts from aiui validate. For the exact installed version (offline, or pinned), run aiui schema -o aiui.schema.json and use $schema=./aiui.schema.json.

Note: The ui field is a theming hint. Components are UI-agnostic and use CSS classes you can style with any framework.

Auto-install shadcn components at build time: When you run aiui build, missing components are installed with npx shadcn@latest add into the frontend source (src/frontend in a repository checkout). This only matters when you build the frontend yourself; the bundled React app does not change.

editLink, lastUpdated and feedback draw the page footer; see Writing docs pages → Page footer. related is the related pages list. mcp is the docs MCP server and assistant is Ask AI. indexFiles and nav (mode, sort, collapsible, maxDepth) are accepted but not read by the build yet; see Navigation.
Define reusable components:
Type Description Header Site header with logo, nav, CTA Footer Site footer DocsSidebar Documentation sidebar navigation Toc Table of contents DocContent Rendered markdown content
Templates combine a layout with slot assignments:

Layout Description ThreeColumnLayout Sidebar + Content + TOC TwoColumnLayout Sidebar + Content CenteredLayout Centered content, no sidebar FullWidthLayout Full width content FlexibleLayout WordPress-style widget zones
Place widgets in layout zones without modifying markdown: Zones, the widgets and which layouts render them: Widget Zones.

Map URL patterns to templates: Route matching uses glob patterns: * - one path segment ** - any number of segments The first matching route wins, so list specific routes before broad ones. A route's slots can override only the right slot in the docs site (right: null hides the table of contents); header and footer are read from the template, so per-route overrides of them have no effect.

Single source of truth for all runtime feature state. In addition to aiui.yaml (which drives static site generation), PraisonAIUI uses a unified runtime config file, config.yaml in the data directory (AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui/). This file stores all feature state — agents, channels, guardrails, schedules, and runtime settings — in a single YAML file that persists across server restarts. This is compatible with the gateway.yaml schema used by praisonai gateway start --config.

All CRUD operations (dashboard, REST API, CLI) automatically write back to this file: Feature Section Written On Config Runtime runtime_config PATCH, PUT, DELETE, apply Guardrails guardrails Register Channels channels Add, update, delete Schedules schedules Add, remove, update Agents agents Create, update, delete Atomic writes: a temp file and os.replace() prevent corruption. Hot reload: the Config Hot-Reload watcher, once started, reloads this file after external edits. Secrets: channel secrets are written as env:VAR_NAME references (a _ref key works too); the server refuses an inline token that looks like a secret and redacts secrets in API responses. Rule of thumb: secrets (API keys, tokens) go in environment variables; preferences (model, theme, branding) in the config file.

File Purpose Used By aiui.yaml Static site layout, components, routes aiui build, aiui serve, aiui validate $AIUI_DATA_DIR/config.yaml Runtime feature state (agents, channels, config) aiui run, dashboard API gateway.yaml Subset of config.yaml (legacy compatibility) praisonai gateway start

pages.t: API Reference page and OpenAPI document
pages.d: The running server describes its own HTTP API at /api/openapi.json and lets you try every route from the app.

s.x: Every aiui server publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document of its own HTTP API, and the app shell has a page to read it and send requests. Nothing to configure: both are on by default. GET /api/openapi.json is built from the route table the server is running, when it is asked. It lists every API route it answers (/api/*, /v1/* and the unprefixed data routes such as /sessions and /run): the core, each enabled built-in, and the routes of your plugins and register_feature() features. It cannot go stale, and a built-in you switch off (extensions: {disabled: [builtin.training]}) leaves it. Field Comes from tags The built-in that owns the route (sessions, api, config…), a plugin's or feature's name, else core summary, description The handler's docstring: first line, then the rest (plain text; a leading POST /path — is dropped) parameters Path parameters and their types ({id:int} is an integer) security Bearer token; [] on the public routes (/api/health, sign-in) servers /: the server that served the document x-websockets The WebSocket routes (/api/chat/ws, /api/logs/stream) The route needs the same credentials as every other /api route in each auth mode. A plugin the caller may not use (an entry-point plugin that is off by default on a remote or sign-in server) is left out. Switch the document and the page off with extensions: {disabled: [builtin.api-reference]}. Use it anywhere an OpenAPI file goes: client generators, API tools, or the API reference of an aiui docs site (api: {openapi: http://localhost:8000/api/openapi.json}, see OpenAPI).

A feature adds request bodies, responses or anything else to its operations with an optional openapi() method, keyed by "METHOD /path": The OpenAI-compatible routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings…) carry their request bodies this way.

In the app shell (style: app), API Reference in the Control group (/api-reference) shows the routes by feature with a search box (method, path or text). Pick a route to read it and try it against this same server: fill in the path parameters, a query string and a JSON body (prefilled from the document's example); Send request shows the status, time and the response, pretty-printed; Copy cURL gives the same request for a terminal, with $AIUI_TOKEN in place of a token; OpenAPI JSON downloads the document; ?op= opens one route (/api-reference?op=get_api_sessions). Requests go to the same origin with your session, so no proxy, CORS setup or pasted key is needed. The default dashboard style is unchanged; its Inspector and API pages stay.

s.x: The AIUI health API provides endpoints to monitor server and provider health status.

The following status values are used throughout the health API: Status Meaning Color Code "ok" Service is functioning normally Green "healthy" Service is functioning normally (legacy) Green "degraded" Service is partially functional Yellow "error" Service has errors Red "unknown" Status cannot be determined Yellow Note: Both "ok" and "healthy" indicate successful operation. The system accepts either value for backward compatibility.
Returns the overall server health status. Response:
Returns information about the active AI provider. Response:

Returns detailed JSON health information from the provider gateway. Always responds with Content-Type: application/json. The base fields from the provider's health() payload are merged with the normalised fields below. Response: Field Type Description status string One of the health status values above. type string Provider type (from provider field, falls back to class name). agents integer Count of agents reported by the provider. detail string Human-readable detail; "ok" for healthy providers. api_key string Built-in PraisonAIProvider only: "set" when a model key is in the environment (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, …), a local base URL is set (OLLAMA_HOST, OPENAI_BASE_URL, …) or a key is saved in Settings; "missing" otherwise. Absent for other providers (unknown). The app shell shows "Add an API key to start" above the composer when it is "missing". pages.d: src/praisonaiui-ts is a small TypeScript package, named praisonaiui, for

s.x: src/praisonaiui-ts is a small TypeScript package, named praisonaiui, for rendering an aiui build site inside your own React or Next.js app. It reads the JSON manifests the build writes and gives you layout and slot components. Status You do not need this package to use PraisonAIUI. aiui run and aiui build ship their own UI inside the Python wheel, and nothing in the current UI is published to npm. The praisonaiui package on npm is version 0.1.0 (January 2026); the source in the repository is 0.2.0 and is not published. The package is not built or tested in CI. To extend the UI that aiui run serves, write a plugin against @aiui/sdk instead; see UI plugins.
Without next installed, npm run build writes the JavaScript but fails at the type-declaration step. React 18 or later is a peer dependency; Next.js 14 or later is optional at runtime.

pages.d: Manifest loading and template resolution in the praisonaiui TypeScript

s.x: Manifest loading and template resolution in the praisonaiui TypeScript package. Read the overview first: the package is optional and built from src/praisonaiui-ts.
Create an instance that loads the three manifests written by aiui build. load() uses fetch, so configPath is a URL path the browser can reach. It throws if any of the three files fails to load.

Find the template for a path. Routes are tried by priority, highest first (aiui build gives the first route in the YAML the highest). In a pattern * matches one path segment and ** any number. It returns null when no route matches or the route names a template that does not exist.
A static map from a component type to a React component, for your own renderer to look up. Nothing in the package reads the registry on its own; the components in Components do not consult it.

[!IMPORTANT] The React frontend always fetches 3 JSON files before rendering, regardless of style: /ui-config.json — must return {"style": "dashboard"} (or "chat", "agents", etc.) /docs-nav.json — sidebar nav (can be {"items": []} for non-docs modes) /route-manifest.json — URL routing (can be {} for non-docs modes) If any of these 404, the user sees "Failed to load manifests" and the dashboard never renders. In server.py, create_app() provides dynamic fallback handlers for these. If you are running via AIUIGateway, these handlers are included automatically. If writing a custom server, ensure these routes exist.

The style field in /ui-config.json controls which React component renders: Style Component Use Case "docs" Three-column docs layout Documentation sites "dashboard" Full sidebar + pages Feature management dashboard "chat" Chat-focused interface Chat-only applications "agents" Agent selector + chat Multi-agent interfaces "playground" Split-pane playground Agent experimentation "custom" Flexible layout Custom configurations Set via Python: aiui.set_style("dashboard")

s.h: Feature Protocol — How to Add a New Feature
s.x: Every feature follows the same 4-step pattern: Define the Protocol ABC — abstract methods for the capability Implement SimpleXxxManager — in-memory fallback, zero dependencies Implement SDKXxxManager — wraps praisonaiagents SDK (if available) Provide get_xxx_manager() — factory function, SDK-first with fallback

Sessions: JSON files in ~/.praisonaiui/sessions/{session_id}.json Memory: Auto-stored from chat (every user + assistant message → short type memory via SDK Memory.store_short_term()). Searchable via /api/memory/search. Filterable by session_id via /api/memory/session/{id} Knowledge: Stored via /api/knowledge (text) or /api/knowledge/add-file (file ingest). Searched via /api/knowledge/search. Context auto-injected into chat prompts when relevant entries exist. Uses SDK Knowledge class with RAG pipeline when [knowledge] extras installed Agents: In-memory by default; SimpleAgentRegistry persists to data file if set_data_file() called Schedules: FileScheduleStore from praisonaiagents SDK persists to disk Config: Runtime config via /api/config_runtime, not persisted by default

pages.d: This document uses RFC 2119 keywords: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY.

s.x: Version: v1alpha1 (draft) Status: Draft — not yet normative Date: August 2026 This document uses RFC 2119 keywords: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY.

ADP defines a declarative format for describing application UI design: site metadata, theming, navigation, reusable components, page templates, and URL routing. It does NOT define: Server-side APIs or data models Agent orchestration or workflow graphs Infrastructure or deployment configuration Executable code or templating logic in manifests Implementations MUST treat ADP manifests as data, not code.

Term Definition Manifest A YAML or JSON document conforming to this spec Application The root kind: Application manifest describing a complete UI Component A named, reusable UI block with a type and props Template A layout definition assigning components to slots or zones Slot A named region within a layout (e.g. header, main) Zone An ordered list of widgets in a slot (WordPress-style) Route A URL pattern mapping to a template Catalog Published JSON Schema defining allowed component types Compiler Tool that validates and emits runtime JSON manifests Renderer Runtime that consumes compiled manifests and renders UI
Every ADP manifest MUST include:

schemaVersion — integer bumped on breaking envelope changes apiVersion — string group/version (e.g. adp.io/v1alpha1, adp.io/v1) metadata.version — application SemVer (independent of protocol version) Breaking changes MUST increment apiVersion (e.g. v1alpha1 → v1) Deprecated fields MUST include deprecated: true and SHOULD include x-sunset date

Manifests MAY be authored as YAML (.application.yaml) or JSON (.application.json). Semantics MUST be identical. Runtimes MUST NOT consume YAML directly; compilers MUST normalise to JSON before validation.

An Application spec MUST contain at minimum: Field Required Description site.title YES Application display name templates YES At least one template routes YES At least one route All other fields are OPTIONAL.
Theme MAY use preset shorthand or reference a DTCG token file:

ADP separates top tab bar from sidebar source: navigation.tabs — top-level tab bar with grouped pages content.docs.nav.mode: auto — sidebar generated from filesystem scan content.docs.nav.mode: manual — sidebar driven by navigation.tabs groups Renderers MUST honour content.docs.nav.mode when building sidebar (R29)
Rules: Component IDs MUST be unique within the manifest type MUST match an entry in the published component catalog props MUST validate against the catalog JSON Schema for that type

Rules: layout MUST be a known layout type in the catalog Each slot value MUST be { ref: id }, { type: ComponentType }, or null Zones MUST use zone names valid for FlexibleLayout A template MUST declare either slots or zones, not both (R13)

Rules: Routes MUST be ordered most-specific-first match MUST be a glob pattern template MUST reference a key in spec.templates Renderers MUST resolve routes at runtime using compiled route-manifest.json

Implementations MUST publish a component-catalog.schema.json (meta-schema) and a catalog instance such as catalogs/default.catalog.json: Custom component types MUST be registered via plugin schema layers. Unknown types MUST cause validation failure in strict mode.

A conforming compiler MUST: Parse YAML or JSON manifest Normalise to JSON Validate against application.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) Validate cross-reference rules (see validation-rules.md) Validate component props against catalog schema Emit runtime manifests: ui-config.json — site, components, templates, theme, navigation route-manifest.json — ordered routes with template refs docs-nav.json — filesystem-derived navigation (if mode auto)

Manifests MAY include external files using Backstage-style placeholders: Rules: Paths MUST be relative to the containing manifest Path traversal (../../) MUST be rejected Supported placeholders: $yaml:, $json:, $text:
Vendor extensions MUST use the x-adp- prefix: Implementations MUST preserve unknown x-adp-* fields. Non-prefixed unknown fields MUST be rejected in strict mode.

An implementation is ADP-conformant if and only if it: Accepts manifests with apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 and kind: Application Validates all MUST-level requirements in this spec and validation-rules.md Rejects manifests with unknown fields in strict mode Emits runtime JSON manifests from valid Application specs Resolves routes to templates at render time
Research report Implementation status PraisonAIUI mapping JSON Schema: application JSON Schema: component catalog JSON Schema: theme Examples

pages.d: Cross-reference validation rules for Application Design Protocol manifests. These constraints cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone and MUST be enforced by c

s.x: Cross-reference validation rules for Application Design Protocol manifests. These constraints cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone and MUST be enforced by conforming compilers. Rules use RFC 2119 keywords: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY. Inspired by AWP validation rules R1–R32 pattern.

Rule Level Description R1 MUST schemaVersion MUST equal 1 for apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 R2 MUST kind MUST be Application for root manifests R3 MUST metadata.name MUST be unique within a deployment scope R4 MUST NOT Unknown top-level fields outside x-adp-* namespace in strict mode

Rule Level Description R5 MUST Every spec.components entry MUST have a unique ID R6 MUST Every component type MUST exist in the published component catalog R7 MUST Component props MUST validate against catalog JSON Schema for that type R8 MUST NOT A component ID be referenced by ref: unless it exists in spec.components R9 SHOULD Unused components (defined but never referenced) SHOULD emit a warning

Rule Level Description R10 MUST Every spec.templates entry MUST declare a valid layout from the catalog R11 MUST Slot names in templates.*.slots MUST be valid for the declared layout R12 MUST Zone names in templates.*.zones MUST be valid for FlexibleLayout R13 MUST Each template MUST declare either slots or zones, not both R14 MUST Inline slot { type: X } types MUST exist in the component catalog R15 MUST Slot { ref: id } MUST resolve to a component in spec.components

Rule Level Description R16 MUST Every route template MUST reference a key in spec.templates R17 MUST Routes MUST be ordered most-specific-first (longer/more precise patterns before wildcards) R18 MUST Route slot overrides MUST use valid slot names for the target template's layout R19 SHOULD At least one route SHOULD match the site root or docs base path

Rule Level Description R20 MUST If content.docs.dir is declared, the directory MUST exist at compile time R21 MUST If content.docs.nav.mode is manual, navigation.tabs MUST be non-empty R22 SHOULD If content.docs.nav.mode is auto, a content source MUST be declared Navigation model: navigation.tabs — top tab bar content.docs.nav.mode — sidebar source: auto (filesystem scan) or manual (use navigation.tabs groups)

Rule Level Description R23 MUST NOT $yaml:, $json:, or $text: paths traverse outside the project root R24 MUST Included files MUST parse as valid YAML/JSON/text respectively R25 MUST NOT Circular file includes (A includes B includes A)

Rule Level Description R26 MUST If theme.tokens is declared, the referenced file MUST exist and validate against DTCG 2025.10 R27 MUST NOT Both theme.preset and theme.tokens be declared simultaneously

pages.d: There is no single existing standard for designing full application UI from a declarative text file. Instead, the problem is addressed in fragments:

s.x: Version: 1.0 (draft) Date: August 2026 Scope: UI, layout, navigation, theming — declarative application design from text manifests Status: Research and recommendation; not yet a published standard

There is no single existing standard for designing full application UI from a declarative text file. Instead, the problem is addressed in fragments: Docs-site generators (commercial docs platforms, PraisonAIUI, Hugo) declare navigation and layout in config files. Form libraries (JSON Forms, RJSF) declare layout trees from JSON Schema. Agent UI protocols (A2UI, AG-UI) declare streaming component surfaces for LLM-generated UI. Catalog standards (OpenUI, Backstage) declare component metadata without runtime layout. Design token standards (DTCG 2025.10) declare theming without structure. Recommendation: Define an Application Design Protocol (ADP) that synthesises proven patterns from 45 surveyed standards into a UI-only manifest format. PraisonAIUI already implements approximately 60% of this model. ADP formalises, extends, and publishes what exists today.
A protocol that lets a developer (or LLM) describe an application's visual design — pages, navigation, components, themes, routes — in one or more text files, without writing application code.

Need Who solves it Gap Docs site from config Commercial docs platforms, PraisonAIUI, Docusaurus No shared spec; some use JSON, others YAML or JS Component catalog OpenUI, A2UI No layout or routing Layout trees JSON Forms uiSchema Forms only, not app shells Theming DTCG, Material 3 Tokens only, no pages Agent-generated UI A2UI Runtime streaming, not human-authored static sites Software metadata Backstage Catalog entities, not UI composition

Human-readable — editable without IDE plugins LLM-safe — structural schema rejects unknown fields Portable — same manifest renders on any ADP-compliant runtime Validatable — fail fast at build time, not in the browser Extensible — plugins add catalog entries, not inline code Accessible — ARIA hints required in component catalog

s.x: Mechanism Standards How it works ADP Envelope document K8s, Backstage, OAM, AWP apiVersion + kind + metadata + spec Adopt Component registry + ref PraisonAIUI, OpenUI Named map; templates use ref: Adopt Layout + slots PraisonAIUI, JSON Forms Layout type + named regions Adopt (unified) Route → template PraisonAIUI, Flutter URL glob → template Adopt Navigation tree Docusaurus, Storybook Hierarchical groups → pages Adopt Design token file DTCG, Material 3 Token JSON with aliases Adopt Catalog allowlist A2UI, OpenUI Closed component vocabulary Adopt Schema + uiSchema split JSON Forms, RJSF Data vs presentation Partial Streaming surfaces A2UI, AG-UI Incremental JSON updates Future Layered spec AWP, Helm Separate files merged at compile Adopt File includes Backstage, OpenAPI $yaml: / $ref external files Adopt Structural pruning K8s CRD Reject unknown fields Adopt Validation rules R1–Rn AWP Cross-ref beyond JSON Schema Adopt JS executable config Docusaurus, Gatsby Code config Reject Visual canvas Figma, Webflow Proprietary designer Reject Code-only UI Compose, SwiftUI No wire format Out of scope

Dimension PraisonAIUI A2UI Backstage Authoring format YAML JSON (stream) YAML Envelope schemaVersion only Message version apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec Navigation navigation.tabs[] + filesystem N/A N/A (metadata catalog) Components components{id: type, props} Catalog + adjacency list Entity kinds Layout templates{layout, slots, zones} Surfaces N/A Routes routes{match, template} N/A N/A Schema published Pydantic only JSON Schema catalog JSON Schema per kind Runtime React SPA Any renderer Catalog API Primary use Docs sites Agent-generated UI Software inventory Synthesis: ADP combines PraisonAIUI's composition model, the published $schema of commercial docs platforms, A2UI's catalog allowlist, and Backstage's envelope and file includes.
YAML is the best authoring format for application design manifests.

Commercial docs platforms — the closest docs-site analogues — use JSON config with a published $schema URL for IDE autocomplete. This works well for flat-to-moderately-nested config but becomes verbose for deep layout trees. A2UI uses JSON as both authoring and wire format because LLMs emit structured JSON reliably and ambiguity is unacceptable at runtime. Docusaurus and Gatsby use JavaScript/TypeScript config for programmatic power — but this sacrifices portability and LLM generation safety.

Format Strengths Weaknesses for ADP YAML Comments; readable nesting; LLM-friendly; PraisonAIUI continuity Ambiguous typing; merge key footguns; no native DRY JSON Unambiguous; $schema IDE support; proven by commercial docs platforms No comments; verbose for layout trees TOML Clear flat tables (Hugo) Poor for nested templates/zones CUE / Jsonnet / Pkl Typed composition without templating Learning curve; not LLM-default HCL Modules, expressions Ecosystem-bound; overkill for UI-only JS/TS Full programmatic power Not portable; not LLM-safe

Primary authoring: YAML — best for nested templates / zones trees Alternate authoring: JSON — for teams preferring $schema editor tooling Never at runtime: YAML — always compile to JSON before serve Composition: $yaml: file includes (Backstage), not Helm Go templates Power users: Optional CUE/Jsonnet compiles to YAML before validation Verdict: YAML remains the recommended default, but ADP MUST accept JSON as an equivalent authoring format with identical semantics.

Declarative, not executable — manifests describe intent; runtimes render; no inline code or templating logic in core spec. Schema-first — JSON Schema 2020-12 is canonical; YAML is authoring convenience. Structural strictness — unknown fields rejected in strict mode (K8s CRD pattern). Catalog allowlist — component type must exist in published catalog (A2UI pattern). Envelope consistency — every document uses apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec. Separation of concerns — theme, navigation, components, templates, routes are distinct spec sections. Compile, don't interpret — YAML → validated JSON manifest → static assets at build time. Accessibility by default — catalog entries include ARIA role hints (WAI-ARIA pattern). Versioned protocol — schemaVersion integer + apiVersion string; breaking changes bump version. Extension namespace — x-adp-* prefix reserved; plugins register catalog layers. File composition — $yaml: includes for modular configs (Backstage pattern). Route-driven rendering — URL resolution selects template; no hardcoded layout in renderer.

PraisonAIUI today ADP equivalent schemaVersion: 1 schemaVersion + apiVersion components + ref: spec.components + slot refs templates.layout + slots spec.templates routes spec.routes site.theme spec.theme Compiler → JSON manifests ADP compile pipeline Pydantic validation JSON Schema + cross-ref rules

Gap ADP fix No published JSON Schema Publish application.schema.json navigation.tabs compiled but not rendered Mandate runtime consumption in spec route-manifest.json not used for routing Mandate route-driven template resolution Dual slots + zones models Unified: zones = ordered slot arrays Closed hardcoded component types Published component-catalog.schema.json No envelope (kind, metadata) Add Backstage-style envelope

Existing aiui.yaml (and aiui.template.yaml) files remain valid. Migration steps: Add apiVersion: adp.io/v1alpha1 and kind: Application (optional during transition). Wrap top-level keys under spec: (compiler accepts both shapes during v1alpha1). Rename site fields unchanged; map navigation, templates, routes as-is. Publish catalog; register custom component types via plugin schema layers. See adp/aiui-mapping.md for field-by-field mapping.

Should ADP standardise layout type names (ThreeColumnLayout) or allow runtime-defined layouts? Should navigation support both filesystem-auto and manual tabs in one spec, or require a mode switch? Should agent-driven surfaces (A2UI) be a separate kind: Surface or embedded in Application? Should theme reference DTCG token files directly or use simplified preset shorthand?

pages.d: PraisonAIUI is a Python package (PyPI aiui, import praisonaiui) with a

s.x: PraisonAIUI is a Python package (PyPI aiui, import praisonaiui) with a Starlette + Uvicorn server and two frontends: Part What it is CLI (aiui) aiui run app.py starts the server; aiui build compiles a YAML docs site into static JSON manifests Server (server.py, features/) HTTP routes, the chat WebSocket, and one feature module per domain (sessions, agents, theme, attachments, ...) Providers @aiui.reply callbacks or the PraisonAI provider turn a message into RunEvents (see Providers) dashboard style The default of create_app() and of apps with @aiui.page: a vanilla-JS dashboard (templates/frontend/plugins/) React bundle The app shell (style: app, what aiui run opens for a chat app; see React app shell) and the chat, agents, playground and docs styles Plugins First-party pages and features are catalog records; third-party packages use the praisonaiui.plugins entry point (see Plugins) The data flow of a docs site is YAML config → Pydantic models → compiler → JSON manifests → React. The layer map, the numbered rules and the review checklist are in ARCHITECTURE.md.
With the praisonai backend, PraisonAIUI has two complementary integration layers. They solve different problems and run side-by-side.

AG-UI sits alongside MCP and A2A in the agentic protocol stack: Protocol Purpose MCP Gives agents tools A2A Agent-to-agent communication AG-UI Agent-to-user-interface (streaming) Gateway Infrastructure management (channels, nodes, instances)

AG-UI is an open, event-based protocol by CopilotKit that standardizes how agent backends stream events to frontends. PraisonAI implements it at praisonaiagents/ui/agui/. What it does: Streams ~16 standard event types (text deltas, tool calls, state sync, generative UI) over SSE. Who uses it: LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, AWS Strands, Mastra, Pydantic AI, LlamaIndex, AG2, and PraisonAI. #### Usage Frontend compatibility: CopilotKit, or any AG-UI-compatible client.

The gateway integration connects PraisonAIUI's dashboard features to the live WebSocketGateway backend for infrastructure management. What it does: CRUD for channels, nodes, instances; live bot status; heartbeat monitoring. #### How It Works #### Key Files File Purpose features/_gateway_ref.py Thread-safe singleton holding reference to the live gateway features/channels.py Channel CRUD + live status enrichment from gateway features/nodes.py Node CRUD + gateway health enrichment integration.py Calls set_gateway() on start, clears on stop config_store.py Unified ~/.praisonaiui/config.yaml — single source of truth for all feature state #### API Endpoints Endpoint Methods Description /api/channels GET, POST List/create channels /api/channels/{id} GET, PUT, DELETE Channel CRUD /api/channels/{id}/toggle POST Enable/disable /api/channels/{id}/status GET Live running status /api/channels/{id}/restart POST Restart a channel bot /api/channels/{id}/test POST Test connectivity of a channel bot /api/channels/platforms GET Supported platforms /api/nodes GET, POST List/register nodes /api/nodes/{id} GET, PUT, DELETE Node CRUD /api/nodes/{id}/status GET Node status + gateway enrichment /api/nodes/{id}/agents GET, PUT Agent bindings /api/instances GET Connected instances /api/instances/heartbeat POST Presence heartbeat

AIUIGateway.start() in integration.py mounts the gateway and dashboard REST API on one server. Chat uses the built-in WebSocket/SSE RunEvent protocol; AG-UI is mounted separately via AguiFeature when enabled:

AG-UI (/agui) Gateway (/api/*) Layer Conversation Operations Transport SSE (server-sent events) REST + WebSocket Purpose Stream agent responses to users Manage channels, nodes, instances Frontend CopilotKit / AG-UI clients PraisonAIUI React dashboard Protocol Open standard (~16 event types) Internal REST API

s.x: aiui run app.py is the one entry point for an app. It imports app.py (under the module name user_app, so an if __name__ == "__main__": block does not run), reads what the module registered, and starts its own server on --host and --port.
Run: aiui run app.py (opens the app shell, the aiui run default; use aiui run app.py --style chat for the classic chat UI)

Run: aiui run app.py (an @aiui.page callback selects the dashboard style; see UI Styles). A module that builds its own app with create_app() and starts Uvicorn under if __name__ == "__main__": is not special-cased: aiui run ignores that app and serves its own. Run such a file with python app.py instead.

Run: aiui run app.py. An async main() together with an import of AIUIGateway from praisonaiui.integration switches to the praisonai backend. When the module defines main(), the CLI sets the PORT and HOST environment variables from --port/--host (unless they are already set) and calls your main(), so main() must read them to honour the CLI options, as above. Without a main(), the CLI builds its own AIUIGateway on --host/--port and registers the module's agent (or each item of agents). The backend needs the praisonai package (pip install "aiui[praisonai]").

app.py contains Backend Style async main() and from praisonaiui.integration import AIUIGateway praisonai as below anything else standalone detected from the callbacks Detection runs whenever --backend is standalone, which is also the default, so passing --backend standalone does not turn it off. The style rules are in UI Styles.
--reload restarts the server when a file in the folder of app.py changes.

s.x: How the PraisonAIUI test suites are laid out and how to run them. To test a running server from the outside, see API Testing.

CI runs ruff check src/praisonaiui, then pytest tests/unit tests/integration -v --no-cov --timeout=120. Tests marked live call a real LLM provider and skip unless PRAISONAI_LIVE_TESTS=1; tests/integration/conftest.py clears provider API keys for the others. The Python suites that need Node 22.15+, src/frontend/node_modules or Chromium run in e2e shard 1 with RUN_BROWSER_TESTS=1 and --fail-on-skip, which fails the run if any test skips (see tests/README.md). Folder What is in it tests/unit/ Isolated tests: schema, compiler, docs scanner, serve, server and app-shell manifest, plugins, CLI, each feature. They use tmp_path and Starlette's TestClient, and start no server tests/unit/fixtures/ Golden files, such as the default dashboard HTML and the built-in page snapshot tests/integration/ End-to-end tests: the validate → build → serve pipeline through Typer's CliRunner, endpoints, agentic round trips, attachments. Some need praisonaiagents or an API key and skip without them tests/ (top level) Feature-level tests for each domain API The suites grow with every change, so count them instead of trusting a number written here:
From src/frontend (Node version in .nvmrc):

Playwright suites in src/frontend/e2e/ start real servers (with a scripted provider instead of a model) and drive Chromium against the default dashboard, the app shell, the chat style, the docs site and the layouts. They serve dist/, so build first: The projects, servers and baselines are described in src/frontend/e2e/README.md.

PraisonAIUI includes built-in integration tests via aiui test. These run against a live server and verify chat, memory, sessions, and API endpoint health.

Command What it tests aiui test endpoints That the feature endpoints answer: health, features, sessions, chat, provider, channels, agents, config, skills, memory, schedules, approvals, auth, knowledge, guardrails, i18n, telemetry, security, logs, usage and more aiui test features Create, read, update and delete for guardrails, knowledge, memory, workflows, channels and eval aiui test chat Sends messages, checks the reply lands in the session history and that two sessions stay separate aiui test memory Stores a fact in one session and recalls it in another (recall is skipped, not failed, when the fact is stored but the model does not use it) aiui test sessions The session is persisted in the server's datastore (GET /sessions/{id}, any backend or AIUI_DATA_DIR) aiui test all All of the above in sequence The only option is --server / -s (default http://127.0.0.1:8082). chat and memory need an app that replies with a model. Each suite prints one line per check and a summary box, for example 34 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped for endpoints; optional checks such as GET /api/provider/agents are skipped when the provider does not offer them.
